19	// Variant identifies which VS Code distribution a Provider instance targets.
20	// The Copilot chat storage layout is identical between VS Code and VS Code
21	// Insiders — only the application identity differs — so a single provider
22	// implementation serves both when instantiated with the right variant.
23	type Variant struct {
24		ID          string // provider ID used for registration and in generated session data
25		AppName     string // user-facing application label (e.g. "VS Code Insiders")
26		DataDirName string // application data directory name under the OS config root (e.g. "Code - Insiders")
27		Command     string // CLI launcher expected on PATH (e.g. "code-insiders")

35			DataDirName: "Code",
36			Command:     "code",

66	type Provider struct {

69		// findWorkspaceForReconstruction is the workspace lookup used by the resume
70		// flow. Held as an instance field (not a package var) so each variant

75	// NewProvider creates a Copilot IDE provider for the given VS Code variant.
76	func NewProvider(variant Variant) *Provider {
77		p := &Provider{variant: variant}
78		p.findWorkspaceForReconstruction = func(projectPath string) (*WorkspaceMatch, error) {
79			return p.findWorkspaceForProject(projectPath, false)
80		}
81		return p
82	}

84	// Name returns the human-readable name of this provider
85	func (p *Provider) Name() string {
86		return p.variant.AppName + " Copilot IDE"

89	// Check verifies the variant's workspace storage exists and returns info
90	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
91		slog.Debug("Check: Checking Copilot installation", "app", p.variant.AppName)
92	
93		// Check for workspace storage directory
94		storagePath := p.workspaceStoragePath()
95		if storagePath == "" {

184	// GetAgentChatSessions retrieves all chat sessions for the given project path
185	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
186		slog.Debug("GetAgentChatSessions", "projectPath", projectPath, "debugRaw", debugRaw)
187	
188		// Find workspace for project
189		workspace, err := p.FindWorkspaceForProject(projectPath)
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to find workspace: %w", err)
192		}
193	
194		// Load all session files
195		sessionFiles, err := LoadAllSessionFiles(workspace.Dir)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load session files: %w", err)
198		}
199	
200		var sessions []spi.AgentChatSession
201		processedCount := 0
202		totalCount := len(sessionFiles)
203	
204		for _, sessionFile := range sessionFiles {
205			composer, err := LoadSessionFile(sessionFile)
206			if err != nil {
207				slog.Warn("Failed to load session", "file", sessionFile, "error", err)
208				continue
209			}
210	
211			// Load state file (optional)
212			state, err := LoadStateFile(workspace.Dir, composer.SessionID)
213			if err != nil {
214				slog.Warn("Failed to load state file", "sessionId", composer.SessionID, "error", err)
215			}
216	
217			// Check if session has content (either chat messages or editing operations)
218			hasConversations := len(composer.Requests) > 0
219			hasEditingOperations := hasEditingActivity(state)
220	
221			if !hasConversations && !hasEditingOperations {
222				slog.Debug("Skipping empty session (no chat or editing activity)", "sessionId", composer.SessionID)
223				continue
224			}
225	
226			// Convert to AgentChatSession
227			session := p.ConvertToSessionData(*composer, projectPath, state)
228			sessions = append(sessions, session)
229	
230			// Write debug files if requested
231			if debugRaw {
232				if err := WriteDebugFiles(composer, composer.SessionID); err != nil {
233					slog.Warn("Failed to write debug files", "sessionId", composer.SessionID, "error", err)
234				}
235			}
236	
237			// Report progress
238			processedCount++
239			if progress != nil {
240				progress(processedCount, totalCount)
241			}
242		}
243	
244		slog.Debug("Loaded sessions", "count", len(sessions))
245		return sessions, nil

311	// ExecAgentAndWatch opens the VS Code variant at the project path and then watches the
312	// workspace's chat store, auto-saving session updates via sessionCallback. VS Code
313	// Copilot is an IDE, not a CLI: there is no child process whose exit ends the session,
314	// so this blocks until the user interrupts (Ctrl-C) rather than until an agent exits.
315	//
316	// The resume flow (resumeSessionID != "") arrives here after ReconstructSession has
317	// already written the imported session into the workspace's chat store — the "session
318	// is ready" note only makes sense in that case, not on a plain `specstory run`.
319	// (Mirrors the Cursor IDE provider's behavior.)
320	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
321		if resumeSessionID != "" {
322			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nSession is ready in %s. Open the Chat panel to find it.\n", p.variant.AppName)
323		}
324		if err := p.openApp(projectPath, customCommand); err != nil {
325			// Opening is best-effort; a failure here should not surface as a hard error
326			// since the user can open the IDE manually and watching still works.
327			slog.Debug("Could not open the IDE automatically", "app", p.variant.AppName, "error", err)
328			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Open %s manually in: %s\n", p.variant.AppName, projectPath)
329			if errors.Is(err, errAppCLIMissing) {
330				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "To let SpecStory open the project for you, install the `%s` shell command:\n", p.variant.Command)
331				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "open the command palette in %s (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) and run \"Shell Command: Install '%s' command in PATH\".\n", p.variant.AppName, p.variant.Command)
332			}
333		}
334	
335		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Watching %s Copilot sessions in this project — press Ctrl-C to stop.\n", p.variant.AppName)
336		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
337		defer cancel()
338	
339		// The watcher needs the project's workspace entry, which won't exist yet if this
340		// project has never been opened in this VS Code variant — the open above creates
341		// it a moment later, once the IDE actually opens the folder. Retry until the
342		// watcher can start or the user interrupts.
343		printedWaiting := false
344		for {
345			err := p.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
346			if ctx.Err() != nil || err == nil {
347				return nil
348			}
349			if !printedWaiting {
350				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Waiting for %s to open this project...\n", p.variant.AppName)
351				printedWaiting = true
352			}
353			slog.Debug("Copilot watcher not ready, retrying", "app", p.variant.AppName, "error", err)
354			select {
355			case <-ctx.Done():
356				return nil
357			case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
358			}
359		}
360	}
361	
362	// errAppCLIMissing signals that the variant's CLI launcher is not on PATH. On macOS the
363	// command is opt-in (installed from the app's command palette), so its absence is an
364	// expected condition, not a failure — callers use this to print installation guidance
365	// instead of a generic error.
366	var errAppCLIMissing = errors.New("the app's shell command is not installed")
367	
368	// openApp launches the VS Code variant at the given project path. By default it uses
369	// the variant's own CLI launcher (`code`, `code-insiders`, …) — the only launcher that
370	// reliably opens the directory as a workspace window (`open -a` on macOS mostly just
371	// activates an already-running instance on its home screen, so it is deliberately not
372	// used as a fallback). A custom command (from --command or the matching *_cmd config
373	// entry) overrides the launcher binary and prepends any extra arguments before the
374	// project path.
375	//
376	// When the default CLI isn't on PATH, errAppCLIMissing is returned so the caller can
377	// tell the user how to install it; a missing custom launcher returns a plain error,
378	// since the install guidance only applies to the variant's own command. On Windows the
379	// launcher is a .cmd shim, which exec.LookPath resolves via PATHEXT.
380	func (p *Provider) openApp(projectPath, customCommand string) error {
381		launcher := p.variant.Command
382		var args []string
383		if customCommand != "" {
384			if parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand); len(parts) > 0 {
385				launcher = parts[0]
386				args = parts[1:]
387			}
388		}
389	
390		if _, err := exec.LookPath(launcher); err != nil {
391			if customCommand == "" {
392				return errAppCLIMissing
393			}
394			return fmt.Errorf("configured %s launcher %q not found on PATH: %w", p.variant.AppName, launcher, err)
395		}
396	
397		args = append(args, projectPath)
398		if out, err := exec.Command(launcher, args...).CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
399			return fmt.Errorf("%s launcher %q failed: %w: %s", p.variant.AppName, launcher, err, string(out))
400		}
401		return nil
402	}
403	
404	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every VS Code Copilot session across all
405	// workspaces, regardless of project. OriginCwd is resolved from each workspace's
406	// workspace.json (folder URI, or the .code-workspace file path for multi-root
407	// workspaces — FindWorkspaceForProject matches both back). NativePath is the session
408	// file itself. Lightweight: sessions are read for metadata only, no SessionData parse.
409	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
410		slog.Debug("ListAllAgentChatSessions: enumerating all Copilot sessions", "app", p.variant.AppName)
411	
412		storagePath := p.workspaceStoragePath()
413		if storagePath == "" {
414			// No workspace storage means this VS Code variant was never used here — nothing to index.
415			return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil
416		}
417	
418		entries, err := os.ReadDir(storagePath)
419		if err != nil {
420			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read workspace storage directory: %w", err)
421		}
422	
423		// A session can exist as both <id>.json (older) and <id>.jsonl (newer) — keep one
424		// ref per session ID, preferring the .jsonl file (matching LoadSessionByID).
425		refByID := make(map[string]spi.GlobalSessionRef)
426		for _, entry := range entries {
427			if !entry.IsDir() {
428				continue
429			}
430			workspaceDir := filepath.Join(storagePath, entry.Name())
431			collectWorkspaceSessionRefs(workspaceDir, refByID)
432		}
433	
434		refs := make([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(refByID))
435		for _, ref := range refByID {
436			refs = append(refs, ref)
437		}
438	
439		slog.Info("Listed all Copilot sessions", "app", p.variant.AppName, "count", len(refs))
440		return refs, nil
441	}
442	
443	// collectWorkspaceSessionRefs adds one GlobalSessionRef per non-empty session in the
444	// given workspace storage directory to refByID. Workspaces without a resolvable
445	// workspace.json or without chat sessions are skipped silently — both are normal
446	// (settings-only workspaces, projects where Copilot chat was never used).
447	func collectWorkspaceSessionRefs(workspaceDir string, refByID map[string]spi.GlobalSessionRef) {
448		workspaceJSON, err := readWorkspaceJSON(GetWorkspaceMetadataPath(workspaceDir))
449		if err != nil {
450			slog.Debug("Skipping workspace directory (no valid workspace.json)",
451				"workspaceDir", workspaceDir, "error", err)
452			return
453		}
454	
455		// Prefer the multi-root workspace URI over the single folder URI, matching
456		// FindWorkspaceForProject, so OriginCwd round-trips through the same matcher.
457		workspaceURI := workspaceJSON.Workspace
458		if workspaceURI == "" {
459			workspaceURI = workspaceJSON.Folder
460		}
461		if workspaceURI == "" {
462			return
463		}
464		originCwd, err := uriToPath(workspaceURI)
465		if err != nil {
466			slog.Debug("Skipping workspace directory (invalid URI)",
467				"workspaceDir", workspaceDir, "uri", workspaceURI, "error", err)
468			return
469		}
470	
471		sessionFiles, err := LoadAllSessionFiles(workspaceDir)
472		if err != nil {
473			// Most commonly the chatSessions directory does not exist — not an error.
474			slog.Debug("No chat sessions in workspace", "workspaceDir", workspaceDir, "error", err)
475			return
476		}
477	
478		for _, sessionFile := range sessionFiles {
479			composer, err := LoadSessionFile(sessionFile)
480			if err != nil {
481				slog.Warn("Failed to load session file", "file", sessionFile, "error", err)
482				continue
483			}
484	
485			// Same emptiness rule as ListAgentChatSessions: skip sessions with neither
486			// chat messages nor editing operations so the index only holds real sessions.
487			state, err := LoadStateFile(workspaceDir, composer.SessionID)
488			if err != nil {
489				slog.Warn("Failed to load state file", "sessionId", composer.SessionID, "error", err)
490			}
491			if len(composer.Requests) == 0 && !hasEditingActivity(state) {
492				slog.Debug("Skipping empty session", "sessionId", composer.SessionID)
493				continue
494			}
495	
496			// Prefer the .jsonl file when the same session exists in both formats.
497			if existing, seen := refByID[composer.SessionID]; seen {
498				if strings.HasSuffix(existing.NativePath, ".jsonl") || !strings.HasSuffix(sessionFile, ".jsonl") {
499					continue
500				}
501			}
502	
503			meta := extractCopilotIDESessionMetadata(composer)
504			refByID[composer.SessionID] = spi.GlobalSessionRef{
505				SessionID:  meta.SessionID,
506				CreatedAt:  meta.CreatedAt,
507				Slug:       meta.Slug,
508				Name:       meta.Name,
509				NativePath: sessionFile,
510				OriginCwd:  originCwd,
511			}
512		}
513	}

515	// WatchAgent watches for new/updated chat sessions
516	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
517		slog.Debug("WatchAgent", "projectPath", projectPath, "debugRaw", debugRaw)
518	
519		// Find workspace for project
520		workspace, err := p.FindWorkspaceForProject(projectPath)
521		if err != nil {
522			return fmt.Errorf("failed to find workspace: %w", err)
523		}
524	
525		// Start watching the chatSessions directory
526		return p.WatchChatSessions(ctx, workspace.Dir, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
527	}

529	// extractCopilotIDESessionMetadata extracts lightweight session metadata from a VSCodeComposer
530	// without fully parsing the conversation
531	func extractCopilotIDESessionMetadata(composer *VSCodeComposer) spi.SessionMetadata {
532		// Use session ID
533		sessionID := composer.SessionID
534	
535		// Convert timestamp (milliseconds to ISO 8601)
536		createdAt := FormatTimestamp(composer.CreationDate)
537	
538		// Generate slug using existing GenerateSlug function
539		slug := GenerateSlug(*composer)
540	
541		// Generate human-readable name
542		name := generateCopilotIDESessionName(composer)
543	
544		return spi.SessionMetadata{
545			SessionID: sessionID,
546			CreatedAt: createdAt,
547			Slug:      slug,
548			Name:      name,
549		}
550	}
551	
552	// generateCopilotIDESessionName creates a human-readable session name from composer data
553	func generateCopilotIDESessionName(composer *VSCodeComposer) string {
554		// Prefer custom title if available (it's already human-readable)
555		if composer.CustomTitle != "" {
556			return spi.GenerateReadableName(composer.CustomTitle)
557		}
558	
559		// Use name if available
560		if composer.Name != "" {
561			return spi.GenerateReadableName(composer.Name)
562		}
563	
564		// Otherwise, use first request message
565		if len(composer.Requests) > 0 {
566			firstMsg := composer.Requests[0].Message.Text
567			if firstMsg != "" {
568				return spi.GenerateReadableName(firstMsg)
569			}
570		}
571	
572		// Fallback to empty string (shouldn't happen with non-empty conversations)
573		return ""
574	}
575	
576	// hasEditingActivity checks if a state file contains editing operations
577	func hasEditingActivity(state *VSCodeStateFile) bool {
578		if state == nil {
579			return false
580		}
581	
582		// Version 2 format: check timeline.operations
583		if state.Timeline != nil && len(state.Timeline.Operations) > 0 {
584			return true
585		}
586	
587		// Version 1 format: check recentSnapshot for entries
588		if state.RecentSnapshot != nil {
589			// Handle array format
590			if stopsArray, ok := state.RecentSnapshot.([]any); ok {
591				for _, stopData := range stopsArray {
592					if stopMap, ok := stopData.(map[string]any); ok {
593						if entriesData, ok := stopMap["entries"].([]any); ok && len(entriesData) > 0 {
594							return true
595						}
596					}
597				}
598			}
599			// Handle object format
600			if stopMap, ok := state.RecentSnapshot.(map[string]any); ok {
601				if entriesData, ok := stopMap["entries"].([]any); ok && len(entriesData) > 0 {
602					return true
603				}
604			}
605		}
606	
607		return false
608	}

1	// Package factory provides the provider registry and factory implementation.
2	// This package imports all concrete provider implementations and manages
3	// their registration, avoiding circular dependencies in the SPI layer.
4	package factory
5	
6	import (
7		"fmt"
8		"log/slog"
9		"sort"
10		"strings"
11		"sync"
12	
13		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/antigravitycli"
14		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/claudecode"
15		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/codexcli"
16		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/copilotide"
17		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcli"
18		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursoride"
19		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/deepseektui"
20		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/droidcli"

22		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
23	)
24	
25	// Registry manages all registered providers
26	type Registry struct {
27		providers         map[string]spi.Provider // key is the provider ID (e.g., "claude", "cursor")
28		mu                sync.RWMutex
29		initialized       bool
30		providerListCache string    // Cached formatted provider list string
31		providerListOnce  sync.Once // Ensures provider list is built only once
32	}
33	
34	// Global registry instance
35	var (
36		registry = &Registry{
37			providers: make(map[string]spi.Provider),
38		}
39		once sync.Once
40	)
41	
42	// ensureInitialized makes sure providers are registered
43	func (r *Registry) ensureInitialized() {
44		once.Do(func() {
45			r.registerAll()
46		})
47	}
48	
49	// registerAll registers all known providers.
50	// This is the ONLY place that needs to be updated when adding new providers.
51	func (r *Registry) registerAll() {
52		r.mu.Lock()
53		defer r.mu.Unlock()
54	
55		if r.initialized {
56			slog.Debug("Provider registry already initialized, skipping registration")
57			return
58		}
59	
60		slog.Debug("Initializing provider registry")
61	
62		// Register providers with simple IDs
63		// Each provider directly implements the spi.Provider interface
64		claudeProvider := claudecode.NewProvider()
65		r.providers["claude"] = claudeProvider
66		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "claude", "name", claudeProvider.Name())
67	
68		cursorProvider := cursorcli.NewProvider()
69		r.providers["cursor"] = cursorProvider
70		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "cursor", "name", cursorProvider.Name())
71	
72		codexProvider := codexcli.NewProvider()
73		r.providers["codex"] = codexProvider
74		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "codex", "name", codexProvider.Name())
75	
76		geminiProvider := geminicli.NewProvider()
77		r.providers["gemini"] = geminiProvider
78		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "gemini", "name", geminiProvider.Name())
79	
80		droidProvider := droidcli.NewProvider()
81		r.providers["droid"] = droidProvider
82		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "droid", "name", droidProvider.Name())
83	
84		cursorideProvider := cursoride.NewProvider()
85		r.providers["cursoride"] = cursorideProvider
86		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "cursoride", "name", cursorideProvider.Name())
87	
88		// The Copilot IDE provider is variant-driven: one instance per VS Code
89		// distribution, keyed by the variant's own ID so the registry key always

91		copilotideProvider := copilotide.NewProvider(copilotide.VSCode)
92		r.providers[copilotide.VSCode.ID] = copilotideProvider

98	
99		copilotideVSCodiumProvider := copilotide.NewProvider(copilotide.VSCodium)
100		r.providers[copilotide.VSCodium.ID] = copilotideVSCodiumProvider
101		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", copilotide.VSCodium.ID, "name", copilotideVSCodiumProvider.Name())
102	
103		copilotideVSCodiumInsidersProvider := copilotide.NewProvider(copilotide.VSCodiumInsiders)
104		r.providers[copilotide.VSCodiumInsiders.ID] = copilotideVSCodiumInsidersProvider
105		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", copilotide.VSCodiumInsiders.ID, "name", copilotideVSCodiumInsidersProvider.Name())
106	
107		deepseekProvider := deepseektui.NewProvider()
108		r.providers["deepseek"] = deepseekProvider
109		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "deepseek", "name", deepseekProvider.Name())
110	
111		antigravityProvider := antigravitycli.NewProvider()
112		r.providers["antigravity"] = antigravityProvider
113		slog.Debug("Registered provider", "id", "antigravity", "name", antigravityProvider.Name())
114

118	
119	// ListIDsUnsafe returns provider IDs without locking (for internal use only)
120	func (r *Registry) ListIDsUnsafe() []string {
121		ids := make([]string, 0, len(r.providers))
122		for id := range r.providers {
123			ids = append(ids, id)
124		}
125		sort.Strings(ids)
126		return ids
127	}
128	
129	// GetRegistry returns the global registry instance
130	func GetRegistry() *Registry {
131		registry.ensureInitialized()
132		return registry
133	}
134	
135	// Get retrieves a provider by ID (case-insensitive)
136	func (r *Registry) Get(id string) (spi.Provider, error) {
137		r.ensureInitialized()
138		r.mu.RLock()
139		defer r.mu.RUnlock()
140	
141		// Case-insensitive lookup
142		for provID, provider := range r.providers {
143			if strings.EqualFold(provID, id) {
144				slog.Debug("Retrieved provider", "requested_id", id, "matched_id", provID, "name", provider.Name())
145				return provider, nil
146			}
147		}
148	
149		// Log available providers when lookup fails to aid debugging
150		availableIDs := make([]string, 0, len(r.providers))
151		for id := range r.providers {
152			availableIDs = append(availableIDs, id)
153		}
154		sort.Strings(availableIDs)
155	
156		slog.Warn("Provider not found",
157			"requested_id", id,
158			"available_providers", availableIDs)
159	
160		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provider '%s' not found", id)
161	}
162	
163	// GetAll returns all registered providers as a map of ID to Provider
164	func (r *Registry) GetAll() map[string]spi.Provider {
165		r.ensureInitialized()
166		r.mu.RLock()
167		defer r.mu.RUnlock()
168	
169		// Return a copy to prevent external modification
170		result := make(map[string]spi.Provider)
171		for id, provider := range r.providers {
172			result[id] = provider
173		}
174	
175		return result
176	}
177	
178	// ListIDs returns all registered provider IDs (sorted)
179	func (r *Registry) ListIDs() []string {
180		r.ensureInitialized()
181		r.mu.RLock()
182		defer r.mu.RUnlock()
183	
184		ids := make([]string, 0, len(r.providers))
185		for id := range r.providers {
186			ids = append(ids, id)
187		}
188	
189		sort.Strings(ids)
190		return ids
191	}
192	
193	// GetDefault returns the default provider (Claude)
194	func (r *Registry) GetDefault() (spi.Provider, error) {
195		r.ensureInitialized()
196		slog.Debug("Getting default provider (claude)")
197		return r.Get("claude")
198	}
199	
200	// GetProviderList returns a formatted string listing all providers.
201	// Used for help text and error messages.
202	// The result is cached since providers are static for the lifetime of the process.
203	func (r *Registry) GetProviderList() string {
204		r.ensureInitialized()
205	
206		// Build the provider list only once and cache it
207		r.providerListOnce.Do(func() {
208			r.mu.RLock()
209			defer r.mu.RUnlock()
210	
211			if len(r.providers) == 0 {
212				r.providerListCache = "No providers registered"
213				return
214			}
215	
216			// Get sorted IDs for consistent ordering
217			ids := make([]string, 0, len(r.providers))
218			for id := range r.providers {
219				ids = append(ids, id)
220			}
221			sort.Strings(ids)
222	
223			// Build the formatted list by accessing providers directly (no Get() calls)
224			var parts []string
225			for _, id := range ids {
226				if provider, ok := r.providers[id]; ok {
227					parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", id, provider.Name()))
228				}
229			}
230	
231			r.providerListCache = strings.Join(parts, ", ")
232		})
233	
234		return r.providerListCache
235	}

13	)
14	
15	// WorkspaceMatch represents a matched workspace directory
16	type WorkspaceMatch struct {
17		ID   string // Workspace directory name
18		Dir  string // Full path to workspace directory
19		URI  string // Original workspace URI
20		Path string // Resolved workspace path
21	}
22	
23	// WorkspaceJSON represents the structure of workspace.json
24	type WorkspaceJSON struct {
25		Workspace string `json:"workspace,omitempty"` // For multi-root workspaces
26		Folder    string `json:"folder,omitempty"`    // For single folder workspaces
27	}
28	
29	// FindWorkspaceForProject finds the workspace directory that matches the given project path
30	// Returns the workspace match or an error if not found
31	func (p *Provider) FindWorkspaceForProject(projectPath string) (*WorkspaceMatch, error) {
32		return p.findWorkspaceForProject(projectPath, true)
33	}
34	
35	// findWorkspaceForProject matches projectPath against every workspace.json in the
36	// variant's storage directory. requireChatSessions filters out matches that have never
37	// had a chat session — wanted when reading sessions, not when picking a write target
38	// for reconstruction (the resume flow creates the chatSessions directory when writing).
39	func (p *Provider) findWorkspaceForProject(projectPath string, requireChatSessions bool) (*WorkspaceMatch, error) {
40		// Get canonical project path (resolve symlinks, normalize case)
41		absProjectPath, err := filepath.Abs(projectPath)
42		if err != nil {
43			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get absolute path: %w", err)
44		}
45	
46		canonicalProjectPath, err := spi.GetCanonicalPath(absProjectPath)
47		if err != nil {
48			slog.Warn("Failed to get canonical path, using absolute path",
49				"projectPath", projectPath,
50				"error", err)
51			canonicalProjectPath = absProjectPath
52		}
53	
54		// If the project path is itself a .code-workspace file, pre-collect its folders.
55		// This lets us also match workspace entries opened directly from those folders
56		// (Method 4 below), so both usage patterns are discoverable via the workspace file path.
57		var workspaceFileFolders []string
58		if strings.HasSuffix(canonicalProjectPath, ".code-workspace") {
59			workspaceFileFolders = collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(canonicalProjectPath)
60		}
61	
62		slog.Debug("Searching for workspace matching project",
63			"projectPath", projectPath,
64			"canonicalPath", canonicalProjectPath)
65	
66		// Get workspace storage directory
67		workspaceStoragePath := p.workspaceStoragePath()
68		if workspaceStoragePath == "" {
69			return nil, fmt.Errorf("workspace storage directory not found")
70		}
71	
72		// Read all workspace directories
73		entries, err := os.ReadDir(workspaceStoragePath)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read workspace storage directory: %w", err)
76		}
77	
78		// Track all workspace directories for potential matches
79		var matches []WorkspaceMatch
80	
81		// Check each workspace directory
82		for _, entry := range entries {
83			if !entry.IsDir() {
84				continue
85			}
86	
87			workspaceID := entry.Name()
88			workspaceDir := filepath.Join(workspaceStoragePath, workspaceID)
89	
90			// Read workspace.json
91			workspaceJSONPath := GetWorkspaceMetadataPath(workspaceDir)
92			workspaceJSON, err := readWorkspaceJSON(workspaceJSONPath)
93			if err != nil {
94				slog.Debug("Skipping workspace directory (no valid workspace.json)",
95					"workspaceID", workspaceID,
96					"error", err)
97				continue
98			}
99	
100			// Get the workspace URI (prefer workspace over folder)
101			workspaceURI := workspaceJSON.Workspace
102			if workspaceURI == "" {
103				workspaceURI = workspaceJSON.Folder
104			}
105	
106			if workspaceURI == "" {
107				slog.Debug("Skipping workspace directory (no workspace or folder URI)",
108					"workspaceID", workspaceID)
109				continue
110			}
111	
112			// Convert URI to file path
113			workspaceFilePath, err := uriToPath(workspaceURI)
114			if err != nil {
115				slog.Debug("Skipping workspace directory (invalid URI)",
116					"workspaceID", workspaceID,
117					"uri", workspaceURI,
118					"error", err)
119				continue
120			}
121	
122			// Get canonical workspace path
123			canonicalWorkspacePath, err := spi.GetCanonicalPath(workspaceFilePath)
124			if err != nil {
125				slog.Debug("Failed to get canonical workspace path",
126					"workspacePath", workspaceFilePath,
127					"error", err)
128				canonicalWorkspacePath = workspaceFilePath
129			}
130	
131			// Direct path match (folder opened directly).
132			isMatch := canonicalProjectPath == canonicalWorkspacePath
133	
134			// Method 3: Code workspace file matching.
135			// When VS Code is opened via a .code-workspace file, workspace.json stores
136			// the workspace file URI rather than the folder URI. Check whether that
137			// workspace file lists our target folder as one of its folders.
138			if !isMatch && strings.HasSuffix(canonicalWorkspacePath, ".code-workspace") {
139				if codeWorkspaceContainsFolder(canonicalWorkspacePath, canonicalProjectPath) {
140					isMatch = true
141					slog.Debug("Matched workspace by .code-workspace folder reference",
142						"workspaceID", workspaceID,
143						"workspaceFile", canonicalWorkspacePath,
144						"targetFolder", canonicalProjectPath)
145				}
146			}
147	
148			// Method 4: project path is a .code-workspace file — also match workspace entries
149			// opened directly from a folder listed in that workspace file.
150			if !isMatch {
151				for _, folderPath := range workspaceFileFolders {
152					if canonicalWorkspacePath == folderPath {
153						isMatch = true
154						slog.Debug("Matched workspace entry by folder listed in .code-workspace",
155							"workspaceID", workspaceID,
156							"folder", folderPath,
157							"workspaceFile", canonicalProjectPath)
158						break
159					}
160				}
161			}
162	
163			if isMatch {
164				// Check if chatSessions directory exists (skipped for reconstruction targets,
165				// where the directory is created on first write)
166				chatSessionsPath := GetChatSessionsPath(workspaceDir)
167				if _, err := os.Stat(chatSessionsPath); err != nil && requireChatSessions {
168					slog.Debug("Workspace match found but chatSessions directory missing",
169						"workspaceID", workspaceID,
170						"chatSessionsPath", chatSessionsPath)
171					continue
172				}
173	
174				matches = append(matches, WorkspaceMatch{
175					ID:   workspaceID,
176					Dir:  workspaceDir,
177					URI:  workspaceURI,
178					Path: workspaceFilePath,
179				})
180	
181				slog.Info("Found matching workspace",
182					"workspaceID", workspaceID,
183					"projectPath", canonicalProjectPath,
184					"workspaceURI", workspaceURI)
185			}
186		}
187	
188		if len(matches) == 0 {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no workspace found for project path %s (searched VS Code workspace storage in %s; open the folder in VS Code once to create one)", projectPath, workspaceStoragePath)
190		}
191	
192		// If multiple matches, return the newest one (based on state.vscdb modification time)
193		if len(matches) > 1 {
194			slog.Warn("Multiple workspaces match project path, selecting newest",
195				"projectPath", projectPath,
196				"matchCount", len(matches))
197			return selectNewestWorkspace(matches)
198		}
199	
200		return &matches[0], nil
201	}
202	
203	// selectNewestWorkspace returns the workspace with the newest state.vscdb modification time
204	func selectNewestWorkspace(matches []WorkspaceMatch) (*WorkspaceMatch, error) {
205		var newest *WorkspaceMatch
206		var newestTime int64
207	
208		for i := range matches {
209			match := &matches[i]
210			stateDBPath := GetWorkspaceStateDBPath(match.Dir)
211	
212			info, err := os.Stat(stateDBPath)
213			if err != nil {
214				slog.Debug("Failed to stat state.vscdb", "path", stateDBPath, "error", err)
215				continue
216			}
217	
218			modTime := info.ModTime().Unix()
219			if newest == nil || modTime > newestTime {
220				newest = match
221				newestTime = modTime
222			}
223		}
224	
225		if newest == nil {
226			return &matches[0], nil // Fall back to first match
227		}
228	
229		slog.Debug("Selected newest workspace", "workspaceID", newest.ID, "modTime", newestTime)
230		return newest, nil
231	}
232	
233	// collectCodeWorkspaceFolders reads a .code-workspace JSON file and returns the
234	// canonical paths of all listed folders. Relative paths are resolved against the
235	// workspace file's directory.
236	func collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(workspaceFilePath string) []string {
237		data, err := os.ReadFile(workspaceFilePath)
238		if err != nil {
239			slog.Debug("collectCodeWorkspaceFolders: failed to read workspace file",
240				"path", workspaceFilePath, "error", err)
241			return nil
242		}
243	
244		var workspace struct {
245			Folders []struct {
246				Path string `json:"path"`
247			} `json:"folders"`
248		}
249		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &workspace); err != nil {
250			slog.Debug("collectCodeWorkspaceFolders: failed to parse workspace file",
251				"path", workspaceFilePath, "error", err)
252			return nil
253		}
254	
255		workspaceDir := filepath.Dir(workspaceFilePath)
256		var folders []string
257		for _, folder := range workspace.Folders {
258			if folder.Path == "" {
259				continue
260			}
261	
262			// Resolve relative paths against the workspace file's directory.
263			var resolved string
264			if filepath.IsAbs(folder.Path) {
265				resolved = folder.Path
266			} else {
267				resolved = filepath.Join(workspaceDir, folder.Path)
268			}
269	
270			canonical, err := spi.GetCanonicalPath(resolved)
271			if err != nil {
272				canonical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
273			}
274			folders = append(folders, canonical)
275		}
276	
277		return folders
278	}
279	
280	// codeWorkspaceContainsFolder reports whether canonicalFolder is listed in the
281	// .code-workspace file at workspaceFilePath.
282	func codeWorkspaceContainsFolder(workspaceFilePath, canonicalFolder string) bool {
283		for _, f := range collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(workspaceFilePath) {
284			if f == canonicalFolder {
285				return true
286			}
287		}
288		return false
289	}
290	
291	// readWorkspaceJSON reads and parses a workspace.json file
292	func readWorkspaceJSON(path string) (*WorkspaceJSON, error) {
293		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
294		if err != nil {
295			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read workspace.json: %w", err)
296		}
297	
298		var workspace WorkspaceJSON
299		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &workspace); err != nil {
300			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse workspace.json: %w", err)
301		}
302	
303		return &workspace, nil
304	}
305	
306	// uriToPath converts a file:// URI to a local file path
307	func uriToPath(uri string) (string, error) {
308		// Handle file:// URIs
309		if !strings.HasPrefix(uri, "file://") {
310			return "", fmt.Errorf("URI must start with file://: %s", uri)
311		}
312	
313		// Parse the URI
314		parsedURI, err := url.Parse(uri)
315		if err != nil {
316			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse URI: %w", err)
317		}
318	
319		// url.Parse already percent-decodes into Path (e.g. %20 -> space), so no
320		// extra PathUnescape is needed — unescaping again would corrupt paths
321		// containing literal % sequences.
322		path := parsedURI.Path
323	
324		// On Windows, URL paths have an extra leading slash (e.g., /C:/Users)
325		// but we don't support Windows, so we can just use the path as-is
326	
327		return path, nil
328	}

45	// LoadSessionFile reads and parses a single session JSON or JSONL file

153	// parseJSONL parses JSONL format with incremental updates
154	// First line (kind: 0) contains initial state in "v" field
155	// Subsequent lines (kind: 1) contain updates with key path in "k" and value in "v"
156	func parseJSONL(data []byte) (VSCodeComposer, error) {
157		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
158		if trimmed == "" {
159			return VSCodeComposer{}, fmt.Errorf("empty JSONL file")
160		}
161		lines := strings.Split(trimmed, "\n")
162	
163		// Parse first line - should be kind:0 with initial state
164		var firstLine struct {
165			Kind int             `json:"kind"`
166			V    json.RawMessage `json:"v"`
167		}
168	
169		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(lines[0]), &firstLine); err != nil {
170			return VSCodeComposer{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse first JSONL line: %w", err)
171		}
172	
173		if firstLine.Kind != 0 {
174			return VSCodeComposer{}, fmt.Errorf("expected kind:0 in first line, got kind:%d", firstLine.Kind)
175		}
176	
177		// Keep the session in map form while applying updates so each line mutates
178		// in place; converting the whole composer to a map and back per update line
179		// is O(session size) per line and dominates load time on long sessions.
180		var composerMap map[string]any
181		if err := json.Unmarshal(firstLine.V, &composerMap); err != nil {
182			return VSCodeComposer{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse initial state in first JSONL line: %w", err)
183		}
184	
185		// Apply subsequent updates.
186		// kind:1 = incremental key-path update (small field changes, e.g. customTitle)
187		// kind:2 = bulk key-path replacement (e.g. full requests array written after initial snapshot)
188		// VS Code Copilot introduced kind:2 to split large payloads from the initial kind:0 snapshot.
189		for i := 1; i < len(lines); i++ {
190			var update struct {
191				Kind int   `json:"kind"`
192				K    []any `json:"k"` // Key path: string map keys and/or numeric array indices, e.g. ["requests", 3, "response"]
193				V    any   `json:"v"` // Value
194			}
195	
196			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(lines[i]), &update); err != nil {
197				slog.Warn("Failed to parse JSONL update line", "line", i+1, "error", err)
198				continue
199			}
200	
201			switch update.Kind {
202			case 1:
203				if len(update.K) > 0 {
204					// Replace the value at the key path
205					if err := applyUpdate(composerMap, update.K, update.V); err != nil {
206						slog.Warn("Failed to apply JSONL update", "line", i+1, "kind", update.Kind, "keyPath", update.K, "error", err)
207					}
208				}
209			case 2:
210				if len(update.K) > 0 {
211					// Append items to the array at the key path.
212					// VS Code writes one kind:2 per user turn, each containing only the new
213					// request(s) for that turn — not the full history — so we must accumulate.
214					if err := appendUpdate(composerMap, update.K, update.V); err != nil {
215						slog.Warn("Failed to apply JSONL append", "line", i+1, "kind", update.Kind, "keyPath", update.K, "error", err)
216					}
217				}
218			default:
219				// Log unknown kinds so we detect future format changes early
220				slog.Warn("Unknown JSONL kind, skipping line", "line", i+1, "kind", update.Kind)
221			}
222		}
223	
224		// Decode the fully-updated map into the typed composer once
225		finalData, err := json.Marshal(composerMap)
226		if err != nil {
227			return VSCodeComposer{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal updated session: %w", err)
228		}
229	
230		var composer VSCodeComposer
231		if err := json.Unmarshal(finalData, &composer); err != nil {
232			return VSCodeComposer{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse updated session: %w", err)
233		}
234	
235		return composer, nil
236	}

238	// pathIndex converts a numeric key path segment (JSON numbers decode as float64)
239	// to an integer array index.
240	func pathIndex(seg any) (int, bool) {
241		f, ok := seg.(float64)
242		if !ok || f != float64(int(f)) || f < 0 {
243			return 0, false
244		}
245		return int(f), true
246	}
247	
248	// setAtPath sets value at keyPath inside container, where string segments index
249	// maps (created when missing) and numeric segments index arrays (an index equal
250	// to the array length appends). It returns the possibly-new container because
251	// growing a slice reallocates it, so callers must store the result back.
252	func setAtPath(container any, keyPath []any, value any) (any, error) {
253		if len(keyPath) == 0 {
254			return value, nil
255		}
256	
257		switch seg := keyPath[0].(type) {
258		case string:
259			m, ok := container.(map[string]any)
260			if !ok {
261				if container != nil {
262					return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot set key %q on non-object value of type %T", seg, container)
263				}
264				m = make(map[string]any)
265			}
266			child, err := setAtPath(m[seg], keyPath[1:], value)
267			if err != nil {
268				return nil, err
269			}
270			m[seg] = child
271			return m, nil
272	
273		case float64:
274			idx, ok := pathIndex(seg)
275			if !ok {
276				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid array index in key path: %v", seg)
277			}
278			s, isSlice := container.([]any)
279			if !isSlice {
280				if container != nil {
281					return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot index into non-array value of type %T", container)
282				}
283				s = []any{}
284			}
285			if idx > len(s) {
286				return nil, fmt.Errorf("array index %d out of range (length %d)", idx, len(s))
287			}
288			if idx == len(s) {
289				s = append(s, nil)
290			}
291			child, err := setAtPath(s[idx], keyPath[1:], value)
292			if err != nil {
293				return nil, err
294			}
295			s[idx] = child
296			return s, nil
297	
298		default:
299			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported key path segment of type %T: %v", seg, seg)
300		}
301	}
302	
303	// getAtPath reads the value at keyPath inside container without modifying it.
304	// Returns nil when any segment is missing or of the wrong shape.
305	func getAtPath(container any, keyPath []any) any {
306		current := container
307		for _, seg := range keyPath {
308			switch key := seg.(type) {
309			case string:
310				m, ok := current.(map[string]any)
311				if !ok {
312					return nil
313				}
314				current = m[key]
315			case float64:
316				idx, ok := pathIndex(key)
317				if !ok {
318					return nil
319				}
320				s, isSlice := current.([]any)
321				if !isSlice || idx >= len(s) {
322					return nil
323				}
324				current = s[idx]
325			default:
326				return nil
327			}
328		}
329		return current
330	}
331	
332	// appendUpdate appends items to the array at a specific key path in the map-form session.
333	// Used for kind:2 lines where VS Code writes only the newly added items (e.g. a single
334	// new request per turn, or new response parts within a request) rather than the full
335	// array, so each write must be accumulated.
336	// Falls back to replace semantics when the target or incoming value is not an array.
337	func appendUpdate(composerMap map[string]any, keyPath []any, value any) error {
338		newItems, isArray := value.([]any)
339		if !isArray {
340			// Not an array delta — treat as a plain replace
341			return applyUpdate(composerMap, keyPath, value)
342		}
343	
344		// Append the new items to whatever is already there; fall back to replace if needed
345		if existing, ok := getAtPath(composerMap, keyPath).([]any); ok {
346			newItems = append(existing, newItems...)
347		}
348		return applyUpdate(composerMap, keyPath, newItems)
349	}
350	
351	// applyUpdate sets value at a specific key path in the map-form session.
352	// keyPath mixes string map keys and numeric array indices
353	// (e.g., ["requests", 3, "response"]).
354	func applyUpdate(composerMap map[string]any, keyPath []any, value any) error {
355		_, err := setAtPath(composerMap, keyPath, value)
356		return err
357	}

233						"error", err)
234					// Don't fail the operation if debug output fails
235				}
236			}

238			sessions = append(sessions, *session)
239			reportProgress()

387	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every Cursor IDE session across all workspaces,
388	// regardless of project. OriginCwd comes from the workspaceIdentifier embedded in each
389	// composer (the live association in Cursor >= 3.12), falling back to the workspace-DB
390	// scan for older sessions that predate the embedded field; when a composer appears in
391	// multiple workspaces (WSL/SSH setups) the first-seen path is used. NativePath is the
392	// global database path (shared by all sessions) because Cursor IDE stores all
393	// conversations as key-value rows in a single state.vscdb.
394	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
395		slog.Debug("ListAllAgentChatSessions: enumerating all Cursor IDE sessions")
396	
397		// Build the fallback composerID → project path mapping from the workspace databases.
398		composerToPath, err := ScanAllWorkspaceComposerPaths()
399		if err != nil {
400			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to scan workspaces: %w", err)
401		}
402	
403		// Load lightweight composer metadata from the global database (no bubble data).
404		globalDbPath, err := GetGlobalDatabasePath()
405		if err != nil {
406			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get global database path: %w", err)
407		}
408		composers, err := LoadAllComposerDataLightweight(globalDbPath)
409		if err != nil {
410			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load composer metadata: %w", err)
411		}
412	
413		var refs []spi.GlobalSessionRef
414		for composerID, composer := range composers {
415			// Prefer the embedded workspaceIdentifier, then the workspace-DB scan. A
416			// composer with neither has no known project and can't be indexed.
417			projectPath := ""
418			if composer.WorkspaceIdentifier != nil && composer.WorkspaceIdentifier.URI != nil {
419				projectPath = composer.WorkspaceIdentifier.URI.FsPath
420			}
421			if projectPath == "" {
422				projectPath = composerToPath[composerID]
423			}
424			if projectPath == "" {
425				slog.Debug("Composer has no known project association", "composerID", composerID)
426				continue
427			}
428	
429			// Skip composers that have never had a conversation.
430			if len(composer.Conversation) == 0 && len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly) == 0 {
431				slog.Debug("Skipping empty composer", "composerID", composerID)
432				continue
433			}
434	
435			// Local time, not UTC, so the same session gets an identical CreatedAt string
436			// here and in extractCursorIDESessionMetadata/ConvertToAgentChatSession.
437			var createdAt string
438			if composer.CreatedAt > 0 {
439				t := time.Unix(composer.CreatedAt/1000, (composer.CreatedAt%1000)*1000000)
440				createdAt = t.Format(time.RFC3339)
441			}
442	
443			refs = append(refs, spi.GlobalSessionRef{
444				SessionID:  composerID,
445				CreatedAt:  createdAt,
446				Slug:       generateSlug(composer),
447				Name:       generateCursorIDESessionName(composer),
448				NativePath: globalDbPath,
449				OriginCwd:  projectPath,
450			})
451		}
452	
453		slog.Info("Listed all Cursor IDE sessions", "count", len(refs))
454		return refs, nil
455	}

457	// ExecAgentAndWatch opens Cursor IDE at the project path and then watches the Cursor
458	// databases, auto-saving session updates via sessionCallback. Cursor IDE is an IDE, not
459	// a CLI: there is no child process whose exit ends the session, so this blocks until the
460	// user interrupts (Ctrl-C) rather than until an agent exits.
461	//
462	// The resume flow (resumeSessionID != "") arrives here after ReconstructSession has
463	// already written the imported session into the global database — the "session is ready"
464	// note only makes sense in that case, not on a plain `specstory run cursoride`.
465	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
466		if resumeSessionID != "" {
467			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nSession is ready in the Cursor IDE. Open the Agents panel to find it.")
468		}
469		if err := openCursorIDE(projectPath, customCommand); err != nil {
470			// Opening is best-effort; a failure here should not surface as a hard error
471			// since the user can open Cursor manually and watching still works.
472			slog.Debug("Could not open Cursor IDE automatically", "error", err)
473			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Open Cursor IDE manually in: %s\n", projectPath)
474			if errors.Is(err, errCursorCLIMissing) {
475				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "To let SpecStory open the project for you, install Cursor's shell command:")
476				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "open the command palette in Cursor (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) and run \"Shell Command: Install 'cursor' command\".")
477			}
478		}
479	
480		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Watching Cursor IDE sessions in this project — press Ctrl-C to stop.")
481		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
482		defer cancel()
483	
484		// The watcher needs the project's workspace entry, which won't exist yet if this
485		// project has never been opened in Cursor — the open above creates it a moment
486		// later, once Cursor actually opens the folder. Retry until the watcher can start
487		// or the user interrupts.
488		printedWaiting := false
489		for {
490			err := p.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
491			if ctx.Err() != nil || err == nil {
492				return nil
493			}
494			if !printedWaiting {
495				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Waiting for Cursor to open this project...")
496				printedWaiting = true
497			}
498			slog.Debug("Cursor IDE watcher not ready, retrying", "error", err)
499			select {
500			case <-ctx.Done():
501				return nil
502			case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
503			}
504		}
505	}
506	
507	// errCursorCLIMissing signals that Cursor's `cursor` shell command is not on PATH. The
508	// command is opt-in (installed from Cursor's command palette), so its absence is an
509	// expected condition, not a failure — callers use this to print installation guidance
510	// instead of a generic error.
511	var errCursorCLIMissing = errors.New("the `cursor` shell command is not installed")
512	
513	// openCursorIDE launches Cursor IDE at the given project path. By default it uses
514	// Cursor's own `cursor` CLI — the only launcher that reliably opens the directory as
515	// a workspace window (`open -a Cursor` on macOS mostly just activates an
516	// already-running instance on its home screen, so it is deliberately not used as a
517	// fallback). A custom command (from --command or the cursoride_cmd config) overrides
518	// the launcher binary and prepends any extra arguments before the project path.
519	//
520	// When the default `cursor` CLI isn't on PATH, errCursorCLIMissing is returned so the
521	// caller can tell the user how to install it; a missing custom launcher returns a
522	// plain error, since the install guidance only applies to Cursor's own command.
523	func openCursorIDE(projectPath, customCommand string) error {
524		launcher := "cursor"
525		var args []string
526		if customCommand != "" {
527			if parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand); len(parts) > 0 {
528				launcher = parts[0]
529				args = parts[1:]
530			}
531		}
532	
533		if _, err := exec.LookPath(launcher); err != nil {
534			if customCommand == "" {
535				return errCursorCLIMissing
536			}
537			return fmt.Errorf("configured Cursor IDE launcher %q not found on PATH: %w", launcher, err)
538		}
539	
540		args = append(args, projectPath)
541		if out, err := exec.Command(launcher, args...).CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
542			return fmt.Errorf("cursor IDE launcher %q failed: %w: %s", launcher, err, string(out))
543		}
544		return nil
545	}

547	// WatchAgent watches for Cursor IDE activity and calls the callback with AgentChatSession
548	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
549		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Starting Cursor IDE activity monitoring",
550			"projectPath", projectPath,
551			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
552	
553		// Create and start watcher
554		watcher, err := NewCursorIDEWatcher(projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback, defaultCheckInterval)
555		if err != nil {
556			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create watcher: %w", err)
557		}
558	
559		if err := watcher.Start(); err != nil {
560			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start watcher: %w", err)
561		}
562	
563		// Wait for context cancellation
564		<-ctx.Done()
565	
566		// Stop watcher gracefully
567		watcher.Stop()
568	
569		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Stopped Cursor IDE activity monitoring")
570		return nil
571	}

573	// writeDebugOutput writes debug JSON files for a Cursor IDE session

588	
589		slog.Debug("Wrote debug output",
590			"sessionID", session.SessionID,
591			"path", debugDir)
592	
593		return nil
594	}

596	// extractCursorIDESessionMetadata extracts lightweight session metadata from a ComposerData
597	// without fully parsing the conversation
598	func extractCursorIDESessionMetadata(composer *ComposerData) spi.SessionMetadata {
599		// Use composer ID as session ID
600		sessionID := composer.ComposerID
601	
602		// Convert timestamp (milliseconds to ISO 8601)
603		var createdAt string
604		if composer.CreatedAt > 0 {
605			t := time.Unix(composer.CreatedAt/1000, (composer.CreatedAt%1000)*1000000)
606			createdAt = t.Format(time.RFC3339)
607		} else {
608			createdAt = time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339)
609		}
610	
611		// Generate slug from composer name or first user message (using existing logic)
612		slug := generateSlug(composer)
613	
614		// Generate human-readable name
615		name := generateCursorIDESessionName(composer)
616	
617		return spi.SessionMetadata{
618			SessionID: sessionID,
619			CreatedAt: createdAt,
620			Slug:      slug,
621			Name:      name,
622		}
623	}
624	
625	// generateCursorIDESessionName creates a human-readable session name from composer data,
626	// taking the first candidate text (composer name, then first user message) that survives
627	// the readable-name transform. Falls back to empty (shouldn't happen with non-empty
628	// conversations).
629	func generateCursorIDESessionName(composer *ComposerData) string {
630		for _, text := range composerNameCandidates(composer) {
631			if name := spi.GenerateReadableName(text); name != "" {
632				return name
633			}
634		}
635		return ""
636	}

19	// WorkspaceMatch represents a matched workspace directory
20	type WorkspaceMatch struct {
21		ID     string // Workspace directory name
22		Path   string // Full path to workspace directory
23		DBPath string // Path to workspace database

27	// isUnixStylePathOnWindows detects if a path represents a remote (WSL/SSH) filesystem
28	// location while running on Windows. VS Code's fsPath returns these paths in two forms:
29	//   - "/home/user/project"  — forward-slash form (the raw fsPath value)
30	//   - "\home\user\project"  — backslash form (Windows filepath.Clean applied to the above)
31	//
32	// Both forms have no drive/volume name and must not be passed through filepath.Abs,
33	// which would corrupt them by prepending the current drive letter (e.g. C:\).
34	func isUnixStylePathOnWindows(path string) bool {
35		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" || filepath.VolumeName(path) != "" {
36			return false
37		}
38		// Forward-slash prefix: /home/user/project
39		if strings.HasPrefix(path, "/") {
40			return true
41		}
42		// Backslash prefix without UNC double-backslash: \home\user\project
43		// (VS Code converts the forward-slash form to this on Windows)
44		if strings.HasPrefix(path, `\`) && !strings.HasPrefix(path, `\\`) {
45			return true
46		}
47		return false
48	}
49	
50	// isWindowsWSLUNCPath reports whether path is a Windows UNC path pointing into WSL,
51	// i.e. \\wsl.localhost\<distro>\... or \\wsl$\<distro>\...
52	func isWindowsWSLUNCPath(path string) bool {
53		lower := strings.ToLower(path)
54		return strings.HasPrefix(lower, `\\wsl.localhost\`) || strings.HasPrefix(lower, `\\wsl$\`)
55	}
56	
57	// normalizeWindowsWSLPath converts Windows UNC WSL paths to Unix format.
58	// Handles paths like:
59	//   - \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\user\project -> /home/user/project
60	//   - \\wsl$\Ubuntu\home\user\project -> /home/user/project
61	func normalizeWindowsWSLPath(path string) string {
62		if !strings.Contains(path, "\\") {
63			return path
64		}
65	
66		// Convert backslashes to forward slashes
67		normalized := strings.ReplaceAll(path, "\\", "/")
68	
69		// Strip Windows UNC WSL prefixes and the distro name
70		lower := strings.ToLower(normalized)
71		for _, prefix := range []string{"//wsl.localhost/", "//wsl$/"} {
72			if strings.HasPrefix(lower, prefix) {
73				remainder := normalized[len(prefix):]
74				// Skip the distro name (e.g., "Ubuntu/home/user" -> "/home/user")
75				if slashIdx := strings.Index(remainder, "/"); slashIdx >= 0 {
76					return remainder[slashIdx:]
77				}
78				return "/"
79			}
80		}
81	
82		return normalized
83	}
84	
85	// normalizePathForComparison normalizes a path for workspace matching.
86	// Handles three cases:
87	// 1. Windows UNC WSL paths: \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\... -> /home/user/...
88	// 2. Unix-style paths on Windows (WSL/SSH remotes): preserved as-is
89	// 3. Normal paths: resolved to canonical form with symlinks and case normalization
90	func normalizePathForComparison(path string) (string, error) {
91		originalPath := path
92	
93		// Step 1: Normalize Windows UNC WSL paths (\\wsl.localhost\... or \\wsl$\...) to Unix format.
94		// We only trigger this for actual WSL UNC paths, not for ordinary Windows paths like C:\Users\...
95		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" && isWindowsWSLUNCPath(path) {
96			path = normalizeWindowsWSLPath(path)
97			if path != originalPath {
98				slog.Debug("Normalized Windows UNC WSL path",
99					"original", originalPath,
100					"normalized", path)
101			}
102		}
103	
104		// Step 2: Check if it's a Unix-style path on Windows (WSL/SSH remote)
105		if isUnixStylePathOnWindows(path) {
106			// Don't use filepath.Abs or GetCanonicalPath - they would corrupt the path
107			// on Windows by treating "/home/user/project" as a relative path
108			cleaned := filepath.Clean(path)
109			slog.Debug("Preserved Unix-style path on Windows",
110				"path", cleaned)
111			return cleaned, nil
112		}
113	
114		// Step 3: Normal path handling - resolve to canonical form
115		absPath, err := filepath.Abs(path)
116		if err != nil {
117			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get absolute path: %w", err)
118		}
119	
120		canonicalPath, err := spi.GetCanonicalPath(absPath)
121		if err != nil {
122			slog.Warn("Failed to get canonical path, using absolute path",
123				"path", path,
124				"error", err)
125			return absPath, nil
126		}
127	
128		return canonicalPath, nil
129	}

131	// FindWorkspaceForProject finds the workspace directory that matches the given project path.
132	// It is a var so tests can replace it with a stub that returns a temporary workspace.
133	var FindWorkspaceForProject = findWorkspaceForProject
134	
135	// findWorkspaceForProject is the real implementation; FindWorkspaceForProject delegates to it.
136	// It picks a single workspace for callers that need exactly one write/watch target (e.g.
137	// reconstructing a session into a specific state.vscdb). It delegates to
138	// FindAllWorkspacesForProject so it benefits from the same matching methods (direct path,
139	// remote basename fallback, .code-workspace folder membership) rather than duplicating
140	// a weaker, path-only version of that logic.
141	func findWorkspaceForProject(projectPath string) (*WorkspaceMatch, error) {
142		matches, err := FindAllWorkspacesForProject(projectPath)
143		if err != nil {
144			return nil, err
145		}
146	
147		if len(matches) == 1 {
148			return &matches[0], nil
149		}
150	
151		// Multiple matches: pick the most recently used workspace (by state.vscdb mtime),
152		// not just the first one in directory-listing order, so a reconstructed session
153		// lands in the workspace instance the user is most likely to actually open next.
154		best := &matches[0]
155		bestModTime := workspaceDBModTime(best)
156		for i := 1; i < len(matches); i++ {
157			if modTime := workspaceDBModTime(&matches[i]); modTime.After(bestModTime) {
158				best = &matches[i]
159				bestModTime = modTime
160			}
161		}
162	
163		slog.Debug("Multiple workspaces match project path, using most recently used",
164			"projectPath", projectPath,
165			"matchCount", len(matches),
166			"selectedWorkspaceID", best.ID)
167	
168		return best, nil
169	}

171	// EnsureWorkspaceForProject returns the workspace entry for the project, minting one in
172	// Cursor's workspaceStorage when the folder has never been opened in Cursor (the case
173	// where FindWorkspaceForProject has nothing to find, which would otherwise make the
174	// project unusable as a resume target). Minting reproduces Cursor's own single-folder
175	// workspace ID — md5(folder path + a platform stat salt; see workspaceIDStatSalt) — so
176	// when the user later opens the folder, Cursor computes the same ID and adopts the
177	// minted entry instead of creating a duplicate.
178	func EnsureWorkspaceForProject(projectPath string) (*WorkspaceMatch, error) {
179		if ws, err := FindWorkspaceForProject(projectPath); err == nil {
180			return ws, nil
181		}

183		id, err := cursorWorkspaceID(projectPath)
184		if err != nil {
185			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot determine Cursor workspace ID for %q: %w", projectPath, err)
186		}

188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, err

192		wsPath := filepath.Join(storagePath, id)
193		dbPath := filepath.Join(wsPath, "state.vscdb")

197			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create workspace storage directory: %w", err)
198		}
199		// workspace.json mirrors the format Cursor writes (2-space indented single field).
200		workspaceJSON, err := json.MarshalIndent(WorkspaceJSON{Folder: folderURI}, "", "  ")
201		if err != nil {
202			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal workspace.json: %w", err)
203		}
204		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(wsPath, "workspace.json"), workspaceJSON, 0644); err != nil {
205			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write workspace.json: %w", err)
206		}
207		if err := createEmptyWorkspaceDB(dbPath); err != nil {
208			return nil, err
209		}

211		slog.Info("Minted Cursor workspace entry for project",
212			"workspaceID", id, "projectPath", projectPath)
213	
214		return &WorkspaceMatch{ID: id, Path: wsPath, DBPath: dbPath, URI: folderURI}, nil
215	}
216	
217	// cursorWorkspaceID computes the workspace storage directory name Cursor derives for a
218	// local single-folder workspace: md5(folder path + platform stat salt). This mirrors
219	// getSingleFolderWorkspaceIdentifier in Cursor's main.js and was verified byte-for-byte
220	// against real workspaceStorage entries. The path is hashed exactly as given (no case
221	// or symlink normalization) because that is what Cursor does — the same folder opened
222	// via differently-spelled paths genuinely gets distinct workspace entries.
223	func cursorWorkspaceID(projectPath string) (string, error) {
224		info, err := os.Stat(projectPath)
225		if err != nil {
226			return "", err
227		}
228		sum := md5.Sum([]byte(projectPath + workspaceIDStatSalt(info)))
229		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]), nil
230	}
231	
232	// workspaceDBModTime returns the modification time of a workspace's state.vscdb, used
233	// as a proxy for how recently that workspace was actually used in Cursor IDE. Returns
234	// the zero time if the file can't be stat'd, so it loses any tie-break comparison
235	// rather than erroring out the whole lookup.
236	func workspaceDBModTime(m *WorkspaceMatch) time.Time {
237		info, err := os.Stat(m.DBPath)
238		if err != nil {
239			return time.Time{}
240		}
241		return info.ModTime()

244	// FindAllWorkspacesForProject finds all workspace directories that match the given project path.
245	// In WSL, the same project may have multiple workspaces with different URI formats
246	// (e.g., file://wsl.localhost/... and vscode-remote://wsl+...).
247	// For SSH remotes and dev containers, where the workspace path lives on a different machine
248	// or inside a container and can never equal the local path, matching falls back to comparing
249	// the workspace folder basename.

251		// Normalize project path for comparison (handles Windows WSL paths, Unix paths on Windows, etc.)
252		canonicalProjectPath, err := normalizePathForComparison(projectPath)

255		}

265		var workspaceFileFolders []string

271			"projectPath", projectPath,
272			"canonicalPath", canonicalProjectPath,
273			"projectBasename", projectBasename)
274	
275		// Get workspace storage directory
276		workspaceStoragePath, err := GetWorkspaceStoragePath()
277		if err != nil {
278			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get workspace storage path: %w", err)
279		}
280	
281		// Read all workspace directories
282		entries, err := os.ReadDir(workspaceStoragePath)
283		if err != nil {

285		}
286	
287		var matches []WorkspaceMatch
288	
289		for _, entry := range entries {
290			if !entry.IsDir() {
291				continue
292			}
293	
294			workspaceID := entry.Name()
295			workspacePath := filepath.Join(workspaceStoragePath, workspaceID)
296	
297			// Read workspace.json
298			workspaceJSONPath := filepath.Join(workspacePath, "workspace.json")
299			workspaceJSON, err := readWorkspaceJSON(workspaceJSONPath)
300			if err != nil {
301				continue
302			}
303	
304			workspaceURI := workspaceJSON.Workspace
305			if workspaceURI == "" {
306				workspaceURI = workspaceJSON.Folder
307			}
308			if workspaceURI == "" {
309				continue
310			}
311	
312			workspaceFilePath, err := uriToPath(workspaceURI)
313			if err != nil {

315			}
316	
317			// Normalize workspace path for comparison (handles Unix paths on Windows, etc.)
318			canonicalWorkspacePath, err := normalizePathForComparison(workspaceFilePath)

327			// Method 1: Direct path matching (works for local and WSL workspaces)
328			isMatch := canonicalProjectPath == canonicalWorkspacePath
329	
330			// Method 2: Basename matching (SSH remotes and dev containers only).
331			// These workspace paths live on a different machine or inside a container, so direct
332			// path comparison can never succeed and the folder basename is the only usable

336			if !isMatch && isRemoteURIRequiringBasenameMatch(workspaceURI) {

342						"workspaceID", workspaceID,

345						"remotePath", canonicalWorkspacePath,
346						"repoName", projectBasename)

352			// the workspace file URI rather than the folder URI. Check whether that workspace

354			if !isMatch && strings.HasSuffix(canonicalWorkspacePath, ".code-workspace") {
355				if codeWorkspaceContainsFolder(canonicalWorkspacePath, canonicalProjectPath) {
356					isMatch = true
357					slog.Debug("Matched workspace by .code-workspace folder reference",
358						"workspaceID", workspaceID,
359						"workspaceFile", canonicalWorkspacePath,
360						"targetFolder", canonicalProjectPath)

363

365			// opened directly from a folder listed in that workspace file.
366			if !isMatch {

368					if canonicalWorkspacePath == folderPath {

371							"workspaceID", workspaceID,
372							"folder", folderPath,

385				matches = append(matches, WorkspaceMatch{
386					ID:     workspaceID,
387					Path:   workspacePath,
388					DBPath: dbPath,
389					URI:    workspaceURI,

393					"workspaceID", workspaceID,
394					"workspaceURI", workspaceURI)
395			}
396		}
397	
398		if len(matches) == 0 {
399			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no workspace found for project path: %s", projectPath)
400		}
401	
402		slog.Debug("Found all matching workspaces",
403			"projectPath", projectPath,
404			"matchCount", len(matches))

409	// isRemoteURIRequiringBasenameMatch checks if a URI is a vscode-remote SSH, tunnel, or
410	// dev-container URI. Case-insensitive to stay consistent with parseVSCodeRemoteURI, which
411	// accepts uppercase authorities — this check gates basename matching, so a case mismatch
412	// would silently drop remote workspaces instead of just changing a log line.
413	//
414	// SSH, tunnel, and dev-container workspace paths all live outside the local filesystem (a
415	// remote machine or a container), so direct path comparison can never succeed for them and
416	// the folder basename is the only usable signal. WSL is deliberately excluded: WSL paths are
417	// reachable from the host via \\wsl.localhost\... / /mnt/wsl/..., so direct path matching
418	// already works there and doesn't need the (weaker, name-collision-prone) basename fallback.
419	func isRemoteURIRequiringBasenameMatch(uri string) bool {
420		lower := strings.ToLower(uri)
421		return strings.HasPrefix(lower, "vscode-remote://ssh-remote") ||
422			strings.HasPrefix(lower, "vscode-remote://tunnel") ||
423			strings.HasPrefix(lower, "vscode-remote://dev-container")
424	}

426	// FindProjectComposerIDs returns the composer IDs associated with the project, merging
427	// the two association sources that exist across Cursor versions:
428	//
429	//  1. Workspace-DB references (composer.composerData / workbench.panel keys) — Cursor 2
430	//     and early Cursor 3 record every conversation there.
431	//  2. The workspaceIdentifier embedded in each global composerData row — in Cursor
432	//     >= 3.12 the workspace DB no longer records conversations at all, and the global
433	//     composer.composerHeaders key is flushed lazily (often not until Cursor exits),
434	//     so this embedded field is the only association that updates live.
435	//
436	// A composer matches via source 2 when its workspace storage ID equals one of the
437	// project's matched workspace entries (covers remote workspaces, whose fsPath is not a
438	// local path), or when its fsPath resolves to the project path (covers workspace
439	// entries created after the caller resolved its workspace list — Cursor mints a fresh
440	// entry per literal path spelling, e.g. `~/source/...` vs `~/Source/...`).
441	// The full-DB lightweight scan this requires is deliberate: it is the only way to see
442	// the embedded workspaceIdentifier, and at watch cadence (>= 10s between checks) the
443	// cost of parsing the composer rows is acceptable. Callers that already hold the
444	// scanned map should use projectComposerIDs directly instead of scanning again.
445	func FindProjectComposerIDs(globalDbPath, projectPath string, workspaces []WorkspaceMatch) ([]string, error) {
446		composers, err := LoadAllComposerDataLightweight(globalDbPath)
447		if err != nil {
448			// The workspace-DB IDs may still be usable (older Cursor versions), so degrade
449			// to source 1 rather than failing the whole lookup.
450			slog.Warn("Failed to load global composer data for workspaceIdentifier matching", "error", err)
451			composers = nil
452		}
453		return projectComposerIDs(composers, projectPath, workspaces)
454	}
455	
456	// projectComposerIDs is the load-free core of FindProjectComposerIDs: it matches an
457	// already-scanned composer map against the project. Split out so callers that need the
458	// scanned map for their own purposes too (e.g. the watcher's seeding, which also reads
459	// the timestamps) don't scan the global database twice.
460	func projectComposerIDs(composers map[string]*ComposerData, projectPath string, workspaces []WorkspaceMatch) ([]string, error) {
461		ids, err := LoadComposerIDsFromAllWorkspaces(workspaces)
462		if err != nil {
463			return nil, err
464		}
465		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(ids))
466		for _, id := range ids {
467			seen[id] = true
468		}
469	
470		canonicalProject, err := normalizePathForComparison(projectPath)
471		if err != nil {
472			canonicalProject = projectPath
473		}
474		workspaceIDs := make(map[string]bool, len(workspaces))
475		for _, ws := range workspaces {
476			workspaceIDs[ws.ID] = true
477		}
478	
479		for composerID, composer := range composers {
480			if seen[composerID] || !composerBelongsToProject(composer, workspaceIDs, canonicalProject) {
481				continue
482			}
483			seen[composerID] = true
484			ids = append(ids, composerID)
485		}
486	
487		slog.Debug("Resolved project composer IDs", "count", len(ids), "projectPath", projectPath)
488		return ids, nil
489	}
490	
491	// composerBelongsToProject implements the embedded-workspaceIdentifier match of
492	// FindProjectComposerIDs (source 2 in its doc comment).
493	func composerBelongsToProject(composer *ComposerData, workspaceIDs map[string]bool, canonicalProject string) bool {
494		wi := composer.WorkspaceIdentifier
495		if wi == nil {
496			return false
497		}
498		if workspaceIDs[wi.ID] {
499			return true
500		}
501		if wi.URI == nil || wi.URI.FsPath == "" {
502			return false
503		}
504		canonicalComposer, err := normalizePathForComparison(wi.URI.FsPath)
505		if err != nil {
506			canonicalComposer = wi.URI.FsPath
507		}
508		return canonicalComposer == canonicalProject
509	}

511	// LoadComposerIDsFromAllWorkspaces loads and deduplicates composer IDs from all matching workspaces.
512	// This handles WSL environments where the same project may have multiple workspace entries.
513	// NOTE: this only covers Cursor 2 / early Cursor 3 — newer versions stopped recording
514	// conversations in the workspace DB entirely; use FindProjectComposerIDs for full coverage.
515	func LoadComposerIDsFromAllWorkspaces(workspaces []WorkspaceMatch) ([]string, error) {
516		seen := make(map[string]bool)
517		var allIDs []string
518	
519		for _, ws := range workspaces {
520			ids, err := LoadWorkspaceComposerIDs(ws.DBPath)
521			if err != nil {
522				slog.Warn("Failed to load composer IDs from workspace",
523					"workspaceID", ws.ID,
524					"error", err)
525				continue
526			}
527	
528			for _, id := range ids {
529				if !seen[id] {
530					seen[id] = true
531					allIDs = append(allIDs, id)
532				}
533			}
534		}
535	
536		return allIDs, nil
537	}

539	// ScanAllWorkspaceComposerPaths enumerates every Cursor IDE workspace directory and
540	// returns a map of composerID → project path (the OriginCwd for each session).
541	// When a composer appears in multiple workspaces (e.g. WSL/SSH setups), the first-seen
542	// workspace path is used. Workspaces that cannot be read are silently skipped so a
543	// single bad entry does not abort the whole enumeration.
544	func ScanAllWorkspaceComposerPaths() (map[string]string, error) {
545		workspaceStoragePath, err := GetWorkspaceStoragePath()
546		if err != nil {
547			// No workspace storage directory means Cursor IDE has never been opened.
548			slog.Debug("Workspace storage not found, no Cursor IDE sessions", "error", err)
549			return map[string]string{}, nil
550		}
551		return scanWorkspaceDirForComposerPaths(workspaceStoragePath)
552	}
553	
554	// scanWorkspaceDirForComposerPaths does the actual directory walk for
555	// ScanAllWorkspaceComposerPaths. It is a separate function so tests can call it
556	// directly with a temp directory rather than relying on the live Cursor installation.
557	func scanWorkspaceDirForComposerPaths(workspaceStoragePath string) (map[string]string, error) {
558		entries, err := os.ReadDir(workspaceStoragePath)
559		if err != nil {
560			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read workspace storage: %w", err)
561		}
562	
563		composerToPath := make(map[string]string)
564		for _, entry := range entries {
565			if !entry.IsDir() {
566				continue
567			}
568	
569			workspacePath := filepath.Join(workspaceStoragePath, entry.Name())
570			dbPath := filepath.Join(workspacePath, "state.vscdb")
571			if _, statErr := os.Stat(dbPath); statErr != nil {
572				continue // workspace directory has no database yet
573			}
574	
575			workspaceJSON, jsonErr := readWorkspaceJSON(filepath.Join(workspacePath, "workspace.json"))
576			if jsonErr != nil {
577				slog.Debug("Skipping workspace (no valid workspace.json)",
578					"workspace", entry.Name(), "error", jsonErr)
579				continue
580			}
581	
582			workspaceURI := workspaceJSON.Workspace
583			if workspaceURI == "" {
584				workspaceURI = workspaceJSON.Folder
585			}
586			if workspaceURI == "" {
587				continue
588			}
589	
590			projectPath, uriErr := uriToPath(workspaceURI)
591			if uriErr != nil {
592				slog.Debug("Skipping workspace (unresolvable URI)",
593					"workspace", entry.Name(), "uri", workspaceURI, "error", uriErr)
594				continue
595			}
596	
597			composerIDs, idsErr := LoadWorkspaceComposerIDs(dbPath)
598			if idsErr != nil {
599				slog.Warn("Failed to load composer IDs from workspace",
600					"workspace", entry.Name(), "error", idsErr)
601				continue
602			}
603	
604			for _, id := range composerIDs {
605				if _, exists := composerToPath[id]; !exists {
606					// First-seen workspace path wins; a composer scoped to multiple workspaces
607					// (WSL/SSH setups) is attributed to whichever workspace is encountered first.
608					composerToPath[id] = projectPath
609				}
610			}
611		}
612	
613		slog.Debug("Scanned all workspaces for composer paths", "composerCount", len(composerToPath))
614		return composerToPath, nil
615	}

617	// readWorkspaceJSON reads and parses a workspace.json file
618	func readWorkspaceJSON(path string) (*WorkspaceJSON, error) {
619		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
620		if err != nil {
621			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read workspace.json: %w", err)
622		}
623	
624		var workspace WorkspaceJSON
625		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &workspace); err != nil {
626			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse workspace.json: %w", err)
627		}
628	
629		return &workspace, nil
630	}

632	// pathToFileURI converts an absolute filesystem path to a file:// URI.
633	// Cursor stores workspaceIdentifier.uri.external in percent-encoded form (e.g.
634	// spaces as %20), so raw string concatenation would produce a URI that doesn't
635	// match what Cursor writes for paths containing reserved characters, which can
636	// mis-associate reconstructed sessions with their workspace.
637	func pathToFileURI(path string) string {
638		u := url.URL{Scheme: "file", Path: path}
639		return u.String()
640	}
641	
642	// uriToPath converts a workspace URI to a local file path. The
643	// vscode-remote:// forms (wsl+distro, ssh-remote+config, tunnel+host) are
644	// Cursor/VS Code specific and handled here; plain file:// URIs — including the
645	// WSL and Windows drive-letter/UNC shapes — are converted by the shared
646	// spi.FileURIToPath so every provider translates them identically.
647	func uriToPath(uri string) (string, error) {
648		// Handle vscode-remote:// URIs before url.Parse because Go's URL parser
649		// rejects percent-encoded characters like %2B in the host component
650		// (e.g., vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/user/project)
651		if strings.HasPrefix(uri, "vscode-remote://") {
652			return parseVSCodeRemoteURI(uri)
653		}
654		return spi.FileURIToPath(uri)
655	}
