657	// collectCodeWorkspaceFolders reads a .code-workspace JSON file and returns the
658	// canonicalized paths of every folder it lists. Used when the project path passed
659	// in is itself a .code-workspace file, so workspace entries opened directly from
660	// one of its folders can also be matched (Method 4 in FindAllWorkspacesForProject).
661	func collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(workspaceFilePath string) []string {
662		data, err := os.ReadFile(workspaceFilePath)
663		if err != nil {
664			slog.Debug("collectCodeWorkspaceFolders: failed to read workspace file",
665				"path", workspaceFilePath, "error", err)
666			return nil
667		}
668	
669		var workspace struct {
670			Folders []struct {
671				Path string `json:"path"`
672			} `json:"folders"`
673		}
674		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &workspace); err != nil {
675			slog.Debug("collectCodeWorkspaceFolders: failed to parse workspace file",
676				"path", workspaceFilePath, "error", err)
677			return nil
678		}
679	
680		workspaceDir := filepath.Dir(workspaceFilePath)
681		var folders []string
682		for _, folder := range workspace.Folders {
683			if folder.Path == "" {
684				continue
685			}
686	
687			// Resolve relative paths against the workspace file's directory.
688			var resolved string
689			if filepath.IsAbs(folder.Path) {
690				resolved = folder.Path
691			} else {
692				resolved = filepath.Join(workspaceDir, folder.Path)
693			}
694	
695			canonical, err := normalizePathForComparison(resolved)
696			if err != nil {
697				canonical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
698			}
699			folders = append(folders, canonical)
700		}
701	
702		return folders
703	}

705	// codeWorkspaceContainsFolder checks whether any folder entry in a .code-workspace
706	// JSON file resolves to canonicalFolder. This is used to find workspaces that were
707	// opened via a .code-workspace file referencing the target folder.
708	func codeWorkspaceContainsFolder(workspaceFilePath, canonicalFolder string) bool {
709		for _, folder := range collectCodeWorkspaceFolders(workspaceFilePath) {
710			if folder == canonicalFolder {
711				return true
712			}
713		}
714		return false
715	}

717	// parseVSCodeRemoteURI extracts the filesystem path from a vscode-remote:// URI.
718	// Handles three types of remote URIs:
719	// 1. WSL: vscode-remote://wsl%2B{distro}/{path} - path is the WSL filesystem path
720	// 2. SSH: vscode-remote://ssh-remote%2B{config-hex}/{path} - path is the remote filesystem path
721	// 3. Tunnel: vscode-remote://tunnel%2B{host}/{path} - path is the remote filesystem path
722	// Go's url.Parse rejects %2B in the host component, so we parse manually.
723	func parseVSCodeRemoteURI(uri string) (string, error) {
724		// Strip scheme prefix: "vscode-remote://"
725		remainder := strings.TrimPrefix(uri, "vscode-remote://")
726	
727		// Split host from path at the first unencoded slash after the host
728		// The host is percent-encoded (e.g., "wsl%2Bubuntu" or "ssh-remote%2B{config-hex}")
729		slashIdx := strings.Index(remainder, "/")
730		if slashIdx < 0 {
731			return "", fmt.Errorf("malformed vscode-remote URI (no path): %s", uri)
732		}
733	
734		host := remainder[:slashIdx]
735		pathPart := remainder[slashIdx:]
736	
737		// Decode the host to determine remote type
738		decodedHost, err := url.PathUnescape(host)
739		if err != nil {
740			decodedHost = host
741		}
742	
743		hostLower := strings.ToLower(decodedHost)
744	
745		// Check if it's a supported remote type: each host is either bare ("wsl") or
746		// carries a "+{config}" suffix ("wsl+ubuntu", "ssh-remote+{config-hex}").
747		supportedHosts := []string{"wsl", "ssh-remote", "tunnel", "dev-container"}
748		supported := false
749		for _, host := range supportedHosts {
750			if hostLower == host || strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, host+"+") {
751				supported = true
752				break
753			}
754		}
755		if !supported {
756			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported vscode-remote host %q: %s", decodedHost, uri)
757		}
758	
759		// Decode the path portion
760		path, err := url.PathUnescape(pathPart)
761		if err != nil {
762			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode vscode-remote URI path: %w", err)
763		}
764	
765		// Log the conversion with appropriate context
766		switch {
767		case strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, "ssh-remote"):
768			slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote SSH URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
769		case strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, "tunnel"):
770			slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote tunnel URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
771		case strings.HasPrefix(hostLower, "dev-container"):
772			slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote dev container URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
773		default:
774			slog.Debug("Converted vscode-remote WSL URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path)
775		}
776	
777		return path, nil
778	}
779

186			for _, key := range keys {
187				valueStr := fmt.Sprintf("%v", tool.Input[key])
188				if strings.Contains(valueStr, "\n") {
189					fence := codeFence(valueStr)
190					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s:\n\n%s\n%s\n%s\n\n", key, fence, valueStr, fence)
191				} else {
192					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s: `%s`\n", key, valueStr)
193				}
194			}
195		}
196	
197		// Result from the output map (BuildToolInfoFromInvocation stores it under "result").
198		if result, ok := tool.Output["result"].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(result) != "" {
199			capped := capRunes(result, toolResultCap)
200			fence := codeFence(capped)
201			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n**Result:**\n\n%s\n%s\n%s\n", fence, capped, fence)
202		}
203	
204		return b.String()
205	}
206	
207	// codeFence returns a backtick fence long enough to safely wrap s: one backtick more
208	// than the longest backtick run inside it (a value containing ``` would otherwise
209	// terminate a plain three-backtick fence early), never shorter than the standard three.
210	func codeFence(s string) string {
211		longest, run := 0, 0
212		for _, r := range s {
213			if r == '`' {
214				run++
215				if run > longest {
216					longest = run
217				}
218			} else {
219				run = 0
220			}
221		}
222		size := longest + 1
223		if size < 3 {
224			size = 3
225		}
226		return strings.Repeat("`", size)
227	}
228	
229	// capRunes truncates s to at most max runes, marking the cut. Rune-based so a cap
230	// never splits a multi-byte character. Scans rune boundaries instead of converting
231	// to []rune, which would allocate O(len(s)) for exactly the oversized tool results
232	// this cap protects against.
233	func capRunes(s string, max int) string {
234		if len(s) <= max {
235			return s // fast path: byte length bounds rune length
236		}
237		count := 0
238		for i := range s {
239			if count == max {
240				return s[:i] + "\n… (output truncated)"
241			}
242			count++
243		}
244		return s // more bytes than max but fewer runes (multi-byte characters)
245	}
246	
247	// GenerateSlug creates a filesystem-safe slug from the composer title, name, or
248	// first request message, using the spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage convention
249	// shared by every other provider (word cap, punctuation as separators, markdown
250	// heading stripping) so slugs stay consistent and bounded across code paths.
251	func GenerateSlug(composer VSCodeComposer) string {
252		if composer.CustomTitle != "" {
253			if slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(composer.CustomTitle); slug != "" {
254				return slug
255			}
256		}
257		if composer.Name != "" {
258			if slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(composer.Name); slug != "" {
259				return slug
260			}
261		}
262	
263		// Fall back to first request message
264		if len(composer.Requests) > 0 {
265			if slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(composer.Requests[0].Message.Text); slug != "" {
266				return slug
267			}
268		}
269	
270		return "untitled"
271	}
272	
273	// FormatTimestamp converts Unix timestamp (ms) to ISO 8601
274	func FormatTimestamp(unixMs int64) string {
275		t := time.Unix(0, unixMs*int64(time.Millisecond))
276		return t.Format(time.RFC3339)
277	}

149	// ParseResponsesForTools extracts tool invocations from response array
150	func ParseResponsesForTools(responses []json.RawMessage, metadata VSCodeResultMetadata, modelID string) []schema.Message {
151		var toolMessages []schema.Message
152	
153		// Build ordered sequence of tool calls from metadata
154		toolCallSequence := BuildToolCallSequence(metadata)
155	
156		// Track sequence index for matching
157		sequenceIndex := 0
158	
159		// Process each response
160		for _, rawResp := range responses {
161			// Parse "kind" field first
162			kind, err := ParseResponseKind(rawResp)
163			if err != nil {
164				slog.Debug("Failed to parse response kind", "error", err)
165				continue
166			}
167	
168			switch kind {
169			case "toolInvocationSerialized":
170				var invocation VSCodeToolInvocationResponse
171				if err := json.Unmarshal(rawResp, &invocation); err != nil {
172					slog.Debug("Failed to parse tool invocation", "error", err)
173					continue
174				}
175	
176				// Match by sequence: get the next tool call from the ordered list
177				if sequenceIndex >= len(toolCallSequence) {
178					slog.Debug("Tool invocation has no matching tool call in sequence",
179						"sequenceIndex", sequenceIndex,
180						"totalToolCalls", len(toolCallSequence),
181						"toolCallId", invocation.ToolCallID)
182					continue
183				}
184	
185				toolCall := toolCallSequence[sequenceIndex]
186				sequenceIndex++
187	
188				// Hidden tools still occupy a slot in metadata's tool call sequence,
189				// so consume the slot above but don't emit a message for them.
190				if invocation.Presentation == "hidden" {
191					continue
192				}
193	
194				slog.Debug("Matched tool by sequence",
195					"sequenceIndex", sequenceIndex-1,
196					"toolName", toolCall.Name,
197					"invocationId", invocation.ToolCallID,
198					"metadataId", toolCall.ID)
199	
200				// Build tool info using the matched tool call
201				toolInfo := BuildToolInfoFromInvocation(invocation, toolCall, metadata.ToolCallResults)
202				if toolInfo != nil {
203					toolMsg := schema.Message{
204						Role:  schema.RoleAgent,
205						Model: modelID,
206						Tool:  toolInfo,
207					}
208					toolMessages = append(toolMessages, toolMsg)
209				}
210	
211			// Handle other response types (textEditGroup, codeblockUri, etc.)
212			// Can defer detailed handling to phase 2
213			case "textEditGroup":
214				slog.Debug("Skipping textEditGroup response (phase 2)", "kind", kind)
215			case "codeblockUri":
216				slog.Debug("Skipping codeblockUri response (phase 2)", "kind", kind)
217			case "confirmation":
218				slog.Debug("Skipping confirmation response (phase 2)", "kind", kind)
219			case "inlineReference":
220				slog.Debug("Skipping inlineReference response (phase 2)", "kind", kind)
221			default:
222				slog.Debug("Unknown response kind", "kind", kind)
223			}
224		}
225	
226		return toolMessages
227	}

229	// BuildToolInfoFromInvocation creates ToolInfo from VS Code invocation + tool call
230	// Uses sequence-based matching: toolCall is passed directly instead of looked up by ID
231	func BuildToolInfoFromInvocation(
232		invocation VSCodeToolInvocationResponse,
233		toolCall VSCodeToolCallInfo,
234		toolResults map[string]VSCodeToolCallResult,
235	) *schema.ToolInfo {
236		toolInfo := &schema.ToolInfo{
237			Name:  toolCall.Name,
238			Type:  MapToolType(toolCall.Name),
239			UseID: invocation.ToolCallID,
240		}
241	
242		// Parse arguments if present
243		if toolCall.Arguments != "" {
244			var args map[string]any
245			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(toolCall.Arguments), &args); err == nil {
246				toolInfo.Input = args
247			}
248		}
249	
250		// Add output from results map. metadata.toolCallResults is keyed by the
251		// same OpenAI-style IDs as toolCallRounds (verified on real session files),
252		// not by the invocation's VS Code UUID — so look up with the matched
253		// toolCall's ID.
254		if result, ok := toolResults[toolCall.ID]; ok {
255			output := make(map[string]any)
256			if len(result.Content) > 0 {
257				var contentParts []string
258				for _, content := range result.Content {
259					// Value can be string or object - convert to string
260					valueStr := valueToString(content.Value)
261					if valueStr != "" {
262						contentParts = append(contentParts, valueStr)
263					}
264				}
265				if len(contentParts) > 0 {
266					output["result"] = strings.Join(contentParts, "\n")
267				}
268			}
269			if len(output) > 0 {
270				toolInfo.Output = output
271			}
272		}
273	
274		// Pre-render Summary/FormattedMarkdown: cross-agent resume flattens tool calls
275		// from these fields only, so without them the tool's payload (e.g. a written
276		// file's content) would collapse to a bare tool name in the resumed session.
277		// The summary matches the markdown generator's default, so archival markdown
278		// keeps its familiar <summary> line.
279		summary := fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s**", toolInfo.Name)
280		toolInfo.Summary = &summary
281		if formatted := FormatToolMarkdown(toolInfo); formatted != "" {
282			toolInfo.FormattedMarkdown = &formatted
283		}
284	
285		return toolInfo
286	}

292		}

347	// createSyntheticRequestsFromEditingState creates synthetic request blocks from editing operations
348	// when there are no chat requests but file operations exist
349	func createSyntheticRequestsFromEditingState(composer VSCodeComposer, state *VSCodeStateFile) []VSCodeRequestBlock {
350		if state == nil {
351			return nil
352		}
353	
354		// Detect state version
355		version := state.Version
356		if version == 0 {
357			version = 1 // Default to version 1
358		}
359	
360		slog.Debug("Processing editing state", "version", version, "sessionId", composer.SessionID)
361	
362		var fileOperationSummaries []string
363	
364		if version >= 2 {
365			// Version 2: Extract from timeline.operations
366			fileOperationSummaries = extractOperationsFromV2State(state)
367			slog.Debug("Extracted operations from v2 state", "count", len(fileOperationSummaries))
368		} else {
369			// Version 1: Extract from recentSnapshot/pendingSnapshot
370			fileOperationSummaries = extractOperationsFromV1State(state)
371			slog.Debug("Extracted operations from v1 state", "count", len(fileOperationSummaries))
372		}
373	
374		// Fallback: If we couldn't extract operations but state exists, show generic message
375		if len(fileOperationSummaries) == 0 {
376			// Check if there's any indication of editing activity
377			hasRecentSnapshot := state.RecentSnapshot != nil
378			hasPendingSnapshot := state.PendingSnapshot != nil
379			hasTimeline := state.Timeline != nil
380	
381			if !hasRecentSnapshot && !hasPendingSnapshot && !hasTimeline {
382				return nil // No editing activity detected
383			}
384	
385			fileOperationSummaries = []string{"File editing session (details not available)"}
386		}
387	
388		// Get user input text if available (from customTitle)
389		userText := composer.CustomTitle
390		if userText == "" {
391			userText = "File editing session"
392		}
393	
394		// Build synthetic text for assistant message
395		var assistantText string
396		if len(fileOperationSummaries) > 0 {
397			plural := ""
398			if len(fileOperationSummaries) > 1 {
399				plural = "s"
400			}
401			assistantText = fmt.Sprintf("Performed %d file operation%s:\n\n%s",
402				len(fileOperationSummaries),
403				plural,
404				strings.Join(fileOperationSummaries, "\n"))
405		} else {
406			assistantText = "Performed file editing operations"
407		}
408	
409		// Create synthetic request block
410		syntheticRequest := VSCodeRequestBlock{
411			RequestID: composer.SessionID + "-synthetic",
412			Timestamp: composer.CreationDate,
413			Message: VSCodeMessage{
414				Text: userText,
415			},
416			Response: []json.RawMessage{},
417			Result: VSCodeResult{
418				Metadata: VSCodeResultMetadata{
419					Messages: []VSCodeMetadataMessage{
420						{
421							Role:    "assistant",
422							Content: assistantText,
423						},
424					},
425				},
426			},
427			ModelID: composer.ResponderUsername,
428		}
429	
430		return []VSCodeRequestBlock{syntheticRequest}
431	}

433	// extractOperationsFromV2State extracts file operations from version 2 state format (timeline.operations)
434	func extractOperationsFromV2State(state *VSCodeStateFile) []string {
435		if state.Timeline == nil || len(state.Timeline.Operations) == 0 {
436			return nil
437		}
438	
439		var summaries []string
440		for _, op := range state.Timeline.Operations {
441			var fileName string
442			if op.URI != nil {
443				// Extract file name from URI
444				path := op.URI.FSPath
445				if path == "" {
446					path = op.URI.Path
447				}
448				if path != "" {
449					parts := strings.Split(path, "/")
450					fileName = parts[len(parts)-1]
451				} else {
452					fileName = "unknown file"
453				}
454			} else {
455				fileName = "unknown file"
456			}
457	
458			switch op.Type {
459			case "create":
460				summaries = append(summaries, fmt.Sprintf("Created file: `%s`", fileName))
461			case "textEdit":
462				editCount := len(op.Edits)
463				if editCount == 0 {
464					editCount = 1
465				}
466				plural := ""
467				if editCount > 1 {
468					plural = "s"
469				}
470				summaries = append(summaries, fmt.Sprintf("Edited `%s` (%d edit%s)", fileName, editCount, plural))
471			case "delete":
472				summaries = append(summaries, fmt.Sprintf("Deleted file: `%s`", fileName))
473			default:
474				summaries = append(summaries, fmt.Sprintf("%s: `%s`", op.Type, fileName))
475			}
476		}
477	
478		return summaries
479	}

481	// extractOperationsFromV1State extracts file operations from version 1 state format (recentSnapshot/pendingSnapshot)
482	func extractOperationsFromV1State(state *VSCodeStateFile) []string {
483		filesSummary := make(map[string]bool)
484	
485		// Try recentSnapshot (can be array or object)
486		if state.RecentSnapshot != nil {
487			entries := extractEntriesFromSnapshot(state.RecentSnapshot)
488			for _, entry := range entries {
489				if fileName := extractFileNameFromEntry(entry); fileName != "" {
490					filesSummary[fmt.Sprintf("Modified `%s`", fileName)] = true
491				}
492			}
493		}
494	
495		// Try pendingSnapshot
496		if state.PendingSnapshot != nil {
497			entries := extractEntriesFromSnapshot(state.PendingSnapshot)
498			for _, entry := range entries {
499				if fileName := extractFileNameFromEntry(entry); fileName != "" {
500					filesSummary[fmt.Sprintf("Modified `%s`", fileName)] = true
501				}
502			}
503		}
504	
505		// Convert map to slice
506		var summaries []string
507		for summary := range filesSummary {
508			summaries = append(summaries, summary)
509		}
510	
511		return summaries
512	}

514	// extractEntriesFromSnapshot extracts entries from a snapshot (handles both array and object formats)
515	func extractEntriesFromSnapshot(snapshot any) []VSCodeStopEntry {
516		if snapshot == nil {
517			return nil
518		}
519	
520		var entries []VSCodeStopEntry
521	
522		// Try to unmarshal as VSCodeStop object
523		if stopMap, ok := snapshot.(map[string]any); ok {
524			if entriesData, ok := stopMap["entries"].([]any); ok {
525				for _, entryData := range entriesData {
526					if entryMap, ok := entryData.(map[string]any); ok {
527						if resource, ok := entryMap["resource"].(string); ok {
528							entries = append(entries, VSCodeStopEntry{Resource: resource})
529						}
530					}
531				}
532				return entries
533			}
534		}
535	
536		// Try to unmarshal as array of VSCodeStop objects
537		if stopsArray, ok := snapshot.([]any); ok {
538			for _, stopData := range stopsArray {
539				if stopMap, ok := stopData.(map[string]any); ok {
540					if entriesData, ok := stopMap["entries"].([]any); ok {
541						for _, entryData := range entriesData {
542							if entryMap, ok := entryData.(map[string]any); ok {
543								if resource, ok := entryMap["resource"].(string); ok {
544									entries = append(entries, VSCodeStopEntry{Resource: resource})
545								}
546							}
547						}
548					}
549				}
550			}
551		}
552	
553		return entries
554	}

556	// extractFileNameFromEntry extracts the file name from an entry object
557	func extractFileNameFromEntry(entry VSCodeStopEntry) string {
558		if entry.Resource == "" {
559			return ""
560		}
561	
562		// Handle both URI strings and file paths
563		resource := entry.Resource
564		parts := strings.Split(resource, "/")
565		if len(parts) > 0 {
566			return parts[len(parts)-1]
567		}
568	
569		return resource
570	}

25	func OpenDatabase(dbPath string) (*sql.DB, error) {

175	// LoadComposerDataBatch loads multiple composers and their bubbles from the global database.
176	// Queries are chunked to composerBatchSize to stay within SQLite's expression-tree depth limit.
177	func LoadComposerDataBatch(globalDbPath string, composerIDs []string) (map[string]*ComposerData, error) {
178		if len(composerIDs) == 0 {
179			return map[string]*ComposerData{}, nil
180		}
181	
182		db, err := OpenDatabase(globalDbPath)
183		if err != nil {
184			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open global database: %w", err)
185		}
186		defer func() {
187			if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
188				slog.Warn("Failed to close global database", "error", closeErr)
189			}
190		}()
191	
192		composers := make(map[string]*ComposerData)
193		bubbles := make(map[string]map[string]*ComposerConversation)
194	
195		for i := 0; i < len(composerIDs); i += composerBatchSize {
196			end := min(i+composerBatchSize, len(composerIDs))
197			chunk := composerIDs[i:end]
198			if err := loadComposerChunk(db, chunk, composers, bubbles); err != nil {
199				return nil, err
200			}
201		}
202	
203		assembleComposerConversations(composers, bubbles)
204	
205		slog.Debug("Loaded composers from global database", "composerCount", len(composers))
206		return composers, nil
207	}

209	// loadComposerChunk runs one bounded query for a slice of composer IDs and merges
210	// the results into the caller-provided composers and bubbles maps.
211	func loadComposerChunk(db *sql.DB, composerIDs []string, composers map[string]*ComposerData, bubbles map[string]map[string]*ComposerConversation) error {
212		placeholders := make([]string, len(composerIDs))
213		likeConditions := make([]string, len(composerIDs))
214		params := make([]interface{}, 0, len(composerIDs)*2)
215	
216		for i, id := range composerIDs {
217			placeholders[i] = "?"
218			likeConditions[i] = "key LIKE ?"
219			params = append(params, "composerData:"+id)
220		}
221		for _, id := range composerIDs {
222			params = append(params, "bubbleId:"+id+":%")
223		}
224	
225		query := fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT key, value FROM cursorDiskKV
226			WHERE value IS NOT NULL AND (
227				key IN (%s)
228				OR (%s)
229			)`,
230			strings.Join(placeholders, ","),
231			strings.Join(likeConditions, " OR "))
232	
233		slog.Debug("Executing composer chunk query", "composerCount", len(composerIDs))
234	
235		rows, err := db.Query(query, params...)
236		if err != nil {
237			return fmt.Errorf("failed to query composer chunk: %w", err)
238		}
239		defer func() {
240			if closeErr := rows.Close(); closeErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("Failed to close chunk query rows", "error", closeErr)
242			}
243		}()
244	
245		for rows.Next() {
246			var key, valueJSON string
247			if err := rows.Scan(&key, &valueJSON); err != nil {
248				slog.Warn("Failed to scan row", "error", err)
249				continue
250			}
251	
252			if strings.HasPrefix(key, "composerData:") {
253				composerID := strings.TrimPrefix(key, "composerData:")
254				var composer ComposerData
255				if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(valueJSON), &composer); err != nil {
256					slog.Warn("Failed to parse composer data", "composerID", composerID, "error", err)
257					continue
258				}
259				composers[composerID] = &composer
260				slog.Debug("Loaded composer", "composerID", composerID, "name", composer.Name)
261			} else if strings.HasPrefix(key, "bubbleId:") {
262				parts := strings.SplitN(key, ":", 3)
263				if len(parts) != 3 {
264					slog.Warn("Invalid bubble key format", "key", key)
265					continue
266				}
267				composerID, bubbleID := parts[1], parts[2]
268				var bubble ComposerConversation
269				if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(valueJSON), &bubble); err != nil {
270					slog.Warn("Failed to parse bubble data", "composerID", composerID, "bubbleID", bubbleID, "error", err)
271					continue
272				}
273				if bubbles[composerID] == nil {
274					bubbles[composerID] = make(map[string]*ComposerConversation)
275				}
276				bubbles[composerID][bubbleID] = &bubble
277				slog.Debug("Loaded bubble", "composerID", composerID, "bubbleID", bubbleID, "type", bubble.Type)
278			}
279		}
280		return rows.Err()
281	}

283	// assembleComposerConversations merges the per-bubble map into each composer's Conversation slice.
284	func assembleComposerConversations(composers map[string]*ComposerData, bubbles map[string]map[string]*ComposerConversation) {
285		for composerID, composer := range composers {
286			composerBubbles, exists := bubbles[composerID]
287			if !exists {
288				continue
289			}
290			if len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly) > 0 {
291				composer.Conversation = make([]ComposerConversation, 0, len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly))
292				for _, header := range composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly {
293					if bubble, found := composerBubbles[header.BubbleID]; found {
294						composer.Conversation = append(composer.Conversation, *bubble)
295					}
296				}
297			} else {
298				// Cursor 2 inline format: merge full bubble data (thinking, timing, etc.) into the
299				// conversation array that was already embedded in the composerData row.
300				for i := range composer.Conversation {
301					bubbleID := composer.Conversation[i].BubbleID
302					fullBubble, found := composerBubbles[bubbleID]
303					if !found {
304						continue
305					}
306					if fullBubble.Thinking != nil {
307						composer.Conversation[i].Thinking = fullBubble.Thinking
308					}
309					if fullBubble.Text != "" {
310						composer.Conversation[i].Text = fullBubble.Text
311					}
312					if fullBubble.TimingInfo != nil {
313						composer.Conversation[i].TimingInfo = fullBubble.TimingInfo
314					}
315					if fullBubble.ModelInfo != nil {
316						composer.Conversation[i].ModelInfo = fullBubble.ModelInfo
317					}
318					if fullBubble.ToolFormerData != nil {
319						composer.Conversation[i].ToolFormerData = fullBubble.ToolFormerData
320					}
321				}
322			}
323		}
324	}

326	// OpenDatabaseReadWrite opens a SQLite database in read-write mode with controlled
327	// connection pooling. It calls spi.EnsureWALMode before returning so the database is
328	// in WAL mode when the caller starts writing.
329	func OpenDatabaseReadWrite(dbPath string) (*sql.DB, error) {
330		if err := spi.EnsureWALMode(dbPath); err != nil {
331			slog.Warn("Failed to ensure WAL mode before opening read-write database", "error", err)
332		}
333		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dbPath+"?"+spi.BusyTimeoutPragma)
334		if err != nil {
335			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open database for writing: %w", err)
336		}
337		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
338		db.SetMaxIdleConns(1)
339		db.SetConnMaxLifetime(30 * time.Second)
340		return db, nil
341	}

343	// InsertComposerSession writes a reconstructed composer session into the global state.vscdb
344	// within a single transaction: one composerData:* row for the metadata and one
345	// bubbleId:*:* row per conversation turn. An existing row with the same key is replaced
346	// so re-runs of the same session ID are idempotent.
347	// composerJSON is the raw JSON to store verbatim; the caller is responsible for serializing
348	// all required Cursor fields (see ReconstructSession for the full set).
349	func InsertComposerSession(db *sql.DB, composerID string, composerJSON []byte, bubbles []ComposerConversation) error {
350		tx, err := db.Begin()
351		if err != nil {
352			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start transaction: %w", err)
353		}
354		// Rollback after a successful Commit is a documented no-op (ErrTxDone), so it can
355		// be deferred unconditionally instead of tracking a separate error flag.
356		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
357	
358		if _, err := tx.Exec(
359			"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO cursorDiskKV (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
360			"composerData:"+composerID, string(composerJSON),
361		); err != nil {
362			return fmt.Errorf("failed to insert composer data: %w", err)
363		}
364	
365		for i := range bubbles {
366			bubbleJSON, err := json.Marshal(&bubbles[i])
367			if err != nil {
368				return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal bubble %s: %w", bubbles[i].BubbleID, err)
369			}
370			key := "bubbleId:" + composerID + ":" + bubbles[i].BubbleID
371			if _, err := tx.Exec(
372				"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO cursorDiskKV (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
373				key, string(bubbleJSON),
374			); err != nil {
375				return fmt.Errorf("failed to insert bubble %s: %w", bubbles[i].BubbleID, err)
376			}
377		}
378	
379		return tx.Commit()
380	}

589	func insertComposerHeaderRow(db *sql.DB, meta ComposerHeadMeta, headJSON []byte) error {
590		var tableName string

602				(composerId, workspaceId, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt, isArchived, isSubagent, recency, checkpointAt, value)
603				VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 0, ?, ?, ?)`,
604			meta.ComposerID, meta.WorkspaceID, meta.CreatedAt, meta.LastUpdatedAt,

611		return nil
612	}

614	// glassProjectsKey and glassMembershipKey are the ItemTable keys behind the Agent
615	// sidebar in Cursor >= 3.12 ("glass" is Cursor's name for that UI layer): the first
616	// holds project entities keyed by workspace, the second maps composerID -> projectID.
617	// Newer Cursors build the sidebar from these — composer.composerHeaders is no longer
618	// read for it — so a reconstructed session must be registered here or it stays
619	// invisible. Older Cursor versions ignore both keys, so writing them is always safe.
620	const (
621		glassProjectsKey   = "glass.localAgentProjects.v1"
622		glassMembershipKey = "glass.localAgentProjectMembership.v1"
623	)
624	
625	// glassProject mirrors the fields of a glass.localAgentProjects.v1 entry needed for
626	// matching; existing entries are carried through verbatim as raw JSON when rewritten.
627	type glassProject struct {
628		ID        string `json:"id"`
629		Workspace struct {
630			ID  string `json:"id"`
631			URI struct {
632				FsPath string `json:"fsPath"`
633			} `json:"uri"`
634		} `json:"workspace"`

637	// RegisterGlassProjectMembership adds a composer to the project-membership map that
638	// backs the Agent sidebar in Cursor >= 3.12, creating a project entry for the workspace
639	// when none exists yet (matched by workspace storage ID, then by canonical fsPath).
640	//
641	// Caveat: like every ItemTable write made while Cursor is running, a running instance
642	// can flush its own in-memory copy of these keys over ours. The resume flow already
643	// tells the user to restart Cursor; registration is reliable when Cursor is not
644	// running or is restarted afterwards.
645	func RegisterGlassProjectMembership(globalDbPath, composerID, workspaceID, workspaceRoot string) error {
646		db, err := OpenDatabaseReadWrite(globalDbPath)
647		if err != nil {
648			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open global database for glass registration: %w", err)
649		}
650		defer func() {
651			if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
652				slog.Warn("Failed to close global database after glass registration", "error", closeErr)
653			}
654		}()
655	
656		// Resolve (or create) the project entry for this workspace. Unknown fields of
657		// existing entries are preserved by keeping them as raw JSON.
658		var rawProjects []json.RawMessage
659		var projectsRaw string
660		err = db.QueryRow("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = ?", glassProjectsKey).Scan(&projectsRaw)
661		if err != nil && err != sql.ErrNoRows {
662			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read %s: %w", glassProjectsKey, err)
663		}
664		if projectsRaw != "" {
665			if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(projectsRaw), &rawProjects); jsonErr != nil {
666				slog.Warn("Failed to parse glass projects, starting fresh", "error", jsonErr)
667				rawProjects = nil
668			}
669		}
670	
671		canonicalRoot, cErr := normalizePathForComparison(workspaceRoot)
672		if cErr != nil {
673			canonicalRoot = workspaceRoot
674		}
675		projectID := ""
676		for _, entry := range rawProjects {
677			var project glassProject
678			if json.Unmarshal(entry, &project) != nil {
679				continue
680			}
681			if project.Workspace.ID == workspaceID {
682				projectID = project.ID
683				break
684			}
685			if project.Workspace.URI.FsPath != "" {
686				if canonical, pErr := normalizePathForComparison(project.Workspace.URI.FsPath); pErr == nil && canonical == canonicalRoot {
687					projectID = project.ID
688					break
689				}
690			}
691		}
692	
693		if projectID == "" {
694			projectID = uuid.NewString()
695			nowMs := time.Now().UnixMilli()
696			// "New Project" mirrors the placeholder name Cursor writes for its own
697			// freshly-created project entries.
698			newEntry := map[string]interface{}{
699				"id":   projectID,
700				"name": "New Project",
701				"workspace": map[string]interface{}{
702					"id": workspaceID,
703					"uri": map[string]interface{}{
704						"$mid":     1,
705						"fsPath":   workspaceRoot,
706						"external": pathToFileURI(workspaceRoot),
707						"path":     workspaceRoot,
708						"scheme":   "file",
709					},
710				},
711				"createdAt":     nowMs,
712				"lastUpdatedAt": nowMs,
713				"isArchived":    false,
714			}
715			entryJSON, mErr := json.Marshal(newEntry)
716			if mErr != nil {
717				return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal glass project entry: %w", mErr)
718			}
719			rawProjects = append(rawProjects, entryJSON)
720			projectsJSON, mErr := json.Marshal(rawProjects)
721			if mErr != nil {
722				return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal glass projects: %w", mErr)
723			}
724			if _, execErr := db.Exec(
725				"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO ItemTable (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
726				glassProjectsKey, string(projectsJSON),
727			); execErr != nil {
728				return fmt.Errorf("failed to write %s: %w", glassProjectsKey, execErr)
729			}
730			slog.Debug("Created glass project entry for workspace",
731				"projectID", projectID, "workspaceID", workspaceID)
732		}
733	
734		// Add the composer -> project mapping, preserving all existing entries verbatim.
735		membership := make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
736		var membershipRaw string
737		err = db.QueryRow("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = ?", glassMembershipKey).Scan(&membershipRaw)
738		if err != nil && err != sql.ErrNoRows {
739			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read %s: %w", glassMembershipKey, err)
740		}
741		if membershipRaw != "" {
742			if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(membershipRaw), &membership); jsonErr != nil {
743				slog.Warn("Failed to parse glass membership, starting fresh", "error", jsonErr)
744				membership = make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
745			}
746		}
747		encodedProjectID, err := json.Marshal(projectID)
748		if err != nil {
749			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal project ID: %w", err)
750		}
751		membership[composerID] = encodedProjectID
752		membershipJSON, err := json.Marshal(membership)
753		if err != nil {
754			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal glass membership: %w", err)
755		}
756		if _, err := db.Exec(
757			"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO ItemTable (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
758			glassMembershipKey, string(membershipJSON),
759		); err != nil {
760			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write %s: %w", glassMembershipKey, err)
761		}
762	
763		// Checkpoint so the write lands in the main DB file before Cursor next opens it
764		// (same rationale as WriteGlobalComposerHeader).
765		if _, err := db.Exec("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)"); err != nil {
766			slog.Warn("WAL checkpoint failed after glass registration", "error", err)
767		}
768	
769		slog.Info("Registered composer in glass sidebar",
770			"composerID", composerID, "projectID", projectID)
771		return nil
772	}
773	
774	// LoadAllComposerDataLightweight loads composer records for all sessions in the global database.
775	// Unlike LoadComposerDataBatch, it only reads composerData:* keys — no bubble records — so it
776	// is fast enough for global enumeration (ListAllAgentChatSessions). Inline conversation turns
777	// are included when present (Cursor 2 format); for Cursor 3 only the header list is returned
778	// and slug/name derivation falls back to the composer Name field.
779	func LoadAllComposerDataLightweight(globalDbPath string) (map[string]*ComposerData, error) {
780		db, err := OpenDatabase(globalDbPath)
781		if err != nil {
782			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open global database: %w", err)
783		}
784		defer func() {
785			if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
786				slog.Warn("Failed to close global database", "error", closeErr)
787			}
788		}()
789	
790		rows, err := db.Query("SELECT key, value FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE key LIKE 'composerData:%' AND value IS NOT NULL")
791		if err != nil {
792			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to query composer data: %w", err)
793		}
794		defer func() {
795			if closeErr := rows.Close(); closeErr != nil {
796				slog.Warn("Failed to close query rows", "error", closeErr)
797			}
798		}()
799	
800		composers := make(map[string]*ComposerData)
801		for rows.Next() {
802			var key, valueJSON string
803			if err := rows.Scan(&key, &valueJSON); err != nil {
804				slog.Warn("Failed to scan composer row", "error", err)
805				continue
806			}
807			composerID := strings.TrimPrefix(key, "composerData:")
808			var composer ComposerData
809			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(valueJSON), &composer); err != nil {
810				slog.Warn("Failed to parse composer data", "composerID", composerID, "error", err)
811				continue
812			}
813			composers[composerID] = &composer
814		}
815		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
816			return nil, fmt.Errorf("error iterating composer rows: %w", err)
817		}
818	
819		slog.Debug("Loaded lightweight composer data from global database", "count", len(composers))
820		return composers, nil
821	}

293		return &schema.ToolInfo{
294			Name:              toolData.Name,
295			Type:              toSchemaToolType(toolType),
296			Summary:           &summary,
297			FormattedMarkdown: &body,
298		}
299	}

301	// registeredToolType looks up the tool's category from the registry so error and
302	// cancelled invocations keep their real type (shell, write, …) instead of unknown,
303	// falling back to unknown for unregistered tools.
304	func registeredToolType(toolName string, toolRegistry *ToolRegistry) ToolType {
305		if handler := toolRegistry.GetHandler(toolName); handler != nil {
306			return handler.GetToolType()
307		}
308		return ToolTypeUnknown
309	}
310	
311	// resolveToolData finds the BubbleConversation for a tool bubble.
312	// V3+ stores it in bubble.ToolFormerData; V1 stores it in the capabilities map.
313	// Returns nil if the tool data cannot be found.
314	func resolveToolData(bubble *ComposerConversation, capabilitiesMap map[int]*CapabilityData, composerVersion int) *BubbleConversation {
315		if composerVersion >= 3 && bubble.ToolFormerData != nil {
316			return bubble.ToolFormerData
317		}
318		if capData, ok := capabilitiesMap[bubble.CapabilityType]; ok {
319			if capData.ParsedBubbleMap != nil {
320				if bubbleData, found := capData.ParsedBubbleMap[bubble.BubbleID]; found {
321					return bubbleData
322				}
323			}
324		}
325		return nil
326	}
327	
328	// processToolInvocation processes a tool invocation bubble and returns formatted markdown
329	func processToolInvocation(bubble *ComposerConversation, capabilitiesMap map[int]*CapabilityData, toolRegistry *ToolRegistry, composerVersion int) string {
330		toolData := resolveToolData(bubble, capabilitiesMap, composerVersion)
331		if toolData == nil {
332			slog.Warn("Tool invocation data not found",
333				"bubbleId", bubble.BubbleID,
334				"capabilityType", bubble.CapabilityType)
335			return bubble.Text // Fallback to original text
336		}
337	
338		// Format the tool invocation using the registry
339		return FormatToolInvocation(toolData, toolRegistry)
340	}
341	
342	// toSchemaToolType converts a cursoride ToolType to the schema tool type string.
343	// The only mapping difference is "mcp" which has no schema equivalent and maps to "generic".
344	func toSchemaToolType(t ToolType) string {
345		if t == ToolTypeMCP {
346			return schema.ToolTypeGeneric
347		}
348		return string(t)
349	}
350	
351	// parseCapabilities parses the capabilities array and extracts tool data
352	// Returns a map of capabilityType -> CapabilityData
353	func parseCapabilities(composer *ComposerData) map[int]*CapabilityData {
354		capabilitiesMap := make(map[int]*CapabilityData)
355	
356		for _, capability := range composer.Capabilities {
357			capData := capability.Data
358	
359			// Parse bubbleDataMap if it's a string (JSON)
360			if capData.BubbleDataMap != nil {
361				if bubbleMapStr, ok := capData.BubbleDataMap.(string); ok {
362					// Parse the JSON string into a map
363					var bubbleMap map[string]*BubbleConversation
364					if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(bubbleMapStr), &bubbleMap); err != nil {
365						slog.Warn("Failed to parse bubbleDataMap",
366							"capabilityType", capability.Type,
367							"error", err)
368					} else {
369						capData.ParsedBubbleMap = bubbleMap
370					}
371				}
372			}
373	
374			capabilitiesMap[capability.Type] = &capData
375		}
376	
377		return capabilitiesMap
378	}
379	
380	// calculateTimestamp calculates the absolute timestamp from timing info.
381	// Based on the TypeScript extension logic:
382	// Sometimes clientStartTime is relative (< 946684800000 = Jan 1, 2000).
383	// In the relative form clientStartTime holds elapsed milliseconds rather than an epoch
384	// timestamp, while the end-time fields stay absolute epoch milliseconds — so the
385	// absolute start is recovered as: clientEndTime (absolute) - clientStartTime (elapsed).
386	func calculateTimestamp(timingInfo *TimingInfo) string {
387		if timingInfo == nil {
388			return ""
389		}
390	
391		clientStartTime := timingInfo.ClientStartTime
392		if clientStartTime == 0 {
393			return ""
394		}
395	
396		// Check if clientStartTime is relative (< 946684800000, which is year 2000)
397		// e.g., full epoch: 1754311716540, relative: 1234.435
398		if clientStartTime < 946684800000 {
399			// Get clientEndTime (try fields in priority order)
400			var clientEndTime float64
401			if timingInfo.ClientRpcSendTime != 0 {
402				clientEndTime = timingInfo.ClientRpcSendTime
403			} else if timingInfo.ClientSettleTime != 0 {
404				clientEndTime = timingInfo.ClientSettleTime
405			} else if timingInfo.ClientEndTime != 0 {
406				clientEndTime = timingInfo.ClientEndTime
407			}
408	
409			// Calculate absolute time
410			if clientEndTime != 0 {
411				clientStartTime = clientEndTime - clientStartTime
412			}
413		}
414	
415		// Convert milliseconds to ISO 8601
416		// Split into seconds and fractional part for precise conversion
417		seconds := int64(clientStartTime / 1000)
418		nanos := int64((clientStartTime - float64(seconds)*1000) * 1000000)
419		t := time.Unix(seconds, nanos)
420		return t.Format(time.RFC3339)
421	}
422	
423	// unifiedModeToString converts Cursor's unifiedMode number to a readable string
424	// Based on the TypeScript extension logic (ts-extension/core/utils/composer.ts:118-132)
425	// 1 = Ask, 2 = Agent, 5 = Plan, other = Custom
426	func unifiedModeToString(unifiedMode int) string {
427		switch unifiedMode {
428		case 1:
429			return "Ask"
430		case 2:
431			return "Agent"
432		case 5:
433			return "Plan"
434		default:
435			if unifiedMode != 0 {
436				return "Custom"
437			}
438			return ""
439		}
440	}

67	func NewCursorIDEWatcher(

96		}

99	
100		// Set default check interval if not provided
101		if checkInterval == 0 {
102			checkInterval = defaultCheckInterval
103		}
104	
105		return &CursorIDEWatcher{

107			workspaces:       workspaces,

117			// actually ran," not "when the watcher was constructed." Seeding it with the

129	// Start begins monitoring the Cursor IDE databases
130	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) Start() error {
131		slog.Info("Starting Cursor IDE watcher",
132			"projectPath", w.projectPath,
133			"workspaceCount", len(w.workspaces),
134			"globalDbPath", w.globalDbPath,
135			"checkInterval", w.checkInterval,
136			"throttleDuration", w.throttleDuration)
137	
138		// Ensure WAL mode is enabled on all databases before watching.
139		// WAL mode is required so that the -wal file exists for fsnotify to detect changes.
140		// This is a one-time read-write operation at startup; all subsequent reads are read-only.
141		for _, ws := range w.workspaces {
142			if err := spi.EnsureWALMode(ws.DBPath); err != nil {
143				slog.Warn("Failed to ensure WAL mode on workspace database",
144					"workspaceID", ws.ID,
145					"error", err)
146			}
147		}
148		if err := spi.EnsureWALMode(w.globalDbPath); err != nil {
149			slog.Warn("Failed to ensure WAL mode on global database", "error", err)
150		}
151	
152		// Seed knownComposers with the sessions that already exist so startup doesn't
153		// re-emit every historical session — matching the other providers' watchers
154		// (e.g. Cursor CLI's SetInitialState). Sessions updated after this point still
155		// process because their lastUpdatedAt advances past the seeded watermark.
156		w.seedKnownComposers()
157	
158		// Set up file watching on all matching workspace databases
159		for _, ws := range w.workspaces {
160			if err := w.watchDatabaseFiles(ws.DBPath); err != nil {
161				slog.Warn("Failed to watch workspace database files",
162					"workspaceID", ws.ID,
163					"error", err)
164			}
165		}
166	
167		// Set up file watching on global database
168		if err := w.watchDatabaseFiles(w.globalDbPath); err != nil {
169			slog.Warn("Failed to watch global database files", "error", err)
170		}
171	
172		// Start the file event handler goroutine
173		w.wg.Add(1)
174		go w.handleFileEvents()
175	
176		// Start the safety net polling goroutine
177		w.wg.Add(1)
178		go w.safetyNetPoller()
179	
180		// Perform initial check after a short delay. The timer is stored so Stop() can
181		// cancel it if it hasn't fired yet.
182		w.initialCheckTimer = time.AfterFunc(5*time.Second, func() {
183			w.triggerCheck("initial")
184		})

186		slog.Info("Cursor IDE watcher started successfully")
187		return nil
188	}

190	// seedKnownComposers records the current lastUpdatedAt of every composer already in the
191	// project's workspaces, without firing callbacks. Uses the lightweight loader (composer
192	// rows only, no bubbles) since only the timestamps are needed. Failures are non-fatal:
193	// the worst case is that the first check re-emits existing sessions, which is the exact
194	// behavior this seeding exists to avoid, not a correctness problem.
195	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) seedKnownComposers() {
196		// One lightweight scan serves both needs here: discovery (via projectComposerIDs)
197		// and the per-composer timestamps read below.
198		composers, err := LoadAllComposerDataLightweight(w.globalDbPath)
199		if err != nil {
200			slog.Warn("Failed to seed existing sessions; first check may re-emit them", "error", err)
201			return
202		}
203		composerIDs, err := projectComposerIDs(composers, w.projectPath, w.workspaces)
204		if err != nil || len(composerIDs) == 0 {
205			return
206		}
207	
208		w.mu.Lock()
209		defer w.mu.Unlock()
210		seeded := 0
211		for _, composerID := range composerIDs {
212			composer, exists := composers[composerID]
213			if !exists {
214				continue
215			}
216			timestamp := composer.LastUpdatedAt
217			if timestamp == 0 {
218				timestamp = composer.CreatedAt
219			}
220			w.knownComposers[composerID] = timestamp
221			seeded++
222		}
223		slog.Debug("Seeded existing sessions as known", "count", seeded)
224	}

226	// Stop gracefully stops the watcher
227	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) Stop() {
228		slog.Info("Stopping Cursor IDE watcher")
229	
230		// Stop the initial-check timer in case it hasn't fired yet — no point starting a
231		// check that would just have to be waited on below.
232		if w.initialCheckTimer != nil {
233			w.initialCheckTimer.Stop()
234		}
235	
236		// Perform one final check before stopping
237		slog.Info("Performing final check for changes before stopping")
238		w.checkForChanges("shutdown")
239	
240		// Close fsnotify watcher
241		if w.fsWatcher != nil {
242			if err := w.fsWatcher.Close(); err != nil {
243				slog.Warn("Error closing fsnotify watcher", "error", err)
244			}
245		}
246	
247		// Cancel under w.mu, then wait. Every check-spawning wg.Add happens under this
248		// lock (triggerCheck/executePendingCheck), so once cancel lands no trigger can
249		// pass the ctx check and Add after Wait has started — Add-concurrent-with-Wait
250		// on a drained WaitGroup is a documented misuse.
251		w.mu.Lock()
252		w.cancel()
253		w.mu.Unlock()
254		w.wg.Wait()
255	
256		// Wait for any pending callback goroutines to complete
257		slog.Info("Waiting for pending callbacks to complete")
258		w.callbackWg.Wait()
259	
260		slog.Info("Cursor IDE watcher stopped")
261	}

263	// watchDatabaseFiles sets up file watching for a database and its WAL file.
264	//
265	// Why the parent directory instead of the files themselves: in WAL mode nearly every
266	// write lands in state.vscdb-wal, and SQLite deletes that file when the last
267	// connection closes and recreates it on the next open. A watch on the file itself is
268	// never added when the file doesn't exist yet (watcher started before Cursor), and
269	// dies with the inode when Cursor checkpoints/restarts — silently degrading all
270	// updates to the 2-minute safety-net poll. A directory watch keeps delivering
271	// Create/Write events for the db and its -wal across those lifecycles.
272	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) watchDatabaseFiles(dbPath string) error {
273		dir := filepath.Dir(dbPath)
274		if err := w.fsWatcher.Add(dir); err != nil {
275			// Log but don't fail - we'll rely on polling
276			slog.Warn("Failed to watch database directory", "dir", dir, "error", err)
277			return err
278		}
279	
280		// Register the db path so handleFileEvents can filter directory events
281		// down to this database's files.
282		w.watchedDBPaths = append(w.watchedDBPaths, dbPath)
283		slog.Debug("Watching database directory", "dir", dir, "dbPath", dbPath)
284	
285		return nil
286	}

288	// isWatchedDBFile reports whether a file event path belongs to one of the watched
289	// databases (the db file itself or a sibling like -wal/-shm/-journal).
290	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) isWatchedDBFile(name string) bool {
291		for _, dbPath := range w.watchedDBPaths {
292			if name == dbPath || strings.HasPrefix(name, dbPath+"-") {
293				return true
294			}
295		}
296		return false
297	}

299	// handleFileEvents processes file system events from fsnotify
300	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) handleFileEvents() {
301		defer w.wg.Done()
302	
303		for {
304			select {
305			case <-w.ctx.Done():
306				return
307	
308			case event, ok := <-w.fsWatcher.Events:
309				if !ok {
310					return
311				}
312	
313				// Only care about Write and Create events on the database files —
314				// the watch is on the parent directory, so unrelated neighbors
315				// (e.g. workspace.json) must be filtered out.
316				if (event.Has(fsnotify.Write) || event.Has(fsnotify.Create)) && w.isWatchedDBFile(event.Name) {
317					slog.Debug("Database file changed", "path", event.Name, "op", event.Op)
318					w.triggerCheck("file-change")
319				}
320	
321			case err, ok := <-w.fsWatcher.Errors:
322				if !ok {
323					return
324				}
325				slog.Warn("File watcher error", "error", err)
326			}
327		}
328	}
329	
330	// safetyNetPoller ensures we check the database periodically even if file events are missed
331	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) safetyNetPoller() {
332		defer w.wg.Done()
333	
334		ticker := time.NewTicker(w.checkInterval)
335		defer ticker.Stop()
336	
337		for {
338			select {
339			case <-w.ctx.Done():
340				return
341			case <-ticker.C:
342				slog.Debug("Safety net poll triggered")
343				w.triggerCheck("poll")
344			}
345		}
346	}
347	
348	// triggerCheck requests a check, respecting throttle limits
349	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) triggerCheck(trigger string) {
350		w.mu.Lock()
351		defer w.mu.Unlock()
352	
353		// Shutdown guard: Stop() cancels the context under this same lock, so a trigger
354		// arriving after cancellation must not wg.Add (Stop may already be in wg.Wait).
355		// This covers the throttle branch below; runCheckAsync re-checks for its own path.
356		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
357			return
358		}
359	
360		now := time.Now()
361		timeSinceLastCall := now.Sub(w.lastThrottledCall)
362	
363		if timeSinceLastCall < w.throttleDuration {
364			// Within throttle window - mark as pending
365			if !w.pendingCheck {
366				w.pendingCheck = true
367				// Schedule a check after throttle duration expires
368				delay := w.throttleDuration - timeSinceLastCall
369				slog.Debug("Check throttled, will retry after delay",
370					"trigger", trigger,
371					"delay", delay)
372	
373				w.wg.Add(1)
374				go func() {
375					defer w.wg.Done()
376					timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
377					defer timer.Stop()
378					select {
379					case <-w.ctx.Done():
380						return
381					case <-timer.C:
382						w.executePendingCheck()
383					}
384				}()
385			}
386			return
387		}
388	
389		// Execute immediately
390		w.lastThrottledCall = now
391		w.pendingCheck = false
392		w.runCheckAsync(trigger)
393	}
394	
395	// runCheckAsync runs checkForChanges in a new goroutine tracked by w.wg, so Stop()'s
396	// w.wg.Wait() actually waits for it instead of returning while it's still running.
397	// It's a no-op if the watcher's context is already cancelled.
398	// Must be called with w.mu held: Stop() cancels the context under the same lock, which
399	// is what makes the ctx check and wg.Add here atomic with respect to shutdown.
400	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) runCheckAsync(trigger string) {
401		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
402			return
403		}
404		w.wg.Add(1)
405		go func() {
406			defer w.wg.Done()
407			w.checkForChanges(trigger)
408		}()
409	}
410	
411	// executePendingCheck executes a pending check if one was scheduled
412	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) executePendingCheck() {
413		w.mu.Lock()
414		defer w.mu.Unlock()
415	
416		if !w.pendingCheck {
417			return
418		}
419	
420		now := time.Now()
421		timeSinceLastCall := now.Sub(w.lastThrottledCall)
422	
423		if timeSinceLastCall >= w.throttleDuration {
424			w.lastThrottledCall = now
425			w.pendingCheck = false
426			w.runCheckAsync("throttled")
427		}
428	}
429	
430	// checkForChanges queries the databases and processes any new or updated sessions.
431	// The checking mutex prevents concurrent executions that would multiply DB connections.
432	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) checkForChanges(trigger string) {
433		// Prevent overlapping checks. Normal triggers use TryLock and skip so slow checks
434		// don't pile up goroutines, but the shutdown flush must not be skipped — its whole
435		// purpose is to catch changes an in-flight check's snapshot missed, so it blocks
436		// until that check finishes.
437		if trigger == "shutdown" {
438			w.checking.Lock()
439		} else if !w.checking.TryLock() {
440			slog.Debug("Skipping check, previous check still running", "trigger", trigger)
441			return
442		}
443		defer w.checking.Unlock()
444	
445		slog.Debug("Checking for changes", "trigger", trigger)
446	
447		w.mu.Lock()
448		lastCheck := w.lastCheck
449		w.lastCheck = time.Now()
450		w.mu.Unlock()
451	
452		// Load the project's composer IDs from both association sources: workspace-DB
453		// references (older Cursor) and the workspaceIdentifier embedded in global
454		// composerData rows (the only live source in Cursor >= 3.12).
455		composerIDs, err := FindProjectComposerIDs(w.globalDbPath, w.projectPath, w.workspaces)
456		if err != nil {
457			slog.Error("Failed to load project composer IDs", "error", err)
458			return
459		}
460	
461		if len(composerIDs) == 0 {
462			slog.Debug("No composers found for project")
463			return
464		}
465	
466		// Load composer data from global database
467		composers, err := LoadComposerDataBatch(w.globalDbPath, composerIDs)
468		if err != nil {
469			slog.Error("Failed to load composer data", "error", err)
470			return
471		}
472	
473		// Track new/updated sessions
474		newCount := 0
475		updatedCount := 0
476	
477		for composerID, composer := range composers {
478			// Skip if conversation is empty
479			if len(composer.Conversation) == 0 {
480				continue
481			}
482	
483			// Check if this is a new or updated session
484			w.mu.RLock()
485			knownTimestamp, exists := w.knownComposers[composerID]
486			w.mu.RUnlock()
487	
488			currentTimestamp := composer.LastUpdatedAt
489			if currentTimestamp == 0 {
490				currentTimestamp = composer.CreatedAt
491			}
492	
493			// Determine if we should process this session
494			shouldProcess := false
495			if !exists {
496				// New session
497				shouldProcess = true
498				newCount++
499				slog.Info("Found new session", "composerID", composerID, "name", composer.Name)
500			} else if currentTimestamp > knownTimestamp {
501				// Updated session
502				shouldProcess = true
503				updatedCount++
504				slog.Info("Found updated session",
505					"composerID", composerID,
506					"name", composer.Name,
507					"oldTimestamp", knownTimestamp,
508					"newTimestamp", currentTimestamp)
509			}
510	
511			if shouldProcess {
512				// Guard against a race condition: Cursor may commit the composerData record
513				// (updating LastUpdatedAt and FullConversationHeadersOnly) before the
514				// corresponding bubble records are committed to the database. If the header
515				// list references more bubbles than were actually loaded, the session data is
516				// incomplete. By not advancing knownComposers, the next check cycle will
517				// re-process this session once all bubbles are available.
518				if len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly) > 0 &&
519					len(composer.Conversation) < len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly) {
520					// Debug, not Warn: this is expected, transient state while Cursor is
521					// mid-write, and it fires routinely during normal streaming.
522					slog.Debug("Incomplete composer data (bubble records not yet committed), will retry on next check",
523						"composerID", composerID,
524						"expectedBubbles", len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly),
525						"loadedBubbles", len(composer.Conversation))
526					continue
527				}
528	
529				// Guard against a second race condition: the bubble count may match the header
530				// count (so the guard above passes), but the last committed bubble is a user
531				// message with no agent response yet. This happens because Cursor writes the
532				// user bubble and updates lastUpdatedAt in one step, before the agent has
533				// produced a reply. Processing now would generate markdown that is missing the
534				// agent response entirely.
535				//
536				// We skip the session and let knownComposers stay at the old timestamp so it
537				// is re-evaluated on the next check cycle (when the agent reply arrives).
538				// The pendingIncomplete map records when we first saw the session in this
539				// state. If the agent never replies (e.g. the user abandoned the chat),
540				// we process the session anyway after incompleteTimeout so the markdown is
541				// not lost permanently.
542				if len(composer.Conversation) > 0 {
543					lastBubble := &composer.Conversation[len(composer.Conversation)-1]
544					if lastBubble.Type == 1 {
545						w.mu.Lock()
546						firstSeen, alreadyPending := w.pendingIncomplete[composerID]
547						if !alreadyPending {
548							w.pendingIncomplete[composerID] = time.Now()
549							w.mu.Unlock()
550							// Debug, not Warn: waiting for the agent reply is the normal
551							// state while the user's request is in flight.
552							slog.Debug("Last bubble is a user message (agent not yet responded), will retry on next check",
553								"composerID", composerID,
554								"lastBubbleID", lastBubble.BubbleID)
555							continue
556						}
557						if time.Since(firstSeen) < w.incompleteTimeout {
558							w.mu.Unlock()
559							slog.Debug("Still waiting for agent response, will retry on next check",
560								"composerID", composerID,
561								"waited", time.Since(firstSeen))
562							continue
563						}
564						// Timed out — the agent likely never replied; process anyway.
565						delete(w.pendingIncomplete, composerID)
566						w.mu.Unlock()
567						slog.Warn("Timed out waiting for agent response, processing incomplete session",
568							"composerID", composerID,
569							"waited", time.Since(firstSeen))
570					} else {
571						// Last bubble is an agent message — clear any stale pending state.
572						w.mu.Lock()
573						delete(w.pendingIncomplete, composerID)
574						w.mu.Unlock()
575					}
576				}
577	
578				// Convert to AgentChatSession
579				session, err := ConvertToAgentChatSession(composer, w.projectPath)
580				if err != nil {
581					// Don't advance knownComposers on failure — leave the watermark where it
582					// was so this composer is retried on the next check instead of being
583					// silently skipped forever.
584					slog.Warn("Failed to convert composer to session",
585						"composerID", composerID,
586						"error", err)
587					continue
588				}
589	
590				// Update known timestamp. Only done after a successful conversion so a
591				// failure (see above) doesn't permanently poison the watermark for this composer.
592				w.mu.Lock()
593				w.knownComposers[composerID] = currentTimestamp
594				w.mu.Unlock()
595	
596				// Write debug output if requested
597				if w.debugRaw {
598					if err := writeDebugOutput(session); err != nil {
599						slog.Warn("Failed to write debug output",
600							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
601							"error", err)
602					}
603				}
604	
605				// Invoke callback asynchronously so a panic during processing (e.g. markdown
606				// write or cloud sync) doesn't crash the watcher, and slow callback I/O
607				// doesn't delay processing of the remaining sessions in this check.
608				slog.Info("Invoking callback for session",
609					"sessionID", session.SessionID,
610					"slug", session.Slug)
611				w.callbackWg.Add(1)
612				go func(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
613					defer w.callbackWg.Done()
614					defer func() {
615						if r := recover(); r != nil {
616							slog.Error("Session callback panicked", "panic", r, "sessionID", s.SessionID)
617						}
618					}()
619					w.sessionCallback(s)
620				}(session)
621			}
622		}
623	
624		// On the very first check lastCheck is the zero time; report 0 instead of a
625		// nonsensical ~2000-year duration.
626		var elapsed time.Duration
627		if !lastCheck.IsZero() {
628			elapsed = time.Since(lastCheck)
629		}
630		slog.Info("Completed check for changes",
631			"trigger", trigger,
632			"totalComposers", len(composers),
633			"newSessions", newCount,
634			"updatedSessions", updatedCount,
635			"elapsedSinceLastCheck", elapsed)
636	}
637

272	// formatJSONBlock renders data as an indented JSON code block, truncated to at most
273	// maxRunes when positive (<= 0 means no cap). Content is kept verbatim (fencedBlock
274	// sizes the fence around any backticks) so resumed sessions carry real JSON instead
275	// of HTML entities.
276	func formatJSONBlock(data map[string]interface{}, maxRunes int) string {
277		var jsonStr string
278		if jsonBytes, err := json.MarshalIndent(data, "", "  "); err != nil {
279			jsonStr = fmt.Sprintf("%v", data)
280		} else {
281			jsonStr = string(jsonBytes)
282		}
283		if maxRunes > 0 {
284			jsonStr = capRunes(jsonStr, maxRunes)
285		}
286		return fencedBlock("json", jsonStr) + "\n"
287	}

289	// toolResultCap bounds how much tool output is rendered into the markdown body.
290	// Inputs are not capped — they carry what the agent chose to do (e.g. a patch or
291	// edit content) — but results (command output, tool result payloads) can be
292	// arbitrarily large and matter less once the agent has already responded to them.
293	const toolResultCap = 2000

295	// fencedBlock wraps content in a code fence with an optional language tag, keeping
296	// the content verbatim. codeFence sizes the fence so embedded backtick runs can't
297	// terminate the block early.
298	func fencedBlock(lang, content string) string {
299		fence := codeFence(content)
300		return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s\n%s\n%s", fence, lang, content, fence)
301	}
302	
303	// codeFence returns a backtick fence long enough to safely wrap s: one backtick more
304	// than the longest backtick run inside it (a value containing ``` would otherwise
305	// terminate a plain three-backtick fence early), never shorter than the standard three.
306	func codeFence(s string) string {
307		longest, run := 0, 0
308		for _, r := range s {
309			if r == '`' {
310				run++
311				if run > longest {
312					longest = run
313				}
314			} else {
315				run = 0
316			}
317		}
318		size := longest + 1
319		if size < 3 {
320			size = 3
321		}
322		return strings.Repeat("`", size)
323	}
324	
325	// capRunes truncates s to at most max runes, marking the cut. Rune-based so a cap
326	// never splits a multi-byte character. Scans rune boundaries instead of converting
327	// to []rune, which would allocate O(len(s)) for exactly the oversized tool results
328	// this cap protects against.
329	func capRunes(s string, max int) string {
330		if len(s) <= max {
331			return s // fast path: byte length bounds rune length
332		}
333		count := 0
334		for i := range s {
335			if count == max {
336				return s[:i] + "\n… (output truncated)"
337			}
338			count++
339		}
340		return s // more bytes than max but fewer runes (multi-byte characters)
341	}

1	package copilotide
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"strings"
9		"sync"
10		"time"
11	
12		"github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify"
13		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
14	)
15	
16	// WatchChatSessions watches the chatSessions directory for new/modified session files
17	func (p *Provider) WatchChatSessions(
18		ctx context.Context,
19		workspaceDir string,
20		projectPath string,
21		debugRaw bool,
22		sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession),
23	) error {
24		chatSessionsPath := GetChatSessionsPath(workspaceDir)
25	
26		slog.Info("Starting Copilot watcher",
27			"app", p.variant.AppName,
28			"workspaceDir", workspaceDir,
29			"chatSessionsPath", chatSessionsPath)
30	
31		// Create fsnotify watcher
32		watcher, err := fsnotify.NewWatcher()
33		if err != nil {
34			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create watcher: %w", err)
35		}
36		defer func() {
37			if err := watcher.Close(); err != nil {
38				slog.Warn("Failed to close watcher", "error", err)
39			}
40		}()
41	
42		// Tracks in-flight sessionCallback goroutines so we don't return while a
43		// callback is still writing. Runs before the watcher-close defer (LIFO).
44		var callbackWg sync.WaitGroup
45		defer callbackWg.Wait()
46	
47		// Watch the chatSessions directory
48		if err := watcher.Add(chatSessionsPath); err != nil {
49			return fmt.Errorf("failed to watch directory: %w", err)
50		}
51	
52		slog.Info("Watching chatSessions directory", "path", chatSessionsPath)
53	
54		// Track known sessions and their modification times
55		knownSessions := make(map[string]int64)
56	
57		// Debouncing map - track last processed time for each file
58		lastProcessed := make(map[string]time.Time)
59		debounceWindow := 500 * time.Millisecond
60	
61		// Process existing sessions first
62		existingSessions, err := LoadAllSessionFiles(workspaceDir)
63		if err != nil {
64			slog.Warn("Failed to load existing sessions", "error", err)
65		} else {
66			for _, sessionPath := range existingSessions {
67				composer, err := LoadSessionFile(sessionPath)
68				if err != nil {
69					slog.Warn("Failed to load session", "path", sessionPath, "error", err)
70					continue
71				}
72	
73				// Track as known
74				knownSessions[composer.SessionID] = composer.LastMessageDate
75	
76				slog.Debug("Tracked existing session", "sessionId", composer.SessionID)
77			}
78		}
79	
80		// Event loop
81		for {
82			select {
83			case <-ctx.Done():
84				slog.Info("Watcher context canceled, stopping")
85				return nil
86	
87			case event, ok := <-watcher.Events:
88				if !ok {
89					return fmt.Errorf("watcher events channel closed")
90				}
91	
92				// Only process JSON and JSONL files
93				if !strings.HasSuffix(event.Name, ".json") && !strings.HasSuffix(event.Name, ".jsonl") {
94					continue
95				}
96	
97				// Only process Write and Create events
98				if !event.Has(fsnotify.Write) && !event.Has(fsnotify.Create) {
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				// Debounce rapid events for the same file
103				now := time.Now()
104				if lastTime, ok := lastProcessed[event.Name]; ok && now.Sub(lastTime) < debounceWindow {
105					slog.Debug("Debouncing rapid event", "path", event.Name)
106					continue
107				}
108	
109				slog.Debug("File event detected", "path", event.Name, "op", event.Op)
110	
111				// Load the session file
112				composer, err := LoadSessionFile(event.Name)
113				if err != nil {
114					// Don't record the debounce timestamp on failure: the file was
115					// likely caught mid-write, and the follow-up write event must
116					// not be swallowed by the debounce window or the update is lost.
117					slog.Warn("Failed to load session after event", "path", event.Name, "error", err)
118					continue
119				}
120				lastProcessed[event.Name] = now
121	
122				// Check if this is new or updated
123				sessionID := composer.SessionID
124				lastKnownTime, exists := knownSessions[sessionID]
125	
126				isNew := !exists
127				isUpdated := exists && composer.LastMessageDate > lastKnownTime
128	
129				if isNew || isUpdated {
130					// Update known sessions
131					knownSessions[sessionID] = composer.LastMessageDate
132	
133					if isNew {
134						slog.Info("New session detected", "sessionId", sessionID, "name", composer.Name)
135					} else {
136						slog.Info("Session updated", "sessionId", sessionID, "name", composer.Name)
137					}
138	
139					// Load state file (optional)
140					state, err := LoadStateFile(workspaceDir, sessionID)
141					if err != nil {
142						slog.Warn("Failed to load state file", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
143					}
144	
145					// Convert to AgentChatSession
146					session := p.ConvertToSessionData(*composer, projectPath, state)
147	
148					// Write debug files if requested
149					if debugRaw {
150						if err := WriteDebugFiles(composer, sessionID); err != nil {
151							slog.Warn("Failed to write debug files", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
152						}
153					}
154	
155					// Invoke callback asynchronously so a panic during processing (e.g.
156					// markdown write or cloud sync) doesn't crash the watcher, and slow
157					// callback I/O doesn't block the fsnotify event loop.
158					slog.Info("Invoking callback for session", "sessionId", sessionID, "slug", session.Slug)
159					callbackWg.Add(1)
160					go func(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
161						defer callbackWg.Done()
162						defer func() {
163							if r := recover(); r != nil {
164								slog.Error("Session callback panicked", "panic", r, "sessionId", s.SessionID)
165							}
166						}()
167						sessionCallback(s)
168					}(&session)
169				}
170	
171			case err, ok := <-watcher.Errors:
172				if !ok {
173					return fmt.Errorf("watcher errors channel closed")
174				}
175				slog.Warn("Watcher error", "error", err)
176			}
177		}
178	}
179	
180	// GetSessionIDFromPath extracts session ID from a file path
181	func GetSessionIDFromPath(path string) string {
182		filename := filepath.Base(path)
183		// Remove .json or .jsonl extension
184		if strings.HasSuffix(filename, ".jsonl") {
185			return strings.TrimSuffix(filename, ".jsonl")
186		}
187		return strings.TrimSuffix(filename, ".json")
188	}
189

22		// writes (the `version` field inside the kind:0 snapshot).
23		copilotSessionVersion = 3
24	
25		// copilotResponderUsername mirrors the responderUsername VS Code stamps on sessions.
26		copilotResponderUsername = "GitHub Copilot"
27	
28		// copilotModelID is the model identifier VS Code uses for automatic model selection;
29		// reconstructed turns did not run through a specific Copilot model, so "auto" is the
30		// honest label and lets the user continue with whatever model VS Code picks.
31		copilotModelID = "copilot/auto"
32	
33		// importedRequestText hosts leading agent turns (e.g. the migration note): VS Code's
34		// chat model is strictly request(user) -> response(agent) pairs, so an agent turn
35		// with no preceding user turn needs a synthetic host request.
36		importedRequestText = "Session imported via SpecStory."
37	
38		// chatSessionIndexKey is the ItemTable key in the workspace state.vscdb where VS Code
39		// keeps its chat session index. Sessions absent from this index do not appear in the
40		// Chat panel's session list, so reconstruction must register the new session here.
41		chatSessionIndexKey = "chat.ChatSessionStore.index"
42	
43		// indexResponseStateComplete is the lastResponseState value VS Code records on
44		// sessions whose final response finished normally.
45		indexResponseStateComplete = 1
46	)
47	
48	// ReconstructSession rebuilds a VS Code Copilot native session from the neutral
49	// SessionData: a single kind:0 JSONL snapshot (the format current VS Code writes to
50	// chatSessions/<sessionId>.jsonl) returned as Content for the caller to write via
51	// NativeSessionPath, plus a session entry registered in the workspace state.vscdb
52	// chat.ChatSessionStore.index — without which VS Code never shows the session.
53	//
54	// Flattened turns are paired into VS Code request blocks: each user turn opens a
55	// request, consecutive agent turns collapse into its markdown response. VS Code must be
56	// fully quit and restarted to pick up the index entry — it holds the index in memory in
57	// the main process and flushes it over ours on shutdown, and a "Developer: Reload
58	// Window" keeps that process alive, so a reload is not enough (verified empirically).
59	func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
60		turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64	
65		workspaceRoot := spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts, data)
66		if workspaceRoot == "" {
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot register session in VS Code: no workspace root provided")
68		}
69		workspace, wsErr := p.findWorkspaceForReconstruction(workspaceRoot)
70		if wsErr != nil {
71			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot register session in %s: no workspace found for %q (open the folder in %s once first): %w", p.variant.AppName, workspaceRoot, p.variant.AppName, wsErr)
72		}
73	
74		newID := uuid.NewString()
75		nowMs := time.Now().UnixMilli()
76		title := spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data.Slug)
77	
78		requests := buildRequestBlocks(turns, nowMs)
79		// Match the timestamp of the last request block (staggered 1s per request
80		// starting at nowMs) so the session's "last updated" ordering is exact.
81		lastMs := nowMs
82		if n := len(requests); n > 0 {
83			lastMs = nowMs + int64(n-1)*1000
84		}
85	
86		// Top-level snapshot fields mirror what current VS Code writes (observed on a real
87		// v3 session file); customTitle is what the Chat panel displays and what our own
88		// slug/name extraction prefers. inputState (the chat input box UI state) is omitted —
89		// VS Code defaults it when absent.
90		composer := map[string]any{
91			"version":           copilotSessionVersion,
92			"sessionId":         newID,
93			"customTitle":       title,
94			"creationDate":      nowMs,
95			"lastMessageDate":   lastMs,
96			"isImported":        true,
97			"initialLocation":   "panel",
98			"hasPendingEdits":   false,
99			"pendingRequests":   []any{},
100			"responderUsername": copilotResponderUsername,
101			"requests":          requests,
102		}
103	
104		line, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"kind": 0, "v": composer})
105		if err != nil {
106			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session snapshot: %w", err)
107		}
108	
109		entry := sessionIndexEntry{
110			SessionID:       newID,
111			Title:           title,
112			LastMessageDate: lastMs,
113			Timing: sessionIndexTiming{
114				Created:            nowMs,
115				LastRequestStarted: lastMs,
116				LastRequestEnded:   lastMs,
117			},
118			InitialLocation:   "panel",
119			LastResponseState: indexResponseStateComplete,
120		}
121		if err := writeSessionIndexEntry(GetWorkspaceStateDBPath(workspace.Dir), entry); err != nil {
122			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to register session in VS Code workspace index: %w", err)
123		}
124	
125		slog.Info("Reconstructed session registered in VS Code workspace index",
126			"sessionID", newID, "workspaceID", workspace.ID, "turns", len(turns), "requests", len(requests))
127	
128		return &spi.ReconstructedSession{
129			SessionID: newID,
130			Filename:  newID + ".jsonl",
131			Content:   append(line, '\n'),
132		}, nil
133	}
