135	// NativeSessionPath resolves where a reconstructed session file belongs: the matched
136	// workspace's chatSessions directory. The directory may not exist yet — the caller
137	// creates it — so the lookup must not require it (findWorkspaceForReconstruction).
138	func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(projectPath string, filename string) (string, error) {
139		workspace, err := p.findWorkspaceForReconstruction(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", fmt.Errorf("no %s workspace found for %q (open the folder in %s once first): %w", p.variant.AppName, projectPath, p.variant.AppName, err)
142		}
143		return filepath.Join(GetChatSessionsPath(workspace.Dir), filename), nil
144	}
145	
146	// SupportsReconstruction reports true: this provider has a native serializer
147	// (see ReconstructSession), so it can be a cross-agent resume target.
148	func (p *Provider) SupportsReconstruction() bool {
149		return true
150	}
151	
152	// buildRequestBlocks pairs the flattened turns into VS Code request blocks: a user turn
153	// opens a request, consecutive agent turns join into its single markdown response item.
154	// Leading agent turns (the migration note) get a synthetic host request, and a trailing
155	// user turn simply carries an empty response. Timestamps are staggered one second per
156	// request so ordering is stable.
157	func buildRequestBlocks(turns []spi.Turn, baseMs int64) []map[string]any {
158		var blocks []map[string]any
159		var userText string
160		var agentParts []string
161		open := false
162	
163		flush := func() {
164			if !open {
165				return
166			}
167			ts := baseMs + int64(len(blocks))*1000
168			blocks = append(blocks, buildRequestBlock(userText, strings.Join(agentParts, "\n\n"), ts))
169			userText, agentParts, open = "", nil, false
170		}
171	
172		for _, turn := range turns {
173			if turn.Role == schema.RoleUser {
174				flush()
175				userText, open = turn.Text, true
176			} else {
177				if !open {
178					userText, open = importedRequestText, true
179				}
180				agentParts = append(agentParts, turn.Text)
181			}
182		}
183		flush()
184	
185		return blocks
186	}
187	
188	// buildRequestBlock serializes one user->agent exchange in the shape VS Code writes:
189	// the message carries the parsed single-text-part form, and the response is a serialized
190	// markdown string (an object with a `value` field and no `kind` — exactly what VS Code
191	// itself stores for plain markdown responses, and what our parser reads back).
192	func buildRequestBlock(userText, agentText string, tsMs int64) map[string]any {
193		lines := strings.Split(userText, "\n")
194	
195		response := []any{}
196		if agentText != "" {
197			response = append(response, map[string]any{
198				"value":             agentText,
199				"supportThemeIcons": false,
200				"supportHtml":       false,
201			})
202		}
203	
204		return map[string]any{
205			"requestId":  "request_" + uuid.NewString(),
206			"responseId": "response_" + uuid.NewString(),
207			"timestamp":  tsMs,
208			"modelId":    copilotModelID,
209			"message": map[string]any{
210				"text": userText,
211				"parts": []any{map[string]any{
212					"kind": "text",
213					"text": userText,
214					"range": map[string]any{
215						"start":        0,
216						"endExclusive": utf16Len(userText),
217					},
218					"editorRange": map[string]any{
219						"startLineNumber": 1,
220						"startColumn":     1,
221						"endLineNumber":   len(lines),
222						"endColumn":       utf16Len(lines[len(lines)-1]) + 1,
223					},
224				}},
225			},
226			"response": response,
227			"result": map[string]any{
228				"timings":  map[string]any{"firstProgress": 0, "totalElapsed": 0},
229				"metadata": map[string]any{},
230			},
231			"variableData":      map[string]any{"variables": []any{}},
232			"followups":         []any{},
233			"isCanceled":        false,
234			"contentReferences": []any{},
235			"codeCitations":     []any{},
236		}
237	}
238	
239	// utf16Len returns the length of s in UTF-16 code units — the unit VS Code uses for
240	// offsets and columns in serialized ranges.
241	func utf16Len(s string) int {
242		n := 0
243		for _, r := range s {
244			n++
245			if r > 0xFFFF {
246				n++ // surrogate pair
247			}
248		}
249		return n
250	}
251	
252	// sessionIndexEntry is one entry in VS Code's chat.ChatSessionStore.index, keyed by
253	// session ID. isEmpty/isExternal/hasPendingEdits marshal explicitly (not omitempty)
254	// because VS Code stores them as literal false on real entries.
255	type sessionIndexEntry struct {
256		SessionID         string             `json:"sessionId"`
257		Title             string             `json:"title"`
258		LastMessageDate   int64              `json:"lastMessageDate"`
259		Timing            sessionIndexTiming `json:"timing"`
260		InitialLocation   string             `json:"initialLocation"`
261		HasPendingEdits   bool               `json:"hasPendingEdits"`
262		IsEmpty           bool               `json:"isEmpty"`
263		IsExternal        bool               `json:"isExternal"`
264		LastResponseState int                `json:"lastResponseState"`
265	}
266	
267	// sessionIndexTiming mirrors the timing sub-object of an index entry.
268	type sessionIndexTiming struct {
269		Created            int64 `json:"created"`
270		LastRequestStarted int64 `json:"lastRequestStarted,omitempty"`
271		LastRequestEnded   int64 `json:"lastRequestEnded,omitempty"`
272	}
273	
274	// writeSessionIndexEntry merges entry into the chat.ChatSessionStore.index value of the
275	// given workspace state.vscdb, preserving all existing entries byte-for-byte (they are
276	// kept as raw JSON, never re-marshaled). A missing index row starts a fresh one. The
277	// write races VS Code's own in-memory copy — a running VS Code flushes its version over
278	// ours on shutdown — which is why the resume flow tells the user to restart VS Code.
279	func writeSessionIndexEntry(dbPath string, entry sessionIndexEntry) error {
280		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dbPath)
281		if err != nil {
282			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open workspace state database: %w", err)
283		}
284		defer func() {
285			if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
286				slog.Warn("Failed to close workspace state database", "error", closeErr)
287			}
288		}()
289		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
290		// Wait out short-lived locks from a running VS Code instead of failing immediately.
291		if _, err := db.Exec("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000"); err != nil {
292			slog.Warn("Failed to set busy_timeout on workspace state database", "error", err)
293		}
294	
295		index := struct {
296			Version int                        `json:"version"`
297			Entries map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"entries"`
298		}{Version: 1, Entries: map[string]json.RawMessage{}}
299	
300		var raw string
301		scanErr := db.QueryRow("SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = ?", chatSessionIndexKey).Scan(&raw)
302		switch {
303		case scanErr == nil:
304			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &index); err != nil {
305				return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse existing chat session index: %w", err)
306			}
307			if index.Entries == nil {
308				index.Entries = map[string]json.RawMessage{}
309			}
310		case errors.Is(scanErr, sql.ErrNoRows):
311			// No index yet (chat never used in this workspace) — start a fresh one.
312		default:
313			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read chat session index: %w", scanErr)
314		}
315	
316		entryJSON, err := json.Marshal(entry)
317		if err != nil {
318			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal index entry: %w", err)
319		}
320		index.Entries[entry.SessionID] = entryJSON
321	
322		indexJSON, err := json.Marshal(index)
323		if err != nil {
324			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal chat session index: %w", err)
325		}
326	
327		if _, err := db.Exec(
328			"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO ItemTable (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
329			chatSessionIndexKey, string(indexJSON),
330		); err != nil {
331			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write chat session index: %w", err)
332		}
333		return nil
334	}
335

1	//go:build darwin

5	import (
6		"math"
7		"os"
8		"strconv"
9		"syscall"
10	)
11	
12	// workspaceIDStatSalt returns the salt Cursor mixes into a local folder's workspace
13	// storage ID on macOS: the folder's birthtime in milliseconds. Rounded to the nearest
14	// millisecond to match Node's fs.Stats#birthtime.getTime() as Cursor computes it —
15	// verified against real workspaceStorage entries, where truncation is off by one.
16	// Empty when the salt can't be derived, mirroring Cursor's own fallback of hashing
17	// the bare path.
18	func workspaceIDStatSalt(info os.FileInfo) string {
19		stat, ok := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
20		if !ok {
21			return ""
22		}
23		ts := stat.Birthtimespec
24		ms := ts.Sec*1000 + int64(math.Round(float64(ts.Nsec)/1e6))
25		if ms == 0 {
26			return ""
27		}
28		return strconv.FormatInt(ms, 10)
29	}
30

1	package spi
2	
3	import (
4		"database/sql"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"strings"
8	
9		_ "modernc.org/sqlite" // Pure Go SQLite driver
10	)
11	
12	// BusyTimeoutPragma is appended to SQLite DSNs so each new connection waits for a
13	// briefly-held lock instead of failing immediately with SQLITE_BUSY. The agent that
14	// owns the database may be running and writing to it (e.g. during a checkpoint), so
15	// without a busy timeout a read or a journal-mode change can fail on a transient lock.
16	const BusyTimeoutPragma = "_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)"
17	
18	// EnsureWALMode ensures the database is running in WAL journal mode. WAL lets our
19	// read-only connections and the owning agent's writer proceed concurrently without
20	// blocking each other, and guarantees the -wal file exists for watchers that rely
21	// on fsnotify events. This must open a read-write connection because PRAGMA
22	// journal_mode cannot change the mode on a read-only connection. It is intended to
23	// be called once per database, not on every read.
24	func EnsureWALMode(dbPath string) error {
25		// Open read-write to be able to change journal mode. mode=rw (not the
26		// default create-if-missing) so a wrong path errors instead of leaving a
27		// stray empty database behind; the file: scheme is required because the
28		// driver only honors mode= on URI-form DSNs.
29		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?mode=rw&"+BusyTimeoutPragma)
30		if err != nil {
31			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open database for WAL check: %w", err)
32		}
33		defer func() {
34			if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
35				slog.Warn("Failed to close database after WAL check", "error", closeErr)
36			}
37		}()
38	
39		// Check current journal mode
40		var currentMode string
41		if err := db.QueryRow("PRAGMA journal_mode").Scan(&currentMode); err != nil {
42			return fmt.Errorf("failed to query journal mode: %w", err)
43		}
44	
45		if strings.EqualFold(currentMode, "wal") {
46			slog.Debug("Database already in WAL mode", "path", dbPath)
47			return nil
48		}
49	
50		// Switch to WAL mode. QueryRow rather than Exec because the pragma returns
51		// the resulting mode as a row; checking it catches a silent failure to switch.
52		var newMode string
53		if err := db.QueryRow("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL").Scan(&newMode); err != nil {
54			return fmt.Errorf("failed to set WAL mode: %w", err)
55		}
56	
57		if !strings.EqualFold(newMode, "wal") {
58			return fmt.Errorf("failed to enable WAL mode: got %q instead", newMode)
59		}
60	
61		slog.Info("Enabled WAL mode on database", "path", dbPath)
62		return nil
63	}
64

10	// GetWorkspaceStoragePath returns the workspace storage directory path for the given
11	// application data directory name ("Code" for VS Code, "Code - Insiders" for Insiders).
12	// Returns empty string if the directory doesn't exist
13	func GetWorkspaceStoragePath(dataDirName string) string {
14		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
15		if err != nil {
16			return ""
17		}
18	
19		var storagePath string
20		switch runtime.GOOS {
21		case "darwin":
22			// macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/<dataDirName>/User/workspaceStorage/
23			storagePath = filepath.Join(homeDir, "Library", "Application Support", dataDirName, "User", "workspaceStorage")
24		case "linux":
25			// Linux: ~/.config/<dataDirName>/User/workspaceStorage/
26			storagePath = filepath.Join(homeDir, ".config", dataDirName, "User", "workspaceStorage")
27		default:
28			return ""
29		}
30	
31		// Check if directory exists
32		if _, err := os.Stat(storagePath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
33			return ""
34		}
35	
36		return storagePath
37	}

@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@
 ### 🐛 Bug Fixes
 
 - The Codex CLI provider no longer holds an open file descriptor for every historical Codex session file during `specstory run` and `specstory watch` on macOS. File watches are now limited to a trailing 7-day window of session directories (plus the directory of a resumed session), and watches that age out of the window are released at day rollover, so file descriptor usage stays flat no matter how long a watch runs. Previously, installs with a large Codex session history could pin tens of thousands of descriptors per process and exhaust the system-wide file table, [issue 266](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/266). All historical sessions are still scanned and synced at startup and during `specstory sync`, as before.
-- The Claude Code provider no longer hold an open file descriptor for every historical Claude Code session file during `specstory run` and `specstory watch` on macOS. Session files modified within the trailing 7-day window are watched individually, and a periodic self-healing pass picks up new session files and re-watches dormant sessions the moment they become active again. Even a session idle for longer than the window resumes live markdown updates within seconds. Sessions are still fully covered at startup and during `specstory sync`, as before.
+- The Claude Code provider no longer holds an open file descriptor for every historical Claude Code session file during `specstory run` and `specstory watch` on macOS. Session files modified within the trailing 7-day window are watched individually, and a periodic self-healing pass picks up new session files and re-watches dormant sessions the moment they become active again. Even a session idle for longer than the window resumes live markdown updates within seconds. Sessions are still fully covered at startup and during `specstory sync`, as before.

//go:build linux

package cursoride

import (
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"syscall"
)

// workspaceIDStatSalt returns the salt Cursor mixes into a local folder's workspace
// storage ID on Linux: the folder's inode number (Cursor/VS Code uses stat.ino there;
// see getSingleFolderWorkspaceIdentifier in Cursor's main.js). Empty when the salt
// can't be derived, mirroring Cursor's own fallback of hashing the bare path.
func workspaceIDStatSalt(info os.FileInfo) string {
	stat, ok := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	if stat.Ino == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return strconv.FormatUint(stat.Ino, 10)
}

// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
//
// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
//
// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
type GlobalSessionRef struct {
	SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
	CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
	Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
	Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
	NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
	OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
}

// PathSessionReader is an OPTIONAL capability a Provider may implement: parse a single
// session directly from its already-known native file path, skipping the by-id discovery
// search that GetAgentChatSession performs.
//
// Why: some providers locate a session by scanning their native store. Codex's by-id
// lookup walks the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree on every call, so resolving N sessions
// that way is O(N²). reindex already holds each session's exact file path
// (GlobalSessionRef.NativePath) from enumeration, so a path-keyed parse turns that back
// into O(N). reindex prefers this when a provider implements it and the ref carries a
// NativePath, and falls back to GetAgentChatSession otherwise.
//
// originCwd is the session's originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd),
// passed through as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath.
type PathSessionReader interface {
	GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)
}

// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.
type ScanReporter struct {
	found atomic.Int64
}

// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
// sessions rather than raw files.

// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
//
// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
	// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
	var paths []string
	walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
		}
		if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
			return nil
		}
		paths = append(paths, path)
		return nil
	})
	if walkErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
	}

	// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.

135	// firstWorkspaceResult picks the single workspace result to render. Only one workspace's
136	// results are shown (multi-root workspaces are rare), and taking the lexicographically
137	// smallest key keeps the choice deterministic — Go randomizes map iteration order, so
138	// ranging over the map would render a different workspace on different runs.
139	func firstWorkspaceResult(success *GrepSuccess) *GrepWorkspaceResult {
140		if success == nil || len(success.WorkspaceResults) == 0 {
141			return nil
142		}
143		keys := make([]string, 0, len(success.WorkspaceResults))
144		for key := range success.WorkspaceResults {
145			keys = append(keys, key)
146		}
147		sort.Strings(keys)
148		return success.WorkspaceResults[keys[0]]
149	}

151	// formatContentResults formats content matches as a markdown table
152	func (h *GrepHandler) formatContentResults(content *GrepContentResult) string {
153		if len(content.Matches) == 0 {
154			return "\n_No matches found_"
155		}
156	
157		// Check if we have file names in the results
158		hasFiles := false
159		for _, fileMatch := range content.Matches {
160			if fileMatch.File != "" {
161				hasFiles = true
162				break
163			}
164		}
165	
166		var result strings.Builder
167	
168		// Build table header
169		if hasFiles {
170			result.WriteString("\n| File | Content | Line |\n|------|------|------|\n")
171		} else {
172			result.WriteString("\n| Content | Line |\n|------|------|\n")
173		}
174	
175		// Build table rows
176		for _, fileMatch := range content.Matches {
177			for _, match := range fileMatch.Matches {
178				// Skip context lines
179				if match.IsContextLine {
180					continue
181				}
182				// Skip matches without content (empty lines)
183				if match.Content == "" {
184					continue
185				}
186	
187				// Add file column if needed
188				if hasFiles {
189					fmt.Fprintf(&result, "| `%s` ", escapeTableCellValue(fileMatch.File))
190				}
191	
192				// Add content and line number
193				fmt.Fprintf(&result, "| `%s` | L%d |\n",
194					escapeTableCellValue(match.Content),
195					match.LineNumber)
196			}
197		}
198	
199		return result.String()
200	}

205			return "\n_No matches found_"
206		}
207	
208		var result strings.Builder
209		result.WriteString("\n| File |\n|------|\n")
210	
211		for _, file := range files.Files {
212			// Escape the DB-sourced name so pipes/newlines can't break the table
213			fmt.Fprintf(&result, "| `%s` |\n", escapeTableCellValue(file))
214		}

224	// escapeTableCellValue escapes special characters for markdown table cells.
225	// Matches the TypeScript escapeTableCellValue function, plus backtick escaping:
226	// callers wrap cell values in `...` code spans, and grep results contain source
227	// code lines where backticks are common (markdown, JS template literals), which
228	// would otherwise terminate the span and corrupt the table. The TS extension has
229	// the same flaw; &#96; renders back as a literal backtick in HTML-capable viewers.
230	func escapeTableCellValue(value string) string {
231		// Escape pipes
232		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, "|", "\\|")
233		// Escape backticks so values survive being wrapped in `...` code spans
234		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, "`", "&#96;")
235		// Convert newlines to HTML breaks
236		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, "\n", "<br/>")
237		// Escape braces (for some markdown parsers)
238		value = escapeBraces(value)
239		// Normalize tabs to spaces
240		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, "\t", "    ")
241		// Remove carriage returns
242		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, "\r", "")
243		// Trim whitespace
244		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
245	
246		return value
247	}
248	
249	// escapeBraces escapes curly braces in markdown.
250	//
251	// Why count backslashes: a brace is only already escaped when preceded by an odd
252	// number of backslashes. Looking at just the previous character mistakes an
253	// escaped backslash ("\\{") for an escaped brace and leaves the brace unescaped.
254	func escapeBraces(s string) string {
255		var result strings.Builder
256		backslashCount := 0
257	
258		for _, char := range s {
259			switch char {
260			case '\\':
261				backslashCount++
262			case '{', '}':
263				// An even count (including zero) means the brace is not yet escaped.
264				if backslashCount%2 == 0 {
265					result.WriteRune('\\')
266				}
267				backslashCount = 0
268			default:
269				backslashCount = 0
270			}
271			result.WriteRune(char)
272		}
273	
274		return result.String()

package cursoride

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
)

// ReadFileHandler handles read_file and read_file_v2 tool invocations
type ReadFileHandler struct{}

// ReadFileParams represents the parameters for read_file tool
type ReadFileParams struct {
	RelativeWorkspacePath string `json:"relativeWorkspacePath,omitempty"`
	TargetFile            string `json:"targetFile,omitempty"`
}

// AdaptMessage formats the read_file tool invocation as markdown
func (h *ReadFileHandler) AdaptMessage(bubble *BubbleConversation) (summary string, body string, err error) {
	// Parse params to get the file path
	var params ReadFileParams
	if bubble.Params != "" {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(bubble.Params), &params); err != nil {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse read_file params: %w", err)
		}
	}

	// Get the file path (prefer relativeWorkspacePath, fallback to targetFile)
	filePath := params.RelativeWorkspacePath
	if filePath == "" {
		filePath = params.TargetFile
	}

	// Matches the TypeScript implementation's summary text; there's no body content.

func (h *ListDirectoryHandler) AdaptMessage(bubble *BubbleConversation) (summary string, body string, err error) {
	// Parse raw args to get the directory path
	var rawArgs ListDirectoryRawArgs
	if bubble.RawArgs != "" {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(bubble.RawArgs), &rawArgs); err != nil {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse list_directory rawArgs: %w", err)
		}
	}

	// Parse result to get the file list
	var result ListDirectoryResult
	if bubble.Result != "" {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(bubble.Result), &result); err != nil {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse list_directory result: %w", err)
		}
	}

	filesLength := len(result.Files)

	// Format the workspace path display
	relativeWorkspacePath := rawArgs.RelativeWorkspacePath
	workspaceDisplay := "current directory"
	if relativeWorkspacePath != "" && relativeWorkspacePath != "." {
		workspaceDisplay = fmt.Sprintf("directory %s", relativeWorkspacePath)
	}

	// Build the summary line
	pluralSuffix := ""
	if filesLength != 1 {
		pluralSuffix = "s"
	}
	summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** • Listed %s, %d result%s", escapeSummaryText(bubble.Name), escapeSummaryText(workspaceDisplay), filesLength, pluralSuffix)

	if filesLength == 0 {
		body = "No results found"
	} else {
		// Add table header
		message := "| Name |\n|-------|\n"

		// Add table rows
		for _, file := range result.Files {
			icon := "📄"
			if file.IsDirectory {
				icon = "📁"
			}
			// Escape the DB-sourced name so pipes/newlines can't break the table
			message += fmt.Sprintf("| %s `%s` |\n", icon, escapeTableCellValue(file.Name))
		}
		body = message
	}

	return summary, body, nil
}

215	// The algorithm works by walking the path component by component, starting from the root.
216	// For each component, it opens the parent directory and reads its actual entries,
217	// performing case-insensitive matching to find the correct casing on disk.
218	// This ensures that the returned path matches the real filesystem casing, which is
219	// important for consistent hashing and avoiding subtle bugs on case-insensitive filesystems.
220	//
221	// Note: This can be slow for long paths or directories with many entries, since it
222	// requires reading each directory's contents.
223	//
224	// If a component doesn't exist on disk, the remaining path components are
225	// appended as-is, making this function safe to use with paths that don't
226	// fully exist yet.
227	func GetCanonicalPath(p string) (string, error) {
228		// Ensure we have an absolute, clean path
229		p = filepath.Clean(p)
230		if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
231			var err error
232			p, err = filepath.Abs(p)
233			if err != nil {
234				return "", err
235			}
236		}
237	
238		// Resolve any symlinks in the path to get the real physical path
239		// This is critical for ensuring consistent path hashing across different
240		// ways of accessing the same directory (e.g., through a symlink vs directly)
241		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(p)
242		if err == nil && realPath != p {
243			// Successfully resolved symlinks - update p to the resolved path for case normalization
244			p = realPath
245		} else if err != nil {
246			// Symlink resolution failed (e.g., path doesn't exist yet),
247			// continue with the original path - we'll still normalize the case below
248			slog.Debug("GetCanonicalPath: symlink resolution failed, using original path",
249				"path", p, "error", err)
250		}
251	
252		// Split into components
253		parts := strings.Split(p, string(os.PathSeparator))
254	
255		// Start with root
256		result := string(os.PathSeparator)
257	
258		// Skip empty first element (before leading /) that results from splitting "/foo/bar"
259		firstPartIndex := 1
260	
261		// Build path component by component
262		for i := firstPartIndex; i < len(parts); i++ {
263			if parts[i] == "" {
264				continue
265			}
266	
267			// Open current result directory to read its contents
268			f, err := os.Open(result)
269			if err != nil {
270				// Can't read directory - might not exist yet
271				// Append remaining path as-is
272				return appendRemainingParts(result, parts, i), nil
273			}

27	// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
28	// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
29	// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
30	// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
31	//
32	// Parameters:
33	//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
34	//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
35	//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
36	//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
37	//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
38	//
39	// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
40	// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
41	func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
42		slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)
43	
44		// Track a per-provider, per-session content fingerprint to suppress duplicate callbacks.
45		// Providers fire callbacks on every session-file change, but not all changes
46		// produce new content in the parsed SessionData (e.g. UI metadata updates).
47		// The message count alone is not enough: patch-log providers (e.g. VS Code
48		// Copilot) stream an agent response by growing the text of an existing
49		// message in place, so the count stays flat while the content changes.
50		var mu sync.Mutex
51		lastFingerprint := make(map[string]sessionFingerprint)
52	
53		var wg sync.WaitGroup
54		errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))
55	
56		for providerID, provider := range providers {
57			wg.Add(1)
58			go func() {
59				defer wg.Done()
60	
61				slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())
62	
63				// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
64				wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
65					if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
66						return
67					}
68	
69					fingerprint := fingerprintSession(session)
70	
71					// Key by provider as well as session: the map is shared across all
72					// provider goroutines, and without the scope two providers emitting
73					// the same session ID would suppress each other's callbacks.
74					dedupKey := providerID + "/" + session.SessionID
75	
76					// Skip if the parsed content hasn't changed for this session
77					mu.Lock()
78					prev, seen := lastFingerprint[dedupKey]
79					if seen && prev == fingerprint {
80						mu.Unlock()
81						slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
82							"providerID", providerID,
83							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
84							"messages", fingerprint.messages,
85							"contentBytes", fingerprint.contentBytes)
86						return
87					}
88					lastFingerprint[dedupKey] = fingerprint
89					mu.Unlock()
90	
91					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
92						"providerID", providerID,
93						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
94						"messages", fingerprint.messages,
95						"contentBytes", fingerprint.contentBytes)
96	
97					sessionCallback(providerID, session)
98				}
99	
100				err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
101				if err != nil {
102					// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
103					if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
104						slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
105						errChan <- nil
106					} else {
107						slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
108						errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
109					}
110				} else {
111					errChan <- nil
112				}
113			}()
114		}
115	
116		// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
117		wg.Wait()
118	
119		// Drain error channel — errors are already logged in the goroutines with full context
120		for range len(providers) {
121			<-errChan
122		}
123	
124		return nil
125	}

127	// sessionFingerprint summarizes the parsed content of a session for callback
128	// deduplication. Comparable by value.
129	type sessionFingerprint struct {
130		messages     int // total messages across all exchanges
131		contentBytes int // total bytes of message text, tool summaries, and pre-rendered tool markdown
132	}
133	
134	// fingerprintSession computes the dedup fingerprint for a session. Content size
135	// is tracked alongside the message count because a streaming agent response can
136	// grow the text of an existing message without adding new messages.
137	func fingerprintSession(session *spi.AgentChatSession) sessionFingerprint {
138		var fp sessionFingerprint
139		for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
140			fp.messages += len(exchange.Messages)
141			for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
142				for _, part := range msg.Content {
143					fp.contentBytes += len(part.Text)
144				}
145				if msg.Tool != nil {
146					// The summary is rendered content too (markdown <summary> tag), and a
147					// provider can update it alone — e.g. when a running tool completes —
148					// without growing any message text or formatted markdown.
149					if msg.Tool.Summary != nil {
150						fp.contentBytes += len(*msg.Tool.Summary)
151					}
152					if msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil {
153						fp.contentBytes += len(*msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown)
154					}
155				}
156			}
157		}
158		return fp
159	}

687					if err != nil {

695						}

699	
700				if session == nil {

702						fmt.Printf("❌ Session '%s' not found in any provider\n", sessionID)
703					}

## 1. SPI contract

Interface at `pkg/spi/provider.go:61-154`. `cursoride.Provider` is a stateless empty struct (`provider.go:20`), constructed by `NewProvider()` (`provider.go:23`).

| SPI method | Impl | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Name() string` | `provider.go:28` | `"Cursor IDE"` |
| `Check(customCommand)` | `provider.go:33` | Ignores `customCommand`; probes global DB path + opens it. Returns `Version: ""` deliberately (`provider.go:82-84`) — no placeholder version. Emits analytics on both branches. |
| `DetectAgent(path, helpOutput)` | `provider.go:91` | workspaces → composer IDs → bool; prints two distinct help blocks (no workspace vs workspace-but-no-composers) at `:108` and `:127` |
| `GetAgentChatSessions(path, debugRaw, progress)` | `provider.go:172` | Uses shared `loadProjectComposers` (`:146`). Progress counts *every* composer incl. skipped/failed so the bar reaches total (`:203-208`) |
| `GetAgentChatSession(path, id, debugRaw)` | `provider.go:253` | Deliberately does *not* share the bulk preamble — membership check first, then loads only the one composer (`:249-252`, step comments `:259-333`). Returns `(nil, nil)` for not-found/empty, never an error |
| `ListAgentChatSessions(path)` | `provider.go:343` | Returns empty slice (not error) when no workspace |
| `ExecAgentAndWatch(...)` | `provider.go:465` | IDE-specific: no child process to wait on. Opens Cursor, installs `signal.NotifyContext` (`:481`), retries `WatchAgent` every 5s until the workspace entry exists (`:488-504`) |
| `WatchAgent(ctx, ...)` | `provider.go:548` | Constructs watcher, `Start()`, blocks on `<-ctx.Done()`, `Stop()` |
| `ReconstructSession` | `reconstruct.go:36` | See §4 |
| `NativeSessionPath` | `reconstruct.go:250` | Returns a temp sentinel path (`os.TempDir()/specstory-cursor-<id>`) — Cursor has no per-session files |
| `SupportsReconstruction` | `reconstruct.go:256` | `true` |
| `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` | `provider.go:394` | Global enumeration for `reindex`. `NativePath` = the shared global DB for every ref; `OriginCwd` prefers embedded `workspaceIdentifier.uri.fsPath`, falls back to the workspace-DB scan (`:417-427`) |

**Optional interfaces NOT implemented** (verified by grep):

## 2. Workspace detection / selection

### Storage roots (`path_utils.go`)
- Global DB: `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` (darwin, `:25`) / `~/.config/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` (linux, `:27`). **Windows returns an explicit "unsupported operating system" error** (`:29`, `:61`).
- Workspace storage: `.../User/workspaceStorage/` (`:56`, `:59`).
- Both are `var`s (`:13`, `:43`) delegating to unexported impls, so tests can point at temp dirs.

### Matching (`FindAllWorkspacesForProject`, `workspace.go:250-407`)
Walks each `workspaceStorage/<hash>/`, reads `workspace.json` (`readWorkspaceJSON`, `:618`), prefers `workspace` (multi-root `.code-workspace` URI) over `folder` (`:304-310`), converts URI→path, then applies **four** match methods:
1. **Direct canonical path equality** (`:328`)
2. **Basename fallback, remote-only** (`:336-348`) — gated by `isRemoteURIRequiringBasenameMatch` (`:419`), which allows `vscode-remote://ssh-remote`, `tunnel`, `dev-container` and **deliberately excludes WSL** (WSL paths are locally reachable). Explicit rationale that basename matching for local workspaces would cross-contaminate two different `backend/` folders (`:331-335`). Case-insensitive prefix check, matching `parseVSCodeRemoteURI` (`:410-412`).
3. **`.code-workspace` file lists our folder** (`codeWorkspaceContainsFolder`, `:354-362`, `:708`)
4. **Project path *is* a `.code-workspace`** and the entry was opened on one of its folders (`:366-377`, pre-collected at `:266-268` via `collectCodeWorkspaceFolders`, `:661`, which resolves relative folder paths against the workspace file dir)

Entries without a `state.vscdb` are skipped (`:380-383`). Zero matches → error.

### Path normalization (`normalizePathForComparison`, `workspace.go:90-129`)
- Windows UNC WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\`, `\\wsl$\`) → Unix (`isWindowsWSLUNCPath :52`, `normalizeWindowsWSLPath :61`, strips distro segment)
- Unix-style paths on Windows preserved verbatim, **never through `filepath.Abs`** which would prepend a drive letter (`isUnixStylePathOnWindows :34`, handles both `/home/...` and `\home\...` forms, excludes UNC `\\`)
- Otherwise `filepath.Abs` + `spi.GetCanonicalPath` (`pkg/spi/path_utils.go:227`) which does **symlink resolution + per-component case normalization**, degrading gracefully for non-existent components. Failure → warn + use abs path (`:121-126`).

### URI parsing
- `uriToPath` (`:647`): `vscode-remote://` handled locally (Go's `url.Parse` rejects `%2B` in host); everything else delegated to shared `spi.FileURIToPath` (`pkg/spi/path_utils.go:387`) so all providers translate `file://` identically.
- `parseVSCodeRemoteURI` (`:723`): manual host/path split, `url.PathUnescape` on both, allow-list `{wsl, ssh-remote, tunnel, dev-container}` bare or `+suffix`, case-insensitive; per-type debug logging.
- `pathToFileURI` (`:637`): uses `url.URL{Scheme:"file", Path:...}` so spaces percent-encode the way Cursor writes them — raw concatenation would mis-associate.

### Single-workspace selection & minting
- `FindWorkspaceForProject` (`var` at `:133`, impl `:141`) delegates to the all-matches finder, then breaks ties by **`state.vscdb` mtime** (most recently used), not directory order (`:154-168`, `workspaceDBModTime :236` returns zero time on stat failure so it loses the tie).
- `EnsureWorkspaceForProject` (`:178`) **mints** a workspace entry when the folder was never opened: computes Cursor's own ID = `md5(rawPath + statSalt)` (`cursorWorkspaceID :223`), creates the dir, writes 2-space-indented `workspace.json`, and creates an empty `state.vscdb` with VS Code's exact `ItemTable` schema (`database.go:46`). Salt is platform-specific: macOS birthtime in ms **rounded** to match Node's `getTime()` (`workspace_id_darwin.go:18-28`), Linux inode (`workspace_id_linux.go:14`). Note the deliberate non-normalization: the path is hashed exactly as given because Cursor mints distinct entries per literal spelling (`workspace.go:220-222`).

### Session↔project association (`FindProjectComposerIDs`, `workspace.go:445`)
Merges **two** sources:
1. Workspace-DB keys (`composer.composerData` + `workbench.panel.composerChatViewPane*`) — Cursor 2 / early 3 (`LoadComposerIDsFromAllWorkspaces :515`)
2. `workspaceIdentifier` embedded in each global `composerData` row — the **only live** association in Cursor ≥ 3.12 (`composerBelongsToProject :493`; matches by workspace storage ID *or* canonical fsPath)

Degrades to source 1 if the global scan fails (`:450-452`). `projectComposerIDs` (`:460`) is the load-free core so the watcher can reuse an already-scanned map instead of scanning twice.

`ScanAllWorkspaceComposerPaths` (`:544`) / `scanWorkspaceDirForComposerPaths` (`:557`, split out for tests): composerID → project path, first-seen wins, unreadable workspaces skipped individually.

## 3. Database access patterns (`database.go`)

- **Driver**: `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go, `:13`).
- **Read-only opens**: `OpenDatabase` (`:25`) → DSN `path?mode=ro&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)` via shared `spi.BusyTimeoutPragma` (`pkg/spi/sqlite.go:16`). **No copy-first**; reads go against the live file.
- **FD hygiene**: `SetMaxOpenConns(1)`, `SetMaxIdleConns(1)`, `SetConnMaxLifetime(30s)` on *both* read (`:34-36`) and read-write (`:337-339`) opens, explicitly commented as preventing FD accumulation. Every `db.Close()` and `rows.Close()` is deferred with a logged error (`:51`, `:77`, `:144`, `:186`, `:239`, `:404`, `:465`, `:650`, `:784`, `:794`). This mirrors the repo-wide FD-exhaustion fixes (`0047fd6` Codex, `47a9874` Claude Code, issue #266).
- **WAL**: not set on plain reads. `spi.EnsureWALMode` (`pkg/spi/sqlite.go:24`) is called once at watcher startup for every workspace DB + the global DB (`watcher.go:141-150`) and inside `OpenDatabaseReadWrite` (`database.go:330`). WAL is required so a `-wal` file exists for fsnotify.
- **Batching**: `composerBatchSize = 200` (`:20`) because each ID contributes two expressions and SQLite caps expression depth at ~1000. `LoadComposerDataBatch` (`:177`) chunks, one query per chunk (`loadComposerChunk :211`) selecting both `composerData:<id>` (IN) and `bubbleId:<id>:%` (LIKE), then `assembleComposerConversations` (`:284`) merges bubbles — header-ordered for Cursor 3, field-by-field merge into the inline array for Cursor 2 (`:298-321`).
- **Lightweight scan**: `LoadAllComposerDataLightweight` (`:779`) reads only `composerData:%` rows — used by `ListAllAgentChatSessions`, `FindProjectComposerIDs`, and watcher seeding.
- **Workspace DB reads**: `LoadWorkspaceComposerIDs` (`:72`) with two methods; method 2 (`loadPanelComposerIDs :136`) extracts UUIDs from `workbench.panel.aichat.view.{uuid}` keys, excluding `%.hidden`. All parse/scan failures log-and-continue for a partial result.
- **Writes** (reconstruction only): `InsertComposerSession` (`:349`) in a single transaction with unconditional deferred `Rollback` (documented no-op after Commit, `:354-356`), `INSERT OR REPLACE` for idempotency. Read-modify-write with raw-JSON preservation of unknown fields in `AppendToSelectedComposerIDs` (`:399`), `WriteGlobalComposerHeader` (`:459`), `RegisterGlassProjectMembership` (`:645`). Explicit `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` after sidebar writes so Cursor doesn't read a pre-write snapshot (`:576-581`, `:763-767`).
- **Version probing**: `insertComposerHeaderRow` (`:589`) checks `sqlite_master` for the `composerHeaders` table and skips silently on pre-3.12 Cursor.

### Watcher I/O strategy (`watcher.go`)
- **fsnotify on the parent directory, not the files** (`watchDatabaseFiles :272`) — long comment at `:263-271` explaining that WAL files are deleted/recreated so a file watch dies with the inode. `watchedDBPaths` + `isWatchedDBFile` (`:290`) filter directory events down to `state.vscdb` and `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal` siblings, ignoring `workspace.json`. Written before the goroutine launches, read-only after, so no lock needed (`:44-49`).
- **Debounce/throttle**: `throttleDuration = 10s` (`:115`), `triggerCheck` (`:349`) either runs immediately or sets `pendingCheck` and schedules one deferred run (`:363-387`); `executePendingCheck` (`:412`) re-verifies the window. `lastThrottledCall` deliberately starts at the **zero value**, not `time.Now()` — comment at `:116-120` documents a bug where seeding it doubled startup latency.
- **Safety-net poll**: `defaultCheckInterval = 2m` (`:19`) via `safetyNetPoller` (`:331`); initial check at +5s via a stored `time.AfterFunc` timer that `Stop()` cancels (`:182-184`, `:232-234`).
- **Concurrency guard**: `checking sync.Mutex` with `TryLock` for normal triggers (skip if a check is running) but a blocking `Lock` for `"shutdown"` so the final flush is never skipped (`:432-443`, rationale `:60-63`).

---

## 4. Session data handling

- **Session ID** = `composer.ComposerID` verbatim (`agent_session.go:18`, `provider.go:600`).
- **CreatedAt**: `composer.CreatedAt` ms → `time.Unix(sec, ms*1e6).Format(RFC3339)`, falling back to `time.Now()` (`agent_session.go:22-28`). Deliberately **local time, not UTC**, so the same session yields an identical string in all three producers — noted at `provider.go:435-436`.
- **Slug**: `generateSlug` (`agent_session.go:217`) over `composerNameCandidates` (`:200` — composer name, then first user message), via shared `spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage`; falls back to the composer ID. `generateCursorIDESessionName` (`provider.go:629`) uses the same candidate list with `spi.GenerateReadableName`, so slug and name never diverge in source.
- **Markdown feed**: providers do **not** generate markdown. `SessionData` (`schema.SessionData`) is built with `Provider{ID:"cursoride", Name:"Cursor IDE", Version:"unknown"}` (`agent_session.go:36-40`), `WorkspaceRoot` threaded from the caller's project path (`:44`, documented as the cross-provider convention), and exchanges. `RawData` = `json.Marshal(composer)` (`:177`).
- **Exchange grouping**: a new exchange starts on each user bubble (`:157-160`); `ExchangeID` assigned post-loop as `sessionID:index` (`:172-174`) rather than derived from a bubble ID, explicitly to match other providers and to be always non-empty.
- **Content parts**: thinking emitted as a dedicated `ContentTypeThinking` part **before** text (`:86-91`) so the shared renderer owns its presentation; tool markdown lives only in `message.Tool` and is suppressed from `Content` via the `toolHandledSeparately` flag (`buildMessageText :253`) to avoid double rendering.
- **Model**: only on agent bubbles (`type==2`), bubble `ModelInfo` then composer `ModelConfig` fallback (`:127-135`). Mode (`Ask`/`Agent`/`Plan`/`Custom`) into `Metadata["mode"]` for agent bubbles only (`:148-153`, `unifiedModeToString :426`).
- **Per-bubble timestamps** (`calculateTimestamp :386`): handles Cursor's mixed absolute/relative `clientStartTime` (threshold `946684800000` = Y2K); relative form recovered as `clientEndTime - clientStartTime` using `ClientRpcSendTime` → `ClientSettleTime` → `ClientEndTime` in priority order. User bubbles with no timestamp inherit the next assistant bubble's (`:111-125`, matching the TS extension).
- **Empty filtering**: composers with `len(Conversation)==0` skipped in all three readers (`provider.go:212`, `:314`, `:371`) and in `ListAll` (checks conversation *and* headers, `provider.go:430`). Per-bubble: `isEmptyCapabilityBubble` (`agent_session.go:230`) skips content-free capability bubbles but never tool bubbles (type 15) or plain content (type 0); a second guard skips bubbles that produced no parts and no tool (`:101-106`).
- **Incremental updates** (watcher, `watcher.go:477-621`): watermark map `knownComposers[composerID] = lastUpdatedAt` (falling back to `createdAt`), seeded at startup by `seedKnownComposers` (`:195`) so historical sessions aren't re-emitted. Two race guards:
  1. header count > loaded bubble count ⇒ bubbles not yet committed, skip without advancing the watermark (`:518-527`, logged at Debug because it fires routinely during streaming)
  2. last bubble is a user message ⇒ agent hasn't replied; tracked in `pendingIncomplete` and retried, but force-processed after `incompleteTimeout = 60s` so markdown is never lost (`:542-576`)
  Watermark is advanced **only after successful conversion** (`:590-594`) so failures retry instead of poisoning.
- **Debug output**: `writeDebugOutput` (`provider.go:574`) writes `raw-composer.json` into `spi.GetDebugDir(sessionID)`; failures warn but never fail the operation (`:232-235`, `:329-332`, `watcher.go:597-603`).

### Reconstruction (`reconstruct.go`)
`spi.PrepareTurns` → new UUID composer ID → one bubble + one header per turn with `grouping.isRenderable=true` (mandatory, `:85-91`) → a large literal `composerMap` (`:98-188`) with `_v: 17` and visibility-critical fields (`hasLoaded`, `isDraft`, `status`, `isAgentic`, `unifiedMode`, `workspaceIdentifier`) → `InsertComposerSession` → `WriteGlobalComposerHeader` (pre-3.12 sidebar) → `RegisterGlassProjectMembership` (≥3.12 sidebar, `glass.localAgentProjects.v1` / `glass.localAgentProjectMembership.v1`, `database.go:620-623`) → best-effort `AppendToSelectedComposerIDs` (warn-only, UX nicety). Returns empty `Content` because the write already happened.

## 5. Tool call handling

`tool_handlers.go` defines `ToolType` (`read/write/search/shell/task/mcp/generic/unknown`, `:15-23`), the `ToolHandler` interface returning **(summary, body)** with an explicit contract that handlers must *not* emit the `<details>`/`<summary>` wrapper (`:27-37`), and a name→handler `ToolRegistry` allowing many names per handler (`:41-112`).

**Registered tools (`NewToolRegistry`, `:46-102`):**

| Handler | Type | Tool names | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReadFileHandler` | read | `read_file`, `read_file_v2` | `tool_read_file.go:18` (summary only, no body) |
| `CodeEditHandler` | write | `edit_file`, `MultiEdit`, `edit_notebook`, `reapply`, `search_replace`, `write`, `edit_file_v2` | `tool_write.go:36` (instructions, status, apply-failed, per-chunk `@@` diff fences, `edit_file_v2` codeblock fallback) |
| `DeleteFileHandler` | write | `delete_file` | `tool_write.go:115` |
| `ApplyPatchHandler` | write | `apply_patch` | `tool_write.go:148` |
| `ShellCommandHandler` | shell | `run_terminal_cmd`, `run_terminal_command`, `run_terminal_command_v2` | `tool_shell.go:28` (bash fence for command uncapped, output capped) |
| `GrepHandler` | search | `grep`, `ripgrep` | `tool_grep.go:67` (markdown tables; deterministic workspace pick via `firstWorkspaceResult :139`) |
| `GrepSearchHandler` | search | `grep_search` | `tool_grep_search.go:56` |
| `ListDirectoryHandler` | search* | `list_directory` | `tool_list_directory.go:28` (📄/📁 table) |
| `FileSearchHandler` | search | `file_search` | `tool_file_search.go:31` |
| `GlobFileSearchHandler` | search | `glob_file_search` | `tool_glob_file_search.go:36` |
| `formatCatchAll` | unknown | everything else | `tool_handlers.go:208` (Parameters / Additional data / Result / User decision / Status / Error sections) |

**Two entry points, deliberately split** (`:114-121`):
- `FormatToolContent` (`:122`) → `(summary, body, toolType)` with no wrapper — used by `resolveToolInfo` to populate `schema.ToolInfo{Summary, FormattedMarkdown}`. Handler errors fall back to catch-all with a warn.
- `FormatToolInvocation` (`:151`) → full `<tool-use data-tool-type=… data-tool-name=…><details><summary>…` block — the fallback path when a tool can't be structured (`agent_session.go:329`).

**Error/cancelled/invalid** (`agent_session.go:272-299`): `tool==0` or `status=="error"` → `formatToolError` body (parses `clientVisibleErrorMessage` from the error JSON, `tool_handlers.go:191`); `status=="cancelled"` → `"Cancelled"`. Both still emit structured `ToolInfo` with the **real** registry type preserved via `registeredToolType` (`:304`) — the comment explains cross-agent resume flattens tool calls from `Summary`/`FormattedMarkdown` only, so every tool must carry them.

**V1 vs V3 tool data**: `resolveToolData` (`:314`) — V3+ reads `bubble.ToolFormerData`; V1 reads `capabilitiesMap[capabilityType].ParsedBubbleMap[bubbleID]` (parsed in `parseCapabilities :353`, which handles `bubbleDataMap` being a JSON *string*).

**Type mapping**: `toSchemaToolType` (`:344`) maps `mcp` → `schema.ToolTypeGeneric`; all others pass through.

**Safety helpers** (`tool_handlers.go`): `escapeSummaryText` = `html.EscapeString` applied to every DB-sourced value in summaries and tag attributes (`:186`); `codeFence` (`:306`) sizes fences to longest backtick run + 1 so embedded ``` can't escape; `fencedBlock` (`:298`); `capRunes` (`:329`) rune-safe truncation that scans boundaries instead of allocating `[]rune`; `toolResultCap = 2000` applied to **results only, never inputs** (`:289-293`). `escapeTableCellValue` (`tool_grep.go:230`) escapes pipes, backticks (→`&#96;`), newlines (→`<br/>`), braces, tabs, CRs; `escapeBraces` (`:254`) counts backslashes so `\\{` isn't mistaken for an escaped brace.

## 6. Robustness

- **Error philosophy**: "not found" is `(nil, nil)` or an empty slice, never an error (`provider.go:264`, `:296`, `:310`, `:317`, `:352`). Real failures wrap with `%w`. Per-item failures (bad JSON row, unreadable workspace) log-and-continue so one bad entry never aborts a sweep.
- **Logging**: `log/slog` throughout with structured key/value pairs. Deliberate level discipline — transient mid-write states are `Debug`, not `Warn` (`watcher.go:521-522`, `:551-552`); genuine anomalies (timeout waiting for agent reply) are `Warn` (`:567`); check summaries and lifecycle are `Info`.
- **FD hygiene**: connection-pool caps + lifetime on every open; every `*sql.DB`/`*sql.Rows` closed via deferred closure with logged error; the `checking` mutex exists specifically to stop overlapping checks from multiplying DB connections (`watcher.go:60-63`, `:431`).
- **Context cancellation**: watcher owns its own `context.WithCancel` (`:98`); `WatchAgent` blocks on the caller's ctx and calls `Stop()`. `ExecAgentAndWatch` uses `signal.NotifyContext` for Ctrl-C/SIGTERM.
- **Goroutine lifecycle**: two long-lived goroutines (`handleFileEvents`, `safetyNetPoller`) tracked by `wg`; every check runs in a `wg`-tracked goroutine via `runCheckAsync` (`:400`); callbacks in a separate `callbackWg` with per-callback `recover()` so a panic in markdown/cloud sync can't kill the watcher (`:611-620`). `Stop()` (`:227`) has a carefully ordered shutdown: cancel initial timer → final flush check → close fsnotify → **cancel under `w.mu`** then `wg.Wait()` (the ctx check + `wg.Add` in `triggerCheck`/`runCheckAsync` happen under the same lock, making Add-after-Wait impossible, `:247-254`) → `callbackWg.Wait()`.
- **Fail-fast**: nil `sessionCallback` rejected at construction rather than panicking deep in a check (`watcher.go:74-77`).
- **`#nosec G501`** annotation on the md5 import with justification (`workspace.go:4`).

---

## 7. Other notable items

- **Analytics**: only in `Check` — `EventCheckInstallFailed` with `error_type` of `database_not_found` / `database_open_failed`, and `EventCheckInstallSuccess` with `location` (`provider.go:39`, `:55`, `:75`). No analytics in the read/watch paths.
- **Redaction**: **no provider-level redaction**. It is applied centrally (repo commit `5e1668d` moved secret redaction into cloud-sync artifacts; `4825c65` switched to the Betterleaks lib). Providers just emit content.
- **Reindex**: served by `ListAllAgentChatSessions` only (no `ProgressEnumerator`), with `NativePath` = shared global DB.
- **Version logic**: three distinct Cursor-generation branches, each commented — Cursor 2 (inline `conversation`, `allComposers`), Cursor 3 (`fullConversationHeadersOnly`, `selectedComposerIds`, panel keys), Cursor ≥ 3.12 (embedded `workspaceIdentifier`, `composerHeaders` SQL table, `glass.*` sidebar keys). `Check` intentionally reports no version string.
- **Launching**: `openCursorIDE` (`provider.go:523`) uses only the `cursor` CLI (with a documented reason `open -a Cursor` is *not* a fallback); a sentinel `errCursorCLIMissing` (`:511`) drives install guidance vs a plain error for a misconfigured custom launcher. Custom command split via shared `spi.SplitCommandLine`.
- **Testability seams**: `GetGlobalDatabasePath`, `GetWorkspaceStoragePath`, `FindWorkspaceForProject` are package-level `var`s; `scanWorkspaceDirForComposerPaths` is split from its wrapper for the same reason.

The Cursor IDE inventory is complete and I've read the entire new provider, so here's the full review of PR #160 ("Copilot IDE"), judged against the Cursor IDE provider as the exemplar. Build, `go test ./...` (for the touched packages), and `golangci-lint run` are all clean at the PR head.

## Overall verdict

This is a solid, well-documented provider. The reconstruct/resume path is genuinely excellent — UTF-16 range math, byte-for-byte preservation of unmodeled index entries (with a test proving it), fence-safe markdown, and the honest "restart VS Code" guidance. The JSONL patch-log parser (kind:0/1/2) is careful and well-commented. Where it falls short of the Cursor exemplar is almost entirely in the **watcher's robustness** and a handful of SPI-contract deviations. Nothing here is a blocker for a phase-1 merge, but items 1–3 below will produce real user-visible data gaps in `watch`/`run`.

## Important deviations from the Cursor IDE exemplar

### 1. The watcher can silently drop the final write of a response (watcher.go:102-107)

Cursor's watcher uses a *trailing-edge* throttle: a suppressed trigger sets a `pendingCheck` and schedules a deferred run, plus there's a 2-minute safety-net poll and a 60-second "incomplete session" forcing pass. The Copilot watcher uses a *leading-edge* debounce: any event within 500ms of the last processed one is simply discarded, with no deferred re-read and no safety-net poll. If VS Code's final write for a completed response lands inside that window (very plausible — the stream-end write follows the last content write immediately), the completed answer isn't captured until some future event touches the file, which for the last message of a session may be never. This is the single most important gap: I'd replace the drop with a timer that re-processes the file after the window expires, and/or add a periodic poll like Cursor's.

### 2. `specstory watch` is permanently dead for a project's first-ever chat (workspace.go:167, watcher.go:48)

`WatchAgent` requires the `chatSessions` directory to already exist (`FindWorkspaceForProject` with `requireChatSessions=true`, and `watcher.Add` on that directory). A workspace that has been opened in VS Code but never used Copilot chat has no `chatSessions` dir, so `WatchAgent` errors out. `ExecAgentAndWatch` (i.e. `specstory run`) retries every 5s, so it recovers — but the multi-provider `specstory watch` path (`WatchProviders`) treats a watcher error as terminal for that provider. Scenario: user runs `specstory watch`, then starts their first Copilot chat → nothing is ever saved. Cursor doesn't have this failure mode because it only needs `state.vscdb`, which always exists. Consider watching the workspace dir for `chatSessions` creation, or relaxing `requireChatSessions` for the watch path and retrying internally.

### 3. Remote workspaces are silently invisible (workspace.go:307-310)

`uriToPath` rejects anything that isn't `file://`. VS Code Remote (SSH, WSL, dev containers, tunnels) is one of the most common ways VS Code is used, and those workspaces store `vscode-remote://` URIs — they'll all be skipped with a debug log. Cursor has explicit handling for this (`parseVSCodeRemoteURI` with a scheme allow-list and remote-only basename matching, deliberately excluding WSL because those paths are locally reachable). If this is a deliberate phase-1 cut, it's fine, but it should be listed in the docs/changelog as a known limitation; nothing in the PR mentions it. Also note the exemplar delegates local URI parsing to the shared `spi.FileURIToPath` so all providers translate `file://` identically — this one hand-rolls it.

### 4. Update detection gates on `LastMessageDate` alone (watcher.go:127)

The watcher only re-emits a session when `LastMessageDate` strictly increases. Two consequences: a `kind:1` update that changes only `customTitle` (user renames the chat) never re-emits, so the markdown keeps the stale title forever; and any content-bearing write that doesn't bump `lastMessageDate` is dropped. The dedup layer in `WatchProviders` already fingerprints parsed content precisely so providers can afford to over-emit — Cursor leans on that and re-processes on every DB change. I'd emit on any successful parse whose file changed and let the central fingerprint do the dedup. Relatedly, the watermark is advanced *before* the callback runs, whereas Cursor advances it only after successful conversion so failures retry.

### 5. Unordered async callbacks can write stale markdown (watcher.go:159-168)

Each event spawns a fresh `go sessionCallback(...)`. Two updates to the same session more than 500ms apart produce two concurrent callbacks with no ordering guarantee — the older snapshot can be written last. Cursor serializes session processing behind its `checking` mutex; only the panic isolation is concurrent. A per-session (or global) serialization of callbacks would close this.

### 6. Smaller contract deviations

- **Not-found semantics** (loader.go:92): `GetAgentChatSession` returns an error for a missing session; the SPI contract and the exemplar say return `(nil, nil)`. Concretely, `specstory sync copilotide -s <bad-id>` prints "❌ Error getting session" and counts as an error instead of "not found" (main.go:658-675).
- **No analytics in `Check`** (provider.go:90): Cursor emits `EventCheckInstallFailed`/`EventCheckInstallSuccess`; this provider emits nothing, against the project's PostHog convention.
- **`Check.Version` is a label** (provider.go:108): returns `"VS Code Insiders Copilot"` in the version field; Cursor deliberately returns `""` when no real version is known.
- **Epoch timestamps** (parser.go:274): `FormatTimestamp(0)` yields `1969/1970-…` strings if `creationDate` is ever missing; Cursor falls back to `time.Now()`.
- **Watcher emits empty sessions** (watcher.go:129): the Get/List paths filter sessions with no requests and no editing activity, but the watcher has no such filter — a freshly opened empty chat fires the callback.

## Known-deferred scope (fine, but say so)

The `textEditGroup`, `codeblockUri`, `confirmation`, and `inlineReference` response kinds are logged and skipped (agent_session.go:213-220), and there are no per-tool markdown handlers — everything renders through the generic input/result formatter, versus Cursor's 10-handler registry with HTML-escaped summaries and table escaping. Both are documented as phase 2 in COPILOTIDE-TOOLS-PLAN.md, which is reasonable; the main user-visible effect is that **file edits Copilot makes are not rendered in the markdown** unless they arrive as tool calls. One consequence worth checking: Cursor's exemplar also implements neither `PathSessionReader` nor `ProgressEnumerator` because everything lives in one DB — but Copilot has *per-session files*, so `reindex` re-fetching via `GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID)` re-runs the full workspace-storage scan per session. `PathSessionReader` would be a natural, cheap win here that the exemplar couldn't take.

## Dead code to prune

# Code Review: Copilot IDE Provider (PR #160)

Review of the `copilotide` provider against the Cursor IDE provider (`cursoride`) as the exemplar, noting important omissions and deviations. Build, `go test ./...`, and `golangci-lint run` are all clean at the PR head.

## Overall Verdict

This is a solid, well-documented provider. The reconstruct/resume path is genuinely excellent — UTF-16 range math, byte-for-byte preservation of unmodeled index entries (with a test proving it), fence-safe markdown, and the honest "restart VS Code" guidance. The JSONL patch-log parser (kind:0/1/2) is careful and well-commented. Where it falls short of the Cursor exemplar is almost entirely in the **watcher's robustness** and a handful of SPI-contract deviations. Nothing here is a blocker for a phase-1 merge, but findings 1–3 below will produce real user-visible data gaps in `watch`/`run`.

## Important Deviations from the Cursor IDE Exemplar

### 1. The watcher can silently drop the final write of a response

Location: `watcher.go:102-107`

Cursor's watcher uses a *trailing-edge* throttle: a suppressed trigger sets a `pendingCheck` and schedules a deferred run, plus there's a 2-minute safety-net poll and a 60-second "incomplete session" forcing pass. The Copilot watcher uses a *leading-edge* debounce: any event within 500ms of the last processed one is simply discarded, with no deferred re-read and no safety-net poll.

If VS Code's final write for a completed response lands inside that window (very plausible — the stream-end write follows the last content write immediately), the completed answer isn't captured until some future event touches the file, which for the last message of a session may be never.

This is the single most important gap. Recommended fix: replace the drop with a timer that re-processes the file after the window expires, and/or add a periodic safety-net poll like Cursor's.

### 2. `specstory watch` is permanently dead for a project's first-ever chat

Location: `workspace.go:167`, `watcher.go:48`

`WatchAgent` requires the `chatSessions` directory to already exist (`FindWorkspaceForProject` with `requireChatSessions=true`, and `watcher.Add` on that directory). A workspace that has been opened in VS Code but never used Copilot chat has no `chatSessions` dir, so `WatchAgent` errors out.

`ExecAgentAndWatch` (i.e. `specstory run`) retries every 5s, so it recovers — but the multi-provider `specstory watch` path (`WatchProviders`) treats a watcher error as terminal for that provider. Scenario: user runs `specstory watch`, then starts their first Copilot chat → nothing is ever saved.

Cursor doesn't have this failure mode because it only needs `state.vscdb`, which always exists. Recommended fix: watch the workspace dir for `chatSessions` creation, or relax `requireChatSessions` for the watch path and retry internally.

### 3. Remote workspaces are silently invisible

Location: `workspace.go:307-310`

`uriToPath` rejects anything that isn't `file://`. VS Code Remote (SSH, WSL, dev containers, tunnels) is one of the most common ways VS Code is used, and those workspaces store `vscode-remote://` URIs — they'll all be skipped with a debug log.

Cursor has explicit handling for this (`parseVSCodeRemoteURI` with a scheme allow-list and remote-only basename matching, deliberately excluding WSL because those paths are locally reachable). If this is a deliberate phase-1 cut, it's fine, but it should be listed in the docs/changelog as a known limitation; nothing in the PR mentions it.

Also note the exemplar delegates local URI parsing to the shared `spi.FileURIToPath` so all providers translate `file://` identically — this one hand-rolls it.

### 4. Update detection gates on `LastMessageDate` alone

Location: `watcher.go:127`

The watcher only re-emits a session when `LastMessageDate` strictly increases. Two consequences:

- A `kind:1` update that changes only `customTitle` (user renames the chat) never re-emits, so the markdown keeps the stale title forever.
- Any content-bearing write that doesn't bump `lastMessageDate` is dropped.

The dedup layer in `WatchProviders` already fingerprints parsed content precisely so providers can afford to over-emit — Cursor leans on that and re-processes on every DB change. Recommended fix: emit on any successful parse whose file changed and let the central fingerprint do the dedup.

Relatedly, the watermark is advanced *before* the callback runs, whereas Cursor advances it only after successful conversion so failures retry.

### 5. Unordered async callbacks can write stale markdown

Location: `watcher.go:159-168`

Each event spawns a fresh `go sessionCallback(...)`. Two updates to the same session more than 500ms apart produce two concurrent callbacks with no ordering guarantee — the older snapshot can be written last.

Cursor serializes session processing behind its `checking` mutex; only the panic isolation is concurrent. A per-session (or global) serialization of callbacks would close this.

### 6. Smaller contract deviations

- **Not-found semantics** (`loader.go:92`): `GetAgentChatSession` returns an error for a missing session; the SPI contract and the exemplar say return `(nil, nil)`. Concretely, `specstory sync copilotide -s <bad-id>` prints "❌ Error getting session" and counts as an error instead of "not found" (`main.go:658-675`).
- **No analytics in `Check`** (`provider.go:90`): Cursor emits `EventCheckInstallFailed`/`EventCheckInstallSuccess`; this provider emits nothing, against the project's PostHog convention.
- **`Check.Version` is a label** (`provider.go:108`): returns `"VS Code Insiders Copilot"` in the version field; Cursor deliberately returns `""` when no real version is known.
- **Epoch timestamps** (`parser.go:274`): `FormatTimestamp(0)` yields `1969/1970-…` strings if `creationDate` is ever missing; Cursor falls back to `time.Now()`.
- **Watcher emits empty sessions** (`watcher.go:129`): the Get/List paths filter sessions with no requests and no editing activity, but the watcher has no such filter — a freshly opened empty chat fires the callback.

## Known-Deferred Scope (Fine, But Say So)

The `textEditGroup`, `codeblockUri`, `confirmation`, and `inlineReference` response kinds are logged and skipped (`agent_session.go:213-220`), and there are no per-tool markdown handlers — everything renders through the generic input/result formatter, versus Cursor's 10-handler registry with HTML-escaped summaries and table escaping. Both are documented as phase 2 in `COPILOTIDE-TOOLS-PLAN.md`, which is reasonable; the main user-visible effect is that **file edits Copilot makes are not rendered in the markdown** unless they arrive as tool calls.

One consequence worth checking: Cursor's exemplar also implements neither `PathSessionReader` nor `ProgressEnumerator` because everything lives in one DB — but Copilot has *per-session files*, so `reindex` re-fetching via `GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID)` re-runs the full workspace-storage scan per session. `PathSessionReader` would be a natural, cheap win here that the exemplar couldn't take.

## Dead Code to Prune

- `BuildToolCallMap` (`parser.go:37`) — the comment claims "kept for backward compatibility," but there is no backward compatibility; this is a new package.
- `IsHiddenTool` (`parser.go:27`) — the hidden check is done inline in `ParseResponsesForTools`.
- `GetSessionIDFromPath` (`watcher.go:181`) — unused.
- The four unused response types in `types.go:55-104` (`VSCodeTextEditGroupResponse`, `VSCodeCodeblockUriResponse`, `VSCodeConfirmationResponse`, `VSCodeInlineReferenceResponse`). If these are phase-2 placeholders, a comment saying so beats an exported-but-unused API.

## Shared Code Between cursoride and copilotide

The PR author asked whether workspace-selection code should be shared. The duplication is real and larger than the PR body implies: `workspace.json` reading, `.code-workspace` folder matching (methods 3/4 are near-verbatim copies of Cursor's), `uriToPath`, `selectNewestWorkspace` mtime tie-breaking, the `errAppCLIMissing`/`errCursorCLIMissing` launcher pattern, the 5s `ExecAgentAndWatch` retry loop, and now `codeFence`/`capRunes` (this PR even improves Cursor's `capRunes` and then copy-pastes the improvement).

Options:

1. **Extract now** into a shared package (e.g. `pkg/spi/vscodeworkspace` or similar) covering workspace-storage matching + URI handling, since both apps are VS Code-lineage and the layout is identical.
   - Pros: one place to add remote-URI support (finding 3) for both providers; matches the repo's DRY convention.
   - Cons: touches the mature Cursor provider in a feature PR, risk of regression, bigger diff.
2. **Merge as-is, extract in a follow-up** dedicated refactor PR.
   - Pros: keeps this PR reviewable and de-risks Cursor; the follow-up can also fix finding 3 once for both.
   - Cons: duplication ships and the two copies can drift in the interim.
3. **Leave duplicated permanently.**
   - Pros: cheapest now.
   - Cons: drift already exists — `capRunes` has appeared in three shapes across the repo's history.

Recommendation: **option 2** — this PR is already ~4,600 lines, and folding a cursoride refactor into it would make both harder to verify. But `codeFence`/`capRunes` specifically are tiny, pure functions that could move to `pkg/spi` in *this* PR with near-zero risk, since the PR already modifies Cursor's copy.

## What's Notably Good

- The variant design (one implementation, four registered VS Code distributions: stock, Insiders, VSCodium, VSCodium Insiders) is clean, and the registry/config/resume plumbing is consistent everywhere, including the type-based (not ID-based) restart-note check in `resume.go`.
- The reconstruct tests round-trip through the provider's own loader and prove unmodeled index fields survive the merge.
- The kind:2 append semantics comment ("VS Code writes one kind:2 per user turn... so we must accumulate") is exactly the kind of why-comment this codebase asks for.
- Test gaps mirror the exemplar's (no watcher or workspace-matching tests here; Cursor lacks watcher tests too), so that's parity rather than regression — though a `FindWorkspaceForProject` test with a fake workspaceStorage tree would be cheap and valuable given how much matching logic lives there.

```text
375	// (Cursor IDE workspace identifiers, Antigravity tool args and project
376	// configs), so the non-POSIX forms are translated identically everywhere:
377	//
378	//   - WSL URIs (file://wsl.localhost/<distro>/path, file://wsl$/...): the host
379	//     and distro segment are stripped, yielding the in-distro POSIX path.
380	//   - Drive-letter URIs (file:///C:/Users/...): on Windows the spurious
381	//     leading slash is trimmed and separators converted (C:\Users\...).
382	//   - UNC URIs (file://server/share/...): on Windows the host becomes the UNC
383	//     root (\\server\share\...). On POSIX systems a host has no filesystem
384	//     meaning and is dropped.
385	//
386	// Returns an error for unparseable URIs and schemes other than file.
387	func FileURIToPath(uri string) (string, error) {
388		parsed, err := url.Parse(uri)
389		if err != nil {
390			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse URI: %w", err)
391		}
392		if parsed.Scheme != "file" && parsed.Scheme != "" {
393			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported URI scheme %q: %s", parsed.Scheme, uri)
394		}
395	
396		path, err := url.PathUnescape(parsed.Path)
397		if err != nil {
398			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode URI path: %w", err)
399		}
400	
401		// WSL URIs carry the distro as the first path segment under a wsl host;
402		// the usable path is what remains inside the distro.
403		if strings.EqualFold(parsed.Host, "wsl.localhost") || strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(parsed.Host), "wsl$") {
404			if len(path) > 1 {
405				if idx := strings.Index(path[1:], "/"); idx >= 0 {
406					slog.Debug("Converted WSL file URI to path", "uri", uri, "path", path[idx+1:])
407					return path[idx+1:], nil
408				}
409			}
410			return "", fmt.Errorf("malformed WSL URI path: %s", uri)
411		}
412	
413		if filepath.Separator == '\\' {
414			// A non-WSL host names a UNC share.
415			if parsed.Host != "" {
416				return `\\` + parsed.Host + filepath.FromSlash(path), nil
417			}
418			// Drive-letter URI paths arrive with a spurious leading slash (/C:/Users).
419			return filepath.FromSlash(strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/")), nil
420		}
421	
422		return path, nil
423	}
424
```
</details></tool-use>
