_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-04 15:47:07Z)**_

Finding 3 is addressed. Here's what changed and why:

## What was done

**Extracted the remote-URI handling to `pkg/spi`** (per your choice):

- `ParseVSCodeRemoteURI` and `IsRemoteURIRequiringBasenameMatch` moved from `cursoride/workspace.go` into `pkg/spi/path_utils.go`, right next to the existing `FileURIToPath` — no new files. Their test tables moved to `pkg/spi/path_utils_test.go` verbatim (plus a new unsupported-host case). Cursoride now calls the shared versions; its local copies and their local tests are deleted.

**Wired remote support into copilotide** (`pkg/providers/copilotide/workspace.go`):

- `uriToPath` now delegates `vscode-remote://` URIs to `spi.ParseVSCodeRemoteURI` and everything else to `spi.FileURIToPath` — this also resolves the review's side note that copilotide hand-rolled its `file://` parsing.
- `findWorkspaceForProject` gained the exemplar's Method 2: for SSH/tunnel/dev-container workspaces (whose paths live on another machine or in a container, so direct path comparison can never succeed), it falls back to folder-basename matching. WSL and local workspaces are deliberately excluded from the fallback, with Cursor's rationale comment carried over — two unrelated `backend/` folders must not cross-match. The existing method comments are now numbered 1–4 to match the exemplar.

**One bonus bug fix, found by verification:** before switching copilotide to `spi.FileURIToPath`, I checked it against copilotide's existing `literal%2520pct` test case — and the shared helper failed it. `url.Parse` already percent-decodes into `.Path`, and `FileURIToPath` was calling `PathUnescape` on top, double-decoding: a folder literally named `literal%20pct` came out as `literal pct`. Copilotide's hand-rolled parser had deliberately avoided this (with a test). I fixed the double-decode in `spi.FileURIToPath` itself with a regression test, so every provider using it benefits; no existing test depended on the old behavior (it only bites on `%25` sequences).

## Verification

- `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues
- `go test ./...` — all 22 test packages pass, including the moved spi tests, copilotide's extended `TestUriToPath` (now covering SSH, WSL, and dev-container URIs), and cursoride's `TestUriToPath` which still exercises the delegation path end-to-end.

`docs/COPILOTIDE-REVIEW.md` is updated: finding 3 is marked addressed with a summary of the fix, and the shared-code section now notes the remote-URI helpers are already extracted, narrowing what's left for the follow-up refactor.

One scope note: I did not add an integration-style test for `findWorkspaceForProject`'s basename matching, because copilotide's storage path isn't stubbable (unlike Cursor's `var` seams) — that's the test-seam gap already flagged in the review's closing section, and adding the seam felt like separate scope. The gating function itself is fully tested in spi. Happy to add the seam + test if you want it now.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-04 21:05:16Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should the Copilot watcher serialize session callbacks to prevent stale-overwrite?**

Options:
- **Single FIFO worker (Recommended)** - A buffered channel plus one delivery goroutine that invokes the callback with panic recovery. Strict arrival-order delivery, event loop never blocks on callback I/O (markdown write / cloud sync), and shutdown drains the queue before the watcher closes. Small, idiomatic Go.
- **Synchronous in event loop** - Call the callback inline (with recover) instead of spawning goroutines. Simplest possible fix and perfect ordering, but slow callback I/O delays fsnotify event handling and debounce timing while it runs.
- **Per-session ordered queues** - A map of per-session queues so different sessions deliver concurrently while each session stays ordered. Most code and lifecycle complexity for little practical gain — a single-project watch rarely has concurrent multi-session activity.


**Answer:** Single FIFO worker (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-04 21:07:02Z)**_

MIP #5 is addressed. Summary of the change:

## What was done

The per-event `go sessionCallback(...)` in `pkg/providers/copilotide/watcher.go` is replaced with a **single FIFO delivery worker** (the option you picked):

- A buffered channel (`sessionQueue`, capacity 64) sits between the fsnotify event loop and the callback. One worker goroutine consumes it and invokes the callback in strict arrival order, so an older session snapshot can never be delivered after a newer one — the stale-overwrite race is structurally gone.
- The panic isolation moved into a small `deliverSession` helper, so a panic in markdown writing or cloud sync still can't crash the watcher — same protection as before, now without the concurrency.
- The event loop enqueues with a `select` on context cancellation, so if the queue were ever full while a callback is stuck, Ctrl-C still shuts down cleanly instead of hanging on the send.
- Shutdown ordering is handled by deferred LIFO: on return the queue is closed and drained (`callbackWg.Wait()`) *before* the fsnotify watcher closes, so no callback is still writing when `WatchChatSessions` exits. The worker uses Go 1.25's `WaitGroup.Go`, which the toolchain here (1.26) supports.

The buffer size is a pragmatic backpressure bound: the per-file 500ms debounce caps the event rate, so 64 pending deliveries is effectively unreachable; if it ever did fill, the event loop blocks briefly rather than dropping work — the comment in the code explains this trade-off.

## Verification

- `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues.
- `go test -race ./pkg/providers/copilotide/` — passes under the race detector.
- Full binary builds.

`docs/COPILOTIDE-REVIEW.md` finding 5 is now marked addressed with a description of the fix. Remaining open findings from the review are #1 (trailing-edge debounce drop / no safety-net poll), #2 (watch dead until `chatSessions` exists), #4 (`LastMessageDate`-only gating), and the smaller items in #6 — #1 and #4 touch the same event-loop code we just changed, so they'd be natural next steps if you want to keep going.

All three items are addressed — lint clean, full suite passes (22 packages), race detector clean on the watcher package. And per your note, I haven't touched the review doc.

## What changed

**No analytics in `Check`** (`pkg/providers/copilotide/provider.go`)

`Check` now emits the same PostHog events as the exemplar: `EventCheckInstallFailed` with `error_type: "workspace_storage_not_found"` when the variant's workspace storage is missing, and `EventCheckInstallSuccess` with the storage `location` on success. The `provider` property uses `p.variant.ID`, so the four variants (copilotide, -insiders, -vscodium, -vscodium-insiders) are distinguishable in analytics rather than lumped under one hardcoded string — the one place I deviated from Cursor's literal `"cursoride"`, since this provider is variant-driven.

**Epoch timestamps** (`pkg/providers/copilotide/parser.go`)

`FormatTimestamp` now falls back to `time.Now()` for zero/negative input instead of emitting a 1970 epoch date, matching the Cursor provider. Since it's the single formatting funnel, the guard covers session `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, exchange start times, and message timestamps in one place. The comment notes the practical harm of the old behavior (epoch dates sort the session before every real one).

**Watcher emits empty sessions** (`pkg/providers/copilotide/watcher.go`)

The event handler now applies the same emptiness rule as the read paths — skip when the session has no requests *and* no editing activity in the state file — placed after the state load so editing-only sessions still pass. One subtlety handled deliberately: the session remains tracked in `knownSessions` before the skip, which is safe because the first real message advances `lastMessageDate` and therefore still fires as an update; the comment in the code explains this so the ordering doesn't look accidental.

Remaining open items from the review are #1 (debounce trailing-edge drop), #2 (watch dead until `chatSessions` exists), #4 (`LastMessageDate` gating), the not-found semantics and `Check.Version` bullets in #6, and the dead-code pruning.

package copilotide

// Temporary live verification for the wait-for-chatSessions flow; not part of
// the committed test suite.

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

func TestLiveCheck_WatchWaitsForChatSessionsDir(t *testing.T) {
	workspaceDir := t.TempDir()
	p := NewProvider(VSCode)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	sessions := make(chan *spi.AgentChatSession, 4)
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		done <- p.WatchChatSessions(ctx, workspaceDir, "/tmp/proj", false, func(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
			sessions <- s
		})
	}()

	// Let the watcher enter its wait phase, then create the directory and a
	// session file the way VS Code would on the first-ever chat.
	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
	chatDir := filepath.Join(workspaceDir, "chatSessions")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(chatDir, 0755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
	sessionJSON := `{"version":3,"sessionId":"abc-123","creationDate":1700000000000,"lastMessageDate":1700000001000,"requests":[{"requestId":"r1","timestamp":1700000001000,"message":{"text":"hello"},"response":[{"value":"hi"}],"result":{"metadata":{}}}]}`
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(chatDir, "abc-123.json"), []byte(sessionJSON), 0644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	select {
	case s := <-sessions:
		if s.SessionID != "abc-123" {
			t.Errorf("sessionID = %q, want abc-123", s.SessionID)
		}
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("session callback never fired after chatSessions creation")
	}

	cancel()
	if err := <-done; err != nil {
		t.Errorf("watcher returned error: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestLiveCheck_WatchRaceFileBeforeWatchSwitch(t *testing.T) {
	workspaceDir := t.TempDir()
	p := NewProvider(VSCode)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	sessions := make(chan *spi.AgentChatSession, 4)
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		done <- p.WatchChatSessions(ctx, workspaceDir, "/tmp/proj", false, func(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
			sessions <- s
		})
	}()

	// Create the directory AND the session file in the same instant, so the
	// file very likely lands before the watcher switches to the new directory.
	// The catch-up scan must still emit it.
	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
	chatDir := filepath.Join(workspaceDir, "chatSessions")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(chatDir, 0755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sessionJSON := `{"version":3,"sessionId":"def-456","creationDate":1700000000000,"lastMessageDate":1700000001000,"requests":[{"requestId":"r1","timestamp":1700000001000,"message":{"text":"first"},"response":[{"value":"reply"}],"result":{"metadata":{}}}]}`
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(chatDir, "def-456.json"), []byte(sessionJSON), 0644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	select {
	case s := <-sessions:
		if s.SessionID != "def-456" {
			t.Errorf("sessionID = %q, want def-456", s.SessionID)
		}
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("session callback never fired for file created alongside the directory")
	}

	cancel()
	if err := <-done; err != nil {
		t.Errorf("watcher returned error: %v", err)
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-04 22:42:42Z)**_

MIP #2 is fixed. `specstory watch` now survives a project's first-ever Copilot chat.

## What changed

**`pkg/providers/copilotide/provider.go` — `WatchAgent`** now looks up the workspace with `findWorkspaceForProject(projectPath, false)`, i.e. without requiring a `chatSessions` directory. That requirement was the first failure point: a workspace that had been opened in VS Code but never chatted in has no such directory, and the multi-provider `watch` path treats a watcher error as terminal.

**`pkg/providers/copilotide/watcher.go` — `WatchChatSessions`** no longer fails when `chatSessions` is missing. A new `waitForChatSessionsDir` helper watches the workspace directory (which always exists) and blocks until VS Code creates `chatSessions`, then hands over to the normal chat-directory watch. Any event in the workspace dir triggers a re-stat rather than matching event names, so a rename-into-place can't slip past, and the wait is context-aware for clean Ctrl-C.

**The creation race is handled explicitly.** A session file can land between the directory-create event and our watch registration, and such a file would never produce an event of its own. To cover it, I extracted the per-file processing (load → new/updated check → empty filter → convert → queue) into a `processSessionFile` closure shared by the event loop and a catch-up scan that runs — and *emits* — right after the handover. This also removed the duplication between the event handler and the startup logic: the pre-existing-directory path still seeds `knownSessions` without emitting (unchanged behavior), while the fresh-directory path processes files as new activity.

## Verification

Beyond lint (0 issues) and the full suite (22 packages, race detector clean), I live-tested the actual lifecycle with two temporary integration tests: one where the directory is created first and the session file follows (event path), and one where directory and file are created in the same instant (catch-up path). Both fired the callback with the right session and shut down cleanly. I removed that file afterward since adding new test files needs your sign-off — but they'd be a genuinely useful `watcher_test.go` (currently the watcher has zero test coverage, same gap as Cursor's). Say the word and I'll restore them as a permanent test file.

Remaining open findings: #1 (debounce trailing-edge drop — the biggest one left), #4 (`LastMessageDate` gating), the not-found and `Check.Version` bullets in #6, and dead-code pruning.

Done. The `Check.Version` label is fixed, with a small shared-display improvement on top:

## What changed

**`pkg/providers/copilotide/provider.go`** — `Check` now returns `Version: ""` instead of the `"<AppName> Copilot"` label, matching the exemplar's deliberate choice. The decision is documented in place with data rather than dogma: VS Code's version *would* be discoverable via `code --version`, but I measured it at ~170ms per invocation, and `Check` isn't only used by `specstory check` — it also gates provider availability in the search command and the session TUI (`prov.Check("").Success`). With four registered variants, shelling out would add roughly 0.7s to those latency-sensitive paths, so no subprocess is spawned and no version is reported rather than a label that isn't one.

**`pkg/cmd/check.go`** — reporting an empty version exposed a pre-existing display wart: `specstory check` printed a bare `📦 Version:` line (it already did this for Cursor IDE). Both render sites now omit the line when the version is empty. Verified against the real binary:

  ✅ Status: All systems go!

The fix distinguishes "not here" from "broken", using a sentinel so real failures still surface:

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 15:07:21Z)**_

MIP #1 — the watcher's leading-edge debounce drops events inside the 500ms window with no re-read, so a burst's final write (often the completed response) can be lost forever. The fix follows the review's recommendation and the exemplar's shape: mark suppressed files dirty and re-process them on a ticker once the window passes (trailing edge), plus a 2-minute safety-net rescan like Cursor's for events fsnotify never delivers. The existing `lastMessageDate` gate keeps both mechanisms from re-emitting unchanged sessions.

package copilotide

// Temporary live verification of the trailing-edge debounce; not part of the
// committed test suite.

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// TestLiveCheck_TrailingDebounce reproduces MIP #1: a session file receives a
// second write ~100ms after the first (inside the 500ms debounce window) and
// then goes quiet. Before the fix, the second write's content was lost until
// some future event; now the debounce ticker must re-read and emit it.
func TestLiveCheck_TrailingDebounce(t *testing.T) {
	workspaceDir := t.TempDir()
	chatDir := filepath.Join(workspaceDir, "chatSessions")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(chatDir, 0755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	p := NewProvider(VSCode)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	sessions := make(chan *spi.AgentChatSession, 8)
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		done <- p.WatchChatSessions(ctx, workspaceDir, "/tmp/proj", false, func(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
			sessions <- s
		})
	}()
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond) // let the watcher start

	sessionFile := filepath.Join(chatDir, "abc-123.json")
	write := func(lastMs int64, answer string) {
		content := `{"version":3,"sessionId":"abc-123","creationDate":1700000000000,"lastMessageDate":` +
			timeStr(lastMs) + `,"requests":[{"requestId":"r1","timestamp":1700000001000,"message":{"text":"hello"},"response":[{"value":"` + answer + `"}],"result":{"metadata":{}}}]}`
		if err := os.WriteFile(sessionFile, []byte(content), 0644); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}

	// First write: processed immediately (leading edge).
	write(1700000001000, "partial answer")
	select {
	case s := <-sessions:
		if !strings.Contains(s.RawData, "partial answer") {
			t.Fatalf("first callback should carry the first write, got: %s", s.RawData)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("first write never emitted")
	}

	// Second write ~100ms later: inside the debounce window, then silence.
	// This is the "final write of the response" scenario.
	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	write(1700000002000, "the complete final answer")

	select {
	case s := <-sessions:
		if !strings.Contains(s.RawData, "the complete final answer") {
			t.Fatalf("trailing re-read emitted wrong content: %s", s.RawData)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("final write was dropped: trailing re-read never fired")
	}

	cancel()
	if err := <-done; err != nil {
		t.Errorf("watcher returned error: %v", err)
	}
}

func timeStr(ms int64) string {
	b, _ := jsonMarshalInt(ms)
	return string(b)
}

func jsonMarshalInt(ms int64) ([]byte, error) {
	return []byte(strconvFormatInt(ms)), nil
}

func strconvFormatInt(ms int64) string {
	digits := ""
	for ms > 0 {
		digits = string(rune('0'+ms%10)) + digits
		ms /= 10
	}
	return digits
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 15:08:59Z)**_

MIP #1 is fixed. The watcher can no longer silently drop the final write of a response.

## What changed (`pkg/providers/copilotide/watcher.go`)

**Trailing-edge debounce.** The debounce stays leading-edge (first event in a burst processes immediately), but a suppressed event now marks the file in a `dirty` set instead of being discarded. A ticker running at the debounce interval (500ms) re-processes dirty files once their window has passed — so the burst's final write is emitted at most ~1s later even if no further event ever arrives. A file still inside its window stays dirty for the next tick; on a load failure the dirty mark is dropped deliberately, because `lastProcessed` wasn't advanced, so the event that follows the in-flight write processes immediately (the pre-existing mid-write recovery path, preserved).

**Safety-net poll.** A second ticker rescans all session files every 2 minutes, mirroring the Cursor watcher's safety-net poll, as a backstop for events fsnotify never delivers (kqueue overflow, kernel-coalesced changes). The `lastMessageDate` gate in `processSessionFile` means a quiet scan costs only the file parses — nothing re-emits unless a session actually advanced.

Both mechanisms run inside the existing single event-loop `select`, so there are no new goroutines, no locking, and the FIFO delivery ordering from the MIP #5 fix is preserved.

## Verification

I reproduced the exact failure scenario from the finding in a temporary live test: first write emitted immediately, second write 100ms later (inside the window) followed by silence. Before this fix that content was lost; now the trailing re-read emitted it with the complete final answer, passing under the race detector in ~1s. The throwaway test is removed per our convention. Lint is clean, the full suite has zero failures, and the binary builds.

One honest caveat, which is the bridge to the last open finding: the trailing re-read and safety poll only *emit* when `lastMessageDate` advances. If VS Code writes content without bumping it (the `customTitle` rename case, and possibly some streaming writes), MIP #4's gate still suppresses the update. So #1 is now structurally sound, but its full effectiveness lands when #4 relaxes that gate — that's the natural next step, along with the remaining dead code (`BuildToolCallMap`, the four phase-2 response types).

package copilotide

// Temporary live verification of the file-signature update gate; not part of
// the committed test suite.

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// TestLiveCheck_TitleOnlyRenameEmits reproduces MIP #4: a write that changes
// only customTitle — lastMessageDate identical — previously never re-emitted,
// leaving the markdown title stale forever. With the file-signature gate it
// must re-emit with the new slug.
func TestLiveCheck_TitleOnlyRenameEmits(t *testing.T) {
	workspaceDir := t.TempDir()
	chatDir := filepath.Join(workspaceDir, "chatSessions")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(chatDir, 0755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	p := NewProvider(VSCode)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	sessions := make(chan *spi.AgentChatSession, 8)
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		done <- p.WatchChatSessions(ctx, workspaceDir, "/tmp/proj", false, func(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
			sessions <- s
		})
	}()
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)

	sessionFile := filepath.Join(chatDir, "abc-123.json")
	write := func(title string) {
		content := `{"version":3,"sessionId":"abc-123","customTitle":"` + title + `","creationDate":1700000000000,"lastMessageDate":1700000001000,"requests":[{"requestId":"r1","timestamp":1700000001000,"message":{"text":"hello"},"response":[{"value":"hi"}],"result":{"metadata":{}}}]}`
		if err := os.WriteFile(sessionFile, []byte(content), 0644); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}

	write("original title")
	select {
	case s := <-sessions:
		if s.Slug != "original-title" {
			t.Fatalf("first slug = %q, want original-title", s.Slug)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("first write never emitted")
	}

	// Rename only: identical lastMessageDate, outside the debounce window.
	time.Sleep(700 * time.Millisecond)
	write("renamed by the user")

	select {
	case s := <-sessions:
		if s.Slug != "renamed-by-the-user" {
			t.Fatalf("rename emitted wrong slug: %q", s.Slug)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("title-only rename was never re-emitted (stale markdown title)")
	}

	cancel()
	if err := <-done; err != nil {
		t.Errorf("watcher returned error: %v", err)
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 15:16:25Z)**_

MIP #4 is fixed — the last of the substantive review findings. Verified live: a `customTitle`-only rename with an identical `lastMessageDate` now re-emits with the new slug (`original-title` → `renamed-by-the-user`), which the old gate suppressed forever.

## What changed (`pkg/providers/copilotide/watcher.go`)

**The `lastMessageDate` watermark is replaced with a per-file signature** (`fileSignature{size, modNs}`, mtime as `UnixNano` so struct equality is a plain value compare). A session re-emits whenever its file's on-disk state changes — any real write moves size and/or mtime — so title renames and any content write VS Code makes without bumping `lastMessageDate` now flow through. I chose this over the review's "always emit, let the central fingerprint dedup" suggestion for a concrete reason: `specstory run` doesn't route through `WatchProviders`' fingerprint dedup, and the 2-minute safety poll from MIP #1 would have re-emitted every session each sweep there. The signature gate is caller-independent.

**Ordering fix folded in:** the signature is recorded only *after* the session is successfully handed to the delivery worker — the review's "watermark advanced before the callback" note. A failure anywhere earlier (stat, parse, state load) retries on the next event or tick. The signature is taken *before* the parse, so a write landing between stat and read produces a harmless duplicate emit rather than a miss.

**Two efficiency wins fell out:**

- The startup seed no longer parses every historical session — a stat per file replaces a full load, since suppressing re-emits only needs the signature.
- The MIP #1 safety poll now skips unchanged files before parsing — a quiet 2-minute sweep costs one stat per file instead of a full parse of every session.

Deleted files are handled: a failed stat forgets the signature so a recreated file (or a `.json` superseded by `.jsonl`) is treated as new.

## Verification

Lint clean, full suite zero failures, race detector clean, binary builds. The live check ran the rename scenario end to end and was removed afterward, as before.

That closes MIPs #1–#5 and all of finding #6. The only review items left are cosmetic dead code: `BuildToolCallMap` (with its incorrect "backward compatibility" comment) and the four unused phase-2 response types in `types.go` — plus the offer still stands to formalize the watcher live-checks into a permanent `watcher_test.go`, which would give this now-substantially-reworked watcher real regression coverage.

python3 << 'EOF'
import json, subprocess

query_tmpl = '''
query {
  repository(owner: "specstoryai", name: "getspecstory") {
    pullRequest(number: 160) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100%s) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
        nodes {
          isResolved
          isOutdated
          path
          line
          comments(first: 10) { nodes { author { login } body } }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}'''

threads = []
cursor = None
while True:
    after = f', after: "{cursor}"' if cursor else ''
    out = subprocess.run(['gh', 'api', 'graphql', '-f', f'query={query_tmpl % after}'],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    d = json.loads(out.stdout)['data']['repository']['pullRequest']['reviewThreads']
    threads.extend(d['nodes'])
    if not d['pageInfo']['hasNextPage']:
        break
    cursor = d['pageInfo']['endCursor']

unresolved = [t for t in threads if not t['isResolved']]
print(f'total: {len(threads)}, unresolved: {len(unresolved)}')
print('=' * 80)
for i, t in enumerate(unresolved, 1):
    print(f'--- [{i}] {t["path"]}:{t["line"]} (outdated: {t["isOutdated"]})')
    for c in t['comments']['nodes']:
        print(f'  author: {c["author"]["login"]}')
        print('  ' + c['body'][:2000].replace(chr(10), chr(10) + '  '))
        print()
EOF

// escapeSummaryText escapes DB-sourced strings (tool names, queries, file paths)
// before they are interpolated into HTML contexts like <summary> lines or tag
// attributes. These values come from Cursor's database, so a malformed string
// containing <, >, & or quotes would otherwise break the generated markup.
func escapeSummaryText(s string) string {
	return html.EscapeString(s)
}

// formatToolError formats a tool error message
func formatToolError(bubble *BubbleConversation) string {
	if bubble.Error != "" {
		// Parse the error JSON
		var errorData struct {
			ClientVisibleErrorMessage string `json:"clientVisibleErrorMessage"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(bubble.Error), &errorData); err == nil {
			return errorData.ClientVisibleErrorMessage
		}
		// If parsing fails, return the raw error
		return bubble.Error
	}
	return "An unknown error occurred"
}

I've verified each claim against the current code. Here's the assessment of all 24 unresolved threads. Note several are duplicates of each other, and everything we fixed locally is still uncommitted — the bot can't see it, which explains some "outdated" markers.

## Real issues worth fixing

**[6] / [9] / [13] / [17] — Synthetic editing-only requests set `ModelID` to `composer.ResponderUsername`** (`agent_session.go:427`) — one issue, reported four times.
**Real.** The synthetic request stamps `"GitHub Copilot"` (a username) into `Message.Model`, so exported markdown mislabels the model. Confirmed in code. **Suggest:** leave `ModelID` empty — for a reconstructed editing-only session there's no honest model to claim. One-line fix.

**[18] + [19] — `extractOperationsFromV1State` iterates a map, so summary order is nondeterministic** (`agent_session.go:511`).
**Real.** `filesSummary` is a map; the exported assistant text for v1 editing-only sessions can reorder between runs, which churns markdown diffs. [19] is just the bot noting the `sort` import its own suggestion needs. **Suggest:** `sort.Strings(summaries)` before returning (or dedupe with a seen-set while preserving encounter order — sort is simpler).

**[12] — "Unknown response kind" debug log fires for every plain markdown fragment** (`agent_session.go:223`).
**Real, minor.** Markdown items intentionally have no `kind`, so the `default:` branch logs per fragment — pure debug-log noise during normal parsing. **Suggest:** add `case "":` as a silent no-op, keep the debug log for genuinely unknown kinds. One-line fix.

**[22] — `LoadAllSessionFiles` errors when `chatSessions/` doesn't exist** (`loader.go:20`).
**Real, and it's the same not-found-semantics class we fixed in `GetAgentChatSession`.** A workspace that exists but has never chatted makes `GetAgentChatSessions`/`ListAgentChatSessions` return an *error* instead of an empty list — the exemplar returns empty. **Suggest:** return `([], nil)` on `os.IsNotExist`, keep real stat/read failures as errors; callers simplify.

**[20] + [21] — `resume.go` type-asserts `*copilotide.Provider` and hard-codes "restart VS Code"** (`resume.go:24,439`).
**Half-real.** The "wrapped providers" concern is hypothetical (the registry never wraps), and our type check was deliberate — but two fair points stand: the cmd→concrete-provider import is avoidable, and the message says "VS Code" even when the target is VSCodium/Insiders. **Suggest:** switch to `strings.HasPrefix(plan.toID, "copilotide")` (drops the import) and use `plan.to.Name()` or generic wording so VSCodium users aren't told to restart "VS Code".

**[4] — `WatchProviders` fingerprint is count+length only; same-length in-place edits dedup wrongly** (`watch_agents.go:132`).
**Real but low-probability.** A content change that keeps total byte length identical is suppressed. Our copilotide watcher no longer depends on this (file-signature gate), but `specstory watch` dedup across all providers does. **Suggest:** add a cheap content hash (FNV-1a over the text as it's summed) to the fingerprint struct — small change, eliminates the collision class.

**[23] — `openApp` uses `CombinedOutput()`, blocking until the launcher exits** (`provider.go:424`).
**Real edge case.** The stock `code` CLI forks and returns instantly, so normal use is fine — but a custom command containing `--wait` would hang `specstory run` before the watcher starts. Verified that cursoride has the identical pattern, so copilotide is exemplar-consistent here. **Suggest:** either leave it (parity) or fix both providers together with `Start()` + async reap; if we fix, do it as a symmetric change, not copilot-only.

## Real issues, but in cursoride (pre-existing, touched only incidentally by this PR)

**[5] — `formatToolError` returns `clientVisibleErrorMessage` even when empty** (`cursoride/tool_handlers.go:199`).
**Confirmed real** in current code: valid error-JSON with an empty message hides the raw error. Trivial fix (only return when non-empty), but it's exemplar code, not part of this PR's scope. Fine as a small drive-by or separate cleanup.

**[7] — `parseCapabilities` only handles the string form of `bubbleDataMap`** (`cursoride/agent_session.go:372`).
**Confirmed** the map case is unhandled while the type doc says "string (JSON) or map". Whether Cursor ever writes the object form is unverified; affects only old V1-capability sessions. Low priority; would need a marshal-roundtrip for the map case.

513	// openCursorIDE launches Cursor IDE at the given project path. By default it uses
514	// Cursor's own `cursor` CLI — the only launcher that reliably opens the directory as
515	// a workspace window (`open -a Cursor` on macOS mostly just activates an
516	// already-running instance on its home screen, so it is deliberately not used as a
517	// fallback). A custom command (from --command or the cursoride_cmd config) overrides
518	// the launcher binary and prepends any extra arguments before the project path.
519	//
520	// When the default `cursor` CLI isn't on PATH, errCursorCLIMissing is returned so the
521	// caller can tell the user how to install it; a missing custom launcher returns a
522	// plain error, since the install guidance only applies to Cursor's own command.
523	func openCursorIDE(projectPath, customCommand string) error {
524		launcher := "cursor"
525		var args []string
526		if customCommand != "" {
527			if parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand); len(parts) > 0 {
528				launcher = parts[0]
529				args = parts[1:]
530			}
531		}
532	
533		if _, err := exec.LookPath(launcher); err != nil {
534			if customCommand == "" {
535				return errCursorCLIMissing
536			}
537			return fmt.Errorf("configured Cursor IDE launcher %q not found on PATH: %w", launcher, err)
538		}
539	
540		args = append(args, projectPath)
541		if out, err := exec.Command(launcher, args...).CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
542			return fmt.Errorf("cursor IDE launcher %q failed: %w: %s", launcher, err, string(out))
543		}
544		return nil
545	}

// printIDERestartNote tells the user how to surface a session reconstructed into an
// IDE-backed store. Unlike CLI targets, these are not visible until the app restarts:
// Cursor only picks up imported sessions from its SQLite database on startup, and VS
// Code holds its chat session index in memory and flushes it over ours on shutdown.
func printIDERestartNote(plan *resumePlan, out io.Writer) {
	if plan.toID == "cursoride" {
		fprintf(out, "\nNote: only Cursor 3 is supported. Restart Cursor to see the imported session in the Agent sidebar.\n")
	}
	// A type check (not an ID comparison) so every Copilot IDE variant — stock
	// VS Code, Insiders, and any added later — gets the restart note.
	if _, ok := plan.to.(*copilotide.Provider); ok {
		// "Developer: Reload Window" is NOT enough — it keeps the main process (and
		// the in-memory index) alive; verified empirically.
		fprintf(out, "\nNote: quit and restart VS Code to see the imported session in the Chat panel.\n")
	}
}

// materializeReconstructed reconstructs data into plan.to's native store under cwd, durably writes
// the native file, and waits for it to become readable, returning the fresh session. Shared by the
// cross-agent and cloud resume paths (both reconstruct from a SessionData already in hand). A
// spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported from the provider is returned unwrapped so callers can detect it.

All nine items are done — lint clean, full suite zero failures, race detector clean on every touched package, binary builds. By number:

**[4]** `pkg/utils/watch_agents.go` — `sessionFingerprint` gains a `contentHash` field: FNV-1a computed over the same content the byte count already walks (message text, tool summaries, tool markdown), with a zero-byte separator after each part so content shifting between adjacent parts can't collide either. Same-length in-place edits now change the fingerprint. Added a regression subtest for exactly that case, since it's the one length+count can't see.

**[5]** `cursoride/tool_handlers.go` — `formatToolError` returns the parsed `clientVisibleErrorMessage` only when it's non-empty; message-less error JSON now falls back to the raw error string instead of silently returning `""`.

**[6/9/13/17]** `copilotide/agent_session.go` — the synthetic editing-only request no longer stamps `ModelID: composer.ResponderUsername`; the field is left empty with a comment explaining why ("GitHub Copilot" is a username, not a model ID, and an editing-only session records no model).

**[12]** Same file — `ParseResponsesForTools` now has a silent `case "":` for the kind-less plain-markdown fragments that make up every normal response, keeping the "Unknown response kind" debug log for genuinely unknown kinds.

**[14]** `pkg/utils/watch_agents_test.go` — the two fixtures missing `ContentPart.Type` now set `schema.ContentTypeText`.

**[18/19]** `copilotide/agent_session.go` — `extractOperationsFromV1State` sorts the summaries before returning (`sort` imported), so v1 editing-only exports are deterministic instead of following randomized map iteration order.

**[20/21]** `pkg/cmd/resume.go` — the restart note now uses `strings.HasPrefix(plan.toID, "copilotide")`, and the `copilotide` package import is gone from the cmd layer. The message names the actual app by trimming the `" Copilot IDE"` suffix off the provider name, so VSCodium and Insiders users are told to restart the right application; if the naming convention ever changes, the full provider name prints — awkward but still correct, and the comment says so.

**[22]** `copilotide/loader.go` — `LoadAllSessionFiles` returns `(nil, nil)` when `chatSessions/` doesn't exist (a normal never-chatted state), erroring only on real read failures. All callers were audited: `DetectAgent` already checks length, `Get`/`List` now correctly return empty results for a chat-less workspace, and the watcher paths only reach it when the directory exists.

**[23]** Both providers, symmetrically — `openApp` (copilotide) and `openCursorIDE` (cursoride) now `Start()` the launcher and reap it in a goroutine instead of blocking on `CombinedOutput()`. A custom command like `code --wait` no longer stalls `specstory run` before the watcher starts. Spawn failures still return synchronously; post-spawn failures log at Warn with the captured combined output (read only after `Wait()` returns, so no buffer race).

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 17:45:35Z)**_

Mystery solved — this isn't a rendering bug. The markdown faithfully renders everything VS Code has written to disk; **VS Code itself stopped flushing the conversation log at 13:39:21.**

Here's the evidence chain:

1. **The markdown is newer than the data.** The history file was generated at 13:41:30 and covers the native session file completely. The native JSONL (`f24aa68d….jsonl` in this workspace's `chatSessions/`) hasn't been written since **13:39:21** — it's still 259,603 bytes right now at 13:45.

2. **What's on disk ends exactly where your markdown ends.** The file holds three requests. The last one is your "`/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` is available" message, answered by "Thanks for the Python path update…" — and its stored result is:
   ```
   "errorDetails": { "message": "Canceled" }
   ```
   So the last thing VS Code persisted was that turn ending in a **cancellation** at 13:39:21 (did you hit Stop around then, perhaps during the "transient browser navigation issue" it mentions?). Nothing after that turn exists on disk.

3. **The session is alive, but only half of it is being persisted.** The sibling `chatEditingSessions/…/state.json` for the *same* session was written 20 seconds ago (13:44:45) — VS Code is running and actively flushing editing state. It's specifically the chat JSONL writer that's gone quiet. And no other chat session file anywhere under `Code/User/` has been touched, so the continuation isn't landing in some other store — it's living purely in VS Code's memory.

Notably, earlier in this same session VS Code was flushing generously — per-turn token counts, mid-turn response batches. The abrupt silence right at the `Canceled` write, while the editing-state file keeps updating, suggests the cancellation wedged this session's log writer (a VS Code-side behavior/bug, consistent with what we learned during reconstruct work: VS Code treats its in-memory chat store as authoritative and writes disk lazily).

**What to try:** finish the current turn and see if a completed (non-canceled) turn triggers a flush; if not, close the chat editor or quit VS Code — quit forces the store to flush. Then re-run `specstory sync` (or just leave `specstory run copilotide` going — with the file-signature gate and safety poll it'll pick the change up automatically once the bytes hit disk). If even a full VS Code quit doesn't extend the JSONL past line 83, the rest of that conversation was never persisted anywhere and is unrecoverable — which would be worth noting in the provider docs as an upstream limitation: *SpecStory can only be as current as VS Code's last flush, and cancellations appear to be able to stall that flush indefinitely.*

The watch banner is now exactly what you asked for:

```

```

## What changed

**Variant registration is now usage-gated** (`pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`). Stock VS Code (`copilotide`) is always registered like every other provider. The three alternative distributions — Insiders, VSCodium, VSCodium Insiders — register only when a new `copilotide.HasAnyChatSessions` check (in `path_utils.go`) finds at least one workspace with a `chatSessions` directory in that distribution's storage.

It took two steps to get here: the first gate ("workspace storage exists") killed the two VSCodium entries but kept Insiders, because you genuinely have VS Code Insiders installed with populated workspace storage. Checking deeper showed your 3 Insiders workspaces have zero Copilot chats — you've opened the app but never chatted there. So the gate became "has ever had a Copilot chat," which is the actually-meaningful signal: opening an app creates storage; only using Copilot creates `chatSessions`. Someone who really uses Copilot in Insiders still gets it auto-registered everywhere.

The cost is one `ReadDir` plus a stat per workspace per variant at registry init — a few microseconds — and one documented trade-off (noted in the registry comment): a variant's *very first* Copilot chat must happen without SpecStory, since until a chat exists the variant doesn't resolve at all — including explicit `specstory run copilotide-insiders`. After one chat, everything works, including watch pickup of that first session via `sync`.

Lint clean, full suite zero failures, verified against the real binary in your test project.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 18:03:47Z)**_

Overall verdict: the **structure** is working well — turns, timestamps, thinking blocks, tool `<details>` blocks with correct names/types, input formatting with fenced multiline values, and the 2000-rune result cap are all doing their jobs, and the sequence-based tool matching attributed every tool correctly. But reading it end to end, there are six real quality issues, in descending order of impact:

**1. Raw VS Code "node tree" JSON as results — the big one.** `create_file`, `list_dir`, `file_search`, `read_file`, `get_errors`, `fetch_webpage`, `create_new_jupyter_notebook` all render results like:

```
{"node":{"children":[{"lineBreakBefore":false,"priority":9007199254740991,"text":"The following files were successfully edited:","type":2},...
```

That's VS Code's internal renderer tree; the human-readable content is buried in the `text` leaves. Our `valueToString` JSON-marshals any object result verbatim. A generic extractor that walks `node.children` recursively and joins the `text` fields (newline when `lineBreakBefore` is true) would turn that `list_dir` result into just `sample.txt` and the `read_file` result into the actual file lines — one fix that upgrades most tools at once. Notice the contrast: tools whose results are plain strings (`run_in_terminal`, `memory`, `kill_terminal`) already read great.

**2. Go map/slice syntax in inputs.** Line 603: `- task: map[args:[task demo ok] command:echo ...]` and line 256: `- filePaths: [/Users/...]` — that's `fmt.Sprintf("%v")` leaking Go formatting. Non-scalar input values should be JSON-marshaled (ideally pretty-printed in a fence).

**3. Progress fragments run together without separators.** Every multi-batch turn produces prose like "…with a clear success/failure report.I'll create a tiny notebook…" — `ExtractTextFromResponseArray` concatenates markdown fragments directly. Direct concatenation is *correct* around `inlineReference` chips (that's intra-sentence), but these are separate progress paragraphs from separate response batches. A join rule of "paragraph break between plain fragments, direct concatenation only adjacent to an inlineReference" would fix this without breaking the chip case. The same run-together also shows inside the Thought Process block (line 16).

**4. Thinking text duplicated into the response.** The first turn's `<think>` block content ("I'm going to create a tools.txt… I'll quickly check…") reappears verbatim in the final agent message (lines 116–118). The progress notes live both in `toolCallRounds.response` (→ our thinking) and as response-array fragments (→ our final text). We should probably suppress fragments from the final text when they're already emitted as thinking, or vice versa.

**5. A stray empty code fence.** Lines 809–811 have an orphaned ``` pair between two prose fragments — likely the residue of a `codeblockUri` placeholder in the raw values. Worth checking the raw data; if that's what it is, the phase-2 `codeblockUri` handling would absorb it.

**6. Missing `---` between consecutive user messages.** Lines 828–834: "proceed!" and "proceed" (two user turns whose responses were canceled/empty) render back-to-back with no separator, unlike every other boundary. Minor generator polish.

Also cosmetic but cheap: terminal-style results carry dozens of trailing blank lines from the raw data — trimming trailing whitespace-only lines inside the result fence would tighten things considerably.

If you want to attack these, I'd do #1 and #2 first (both live in `BuildToolInfoFromInvocation`/`FormatToolMarkdown` and are self-contained), then #3/#4 together since they're both in the response-array extraction. Want me to start on any of them?

	// Add header comment
	markdown.WriteString(GeneratedBySpecStory + "\n\n")

	// Create title from session info
	title := generateTitle(sessionData, useUTC)
	fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "# %s\n\n", title)

	// Add session metadata comment using the same timestamp format as the title
	var commentTimestamp string
	if len(sessionData.Exchanges) > 0 && sessionData.Exchanges[0].StartTime != "" {
		commentTimestamp = formatTimestamp(sessionData.Exchanges[0].StartTime, useUTC)
	} else {
		commentTimestamp = formatTimestamp(sessionData.CreatedAt, useUTC)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "<!-- %s Session %s (%s) -->\n\n",
		sessionData.Provider.Name,
		sessionData.SessionID,
		commentTimestamp)

	// Render each exchange, tracking role across exchanges for proper separators
	prevRole := ""
	for _, exchange := range sessionData.Exchanges {
		for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
			// A single agent turn is split across several JSONL records (thinking,
			// text, tool_use). A record can carry no renderable body — e.g. a
			// signature-only thinking block whose text is empty — and would
			// otherwise emit a bare role header. Skip those, and advance prevRole
			// only for records we actually render so the role-change separators
			// stay correct.
			if !hasRenderableContent(msg) {
				continue
			}
			markdown.WriteString(renderMessage(msg, prevRole, includeMessageIDs, useUTC))
			prevRole = msg.Role
		}
	}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 20:10:15Z)**_

All six issues are fixed, verified against your real session — plus one significant bonus fix the fresh debug data exposed. The regenerated file went from 852 to 1,589 lines because previously-dropped tools now render.

**#1 — Node-tree JSON results** (`valueToString` + new `renderNodeTreeText` in `agent_session.go`): result values shaped like VS Code's serialized renderer tree now have their `text` leaves extracted in document order (honoring `lineBreakBefore`). Your `list_dir` result is now literally `sample.txt`; `read_file` shows the file lines; `get_errors` shows "No errors found". Anything that isn't a node tree still falls back to JSON as before.

**Bonus (from your new raw data) — canceled turns dropped every tool.** Requests 2–6 have *empty* metadata (VS Code doesn't record `toolCallRounds` for canceled turns), and even request 1 has 43 invocations vs 29 recorded calls — the sequence matcher silently discarded all of those. New `BuildToolInfoFromInvocationOnly` renders unmatched invocations from the invocation's own `resultDetails` (input JSON + output embeds; binary embeds like screenshots elide to `[image/jpeg embed]`), led by its human message — e.g. `configure_notebook` now shows "Configuring notebook demo.ipynb" with input and result. This is where most of the 700 recovered lines came from.

**#2 — Go map/slice syntax**: new `inputValueString` marshals non-scalar inputs as JSON — compact inline when short, pretty-printed in a fence when long. `create_and_run_task`'s input is now a proper JSON object.

**#3 — Run-together fragments**: `ExtractTextFromResponseArray` now inserts a paragraph break between adjacent plain fragments (unless one already carries boundary newlines), while keeping direct concatenation around `inlineReference` chips so "A new file named `X` has been created" stays intact. Your turn-3 progress notes are now four clean paragraphs.

**#4 — Thinking duplication**: final text is computed first, and `ExtractThinkingFromMetadata` drops any round already present in it — with whitespace-insensitive containment, since VS Code fuses the same sentences differently in the two stores. Result for this session: zero thinking blocks, which is *correct* — Copilot's round responses are visible narration (now living once, in the body); its actual reasoning is the opaque `thinking` response items that carry no text.

**#5 — Empty fence artifact**: bare-fence fragments (VS Code's delimiters around `codeblockUri`/`textEditGroup` items we don't yet render) are dropped; a genuine fenced code example arrives as one multi-line fragment and is preserved — both cases covered by new table tests. Zero empty fence pairs remain.

**#6 — Missing `---` between user turns**: fixed in the shared generator (`pkg/session/markdown.go`) — the first rendered message of each exchange now always separates from the previous exchange. Role-transition separators are unchanged, so other providers' output is unaffected except in this same user-after-user case, where the fix is equally right. "proceed!" / "proceed" now have their divider.

Also folded in: trailing blank-line trimming on results (terminal outputs no longer carry 25 empty lines), and the known-but-unrendered kinds (`thinking`, `undoStop`, `mcpServersStarting`, `notebookEditGroup`) no longer spam the debug log.

Lint clean, full suite zero failures, four new test cases for the join/fence rules. Ready for the per-tool handlers pass whenever you are — the generic layer now gives it a much better floor to build on.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 20:30:36Z)**_

This round exposed something big in the raw data, plus a family of related rendering bugs. Here's the enumeration:

## 1. Duplicate tool blocks — VS Code re-serializes invocations as they progress

The same `toolCallId` appears 2–3× in the response array (request 12: 8 invocations but only 5 distinct calls; `call_dYBOsNeX…` appears **three times**). VS Code appends a new serialized copy of the invocation as its state updates (running → completed), and we render every occurrence. That's your `copilot_createNewWorkspace` ×3, `copilot_createDirectory` ×2, `copilot_viewImage` ×2, `copilot_getVSCodeAPI` ×2, and the identical `base64 -D` terminal blocks. **Fix: dedupe by `toolCallId`, keeping the last occurrence (it carries the final `resultDetails`).**

## 2. The IDs actually match — the plan doc's core assumption is wrong

This is the discovery: request 12's metadata IDs are `call_dYBOsNeX…__vscode-1785961215195` and the invocation's `toolCallId` is `call_dYBOsNeX…` — **the metadata ID is the invocation ID plus a `__vscode-<n>` suffix.** The TOOLS-PLAN doc concluded "VS Code IDs don't match OpenAI IDs" (hence sequence matching); that's only true for the older UUID-style invocations. We can match precisely by stripping the suffix, falling back to sequence for UUID-style ones. This matters because…

## 3. The same call can render twice via both paths

Sequence matching consumes metadata slots by position, so when duplicates inflate the invocation array, a call gets matched once (input+result from metadata) *and* its duplicate serialization later falls into the fallback path ("Running `base64…`" + input + result from `resultDetails`) — two near-identical blocks for one execution. ID-based matching plus cross-path dedupe from #1 eliminates this class entirely.

## 4. Empty tool blocks

`copilot_createNewWorkspace` renders as a bare `<summary>` with an empty body — its `invocationMessage` is literally `""` and it has no `resultDetails`. Mostly noise amplified by #1's triplication; after dedupe one name-only block is arguably honest. Could add a "(no details recorded)" line if you want.

## 5. Narration renders after the tools it introduces

Every turn is `[tool, tool, …, all narration]` — e.g. "I'll locate an existing image and then run `view_image`…" appears *below* the `view_image` calls it announces. The response array actually holds fragments and invocations in true interleaved order, so we could emit messages in array order and get faithful chronology. This is the biggest structural upgrade left, and it dovetails with #2 (both mean "trust the response array as the spine of the turn").

## 6. Cosmetic residue (low priority)

- `[image/png embed]` placeholder appended after terminal text inside one result fence — by design, reads fine.
- `tool\_demos` backslash-escapes inside VS Code's own invocation messages (their markdown escaping, shown literally inside code spans).
- Terminal line-wrap noise (`26-08-05]  base64…`) — that's in the source data, not ours.

Not issues: the repeated kernel-death notebook blocks in request 8 are (mostly) genuine distinct retries — 29 invocations with only 3 duplicate IDs — and the `session_store_sql` table result reads great.

My recommended order: **#1+#3 together** (dedupe by toolCallId across both paths — small, kills the most visible junk), then **#2** (ID-first matching with suffix strip, sequence fallback), then **#5** (interleaved ordering) as the capstone. Want me to start with the dedupe?

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 20:31:25Z)**_

That's VS Code's message markdown leaking through verbatim. The invocation messages we now render (fallback path) contain markdown links whose **label VS Code fills in at render time** — on disk they're literally `Viewed image [](file:///…/tiny.png)`, an empty-label link. VS Code's chat renderer derives the display text from the URI; plain markdown renderers just show the raw `[](file://…)`. Same family: `Read [](file:///…)`, `Ran [](vscode-notebook-cell:/…)`, and links with `vscode-browser:`/`command:` schemes that are dead outside the IDE.

The fix is to sanitize those messages: replace each link with its label — or, when the label is empty, the link target's file name — in backticks. Implementing:

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 20:32:33Z)**_

Fixed. The line from your screenshot now renders as:

```
Viewed image `tiny.png`
```

**Why it happened:** VS Code stores invocation messages with markdown links whose display label is *empty on disk* — `Viewed image [](file:///…/tiny.png)` — because its own chat renderer derives the label from the URI at display time. Our fallback path (added for the canceled-turn tools) emitted those messages verbatim, so plain markdown viewers showed the raw `[](file://…)`. The same pattern covered `Read [](file:///…)`, `Ran [](vscode-notebook-cell:/…)`, and labeled links with IDE-only schemes (`vscode-browser:`, `command:`) that are dead outside VS Code.

**The fix:** a `sanitizeInvocationMessage` pass over those messages replaces every markdown link with its label in backticks — and when the label is empty, with the link target's decoded file name (fragment and query stripped, so notebook-cell links show `demo.ipynb`, not the cell hash). Results across the regenerated file: `Created `tools.txt``, `Read `tasks.json``, `Opened `Browser``, and zero remaining raw `file:///` or `vscode-*` links anywhere. Five new table tests cover the link shapes; lint clean, full suite passing.

One honest note: `Viewed image `tiny.png`` still appears **twice** — that's issue #1 from the enumeration (VS Code re-serializing invocations as they progress), which is still queued along with #2 (ID-suffix matching) and #5 (interleaved ordering) whenever you want to tackle them.

All verified against the real session. Here's the list with current state:

**1. Duplicate tool blocks — DONE.** `collectResponseBodyItems` dedupes by `toolCallId`: one block per call, kept at the first occurrence's position (chronology) with the last serialization's data (final `resultDetails`). Verified: `createNewWorkspace` 3→1, `viewImage` 2→1, `createDirectory` 2→1, `getVSCodeAPI` 2→1; file shrank 2,057→1,859 lines. Guarded by a new table test.

**2. ID matching — DONE.** Metadata calls now pair by suffix-stripped ID (`call_XXX__vscode-<n>` ↔ `call_XXX`) first; invocations that can't ID-match (old UUID style) claim the next unclaimed call in order — the previous sequence behavior as fallback; no metadata at all → `resultDetails` rendering. The new test proves ID matching wins over position even when the response array is out of metadata order.

**3. Same call rendered via both paths — DONE**, as predicted it fell out of #1+#2: the `base64 -D` execution that appeared three times (once matched, twice via fallback) is now a single block.

**4. Empty tool blocks — RESOLVED-BY-DEDUPE.** The bare `createNewWorkspace` block still has no details (VS Code recorded none — empty message, no resultDetails), but there's now exactly one of it, which is an honest record. No filler text added.

**5. Narration ordering — DONE.** The response array is now the spine of the turn: text runs and tool blocks emit interleaved in recorded order. Verified: "I'll locate an existing image… and then run `view_image`" now appears *before* the terminal/tool blocks it announces, not after everything. The old tools-then-text assembly is gone; metadata text sources remain only as fallback for turns whose response array has no text.

**6. Cosmetic residue — NO ACTION**, as agreed (image-embed placeholders by design, VS Code's own escaping, terminal wrap noise from source data).

Also from earlier, already done: the empty-label link sanitization (`Viewed image `tiny.png``).

Implementation shape, for the record: one rework as predicted — `ParseResponsesForTools` is replaced by `ConvertResponsesToMessages` (interleave + ID-resolve + dedupe), sharing `collectResponseBodyItems`/`joinTextItems` with `ExtractTextFromResponseArray` so the fragment rules live in one place. Hidden tools still claim their metadata call without emitting or splitting a text run. One subtlety the tests caught: an inline reference that renders no text still marks its neighbors adjacent, so sentence fragments around a broken chip don't get a spurious paragraph break. _**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-05 20:53:57Z)**_

All resolved. The one remaining `[](file://…` in the file isn't ours — it's inside a `grep_search` **result fence**: the agent grepped the project mid-session and its output quotes the *old* markdown file as it existed then (with the pre-fix link). That's faithful tool output, not rendering.

What your screenshot actually caught was real, though — a **mispairing bug in the new ID resolver**, now fixed:

**The bug:** request 0's response array starts with a hidden `manage_todo_list` carrying a UUID id and **no metadata call at all** (VS Code-internal todo updates aren't recorded in `toolCallRounds`). My resolver ran in a single in-order pass, so that UUID invocation fell through to "claim next unclaimed" and stole `list_dir`'s metadata call. Everything cascaded: `copilot_listDirectory` found its exact ID taken and grabbed `create_file`'s slot (rendering a bogus "create_file" block), and the real `copilot_createFile` was left with nothing, rendering as the fallback block you saw.

**The fix:** resolution is now two passes over the whole turn — exact ID matches claim their calls first, then UUID-style leftovers claim remaining calls in order (the old sequence behavior, restricted to leftovers). The code comment explains exactly why the split matters. Turn 1 now renders correctly: `list_dir` (full input/result from metadata), `create_file` (matched), and `manage_todo_list` → "Created 2 todos" via invocation fallback; the hidden todo update claims nothing and renders nothing.

Guarded by a new regression test built from this exact real-data shape (hidden UUID invocation must not steal an ID-matched call; the metadata-less tool must render from its own invocation data). Lint clean, full suite zero failures, verified on the re-synced file.

One meta-note for your test methodology: since the session greps its own history, older rendering artifacts can get frozen into tool results — so a stray `[](file://` inside a result fence in future syncs is the *session quoting itself*, not a regression. Same for your screenshot if the preview was showing the pre-sync file.

347	func BuildToolInfoFromInvocationOnly(invocation VSCodeToolInvocationResponse) *schema.ToolInfo {

Everything verified on the real session. Summary of this batch:

## Your question first: which tools deserve custom handlers?

The data gave a better answer than a handler list: **VS Code already writes a per-call description for nearly every tool** (`Searched for files matching '**/*.txt', 3 matches`, `` `demo-echo-task` task finished ``, `Sent `demo input` to terminal`…) and we were dropping it on matched tools. That's now attached generically — every tool block leads with its description — which delivers most of what Cursor's 10 handlers exist for. What remains genuinely custom-handler-worthy is narrow: `manage_todo_list` (input JSON could render as a checklist), `run_in_terminal` (bash-fenced command), and search results as tables. Nothing else in this 66-tool session showed structure the generic layer misses.

## What landed

**Real model (A):** `ExtractResolvedModel` reads `autoModeResolution` items (last one wins — turns can re-resolve across rounds). 55 agent messages in your session now say `Agent (gpt-5.3-codex)`; the 101 still showing `copilot/auto` are turns whose flushed data carries no resolution record — honest, not a gap.

**Warnings (B):** rendered as `> ⚠️ …` blockquotes. Your "proceed!" dead turn now explains itself: *"Chat took too long to get ready. Please ensure you are signed in to GitHub…"*.

**Chrome silenced (C):** `progressMessage`, `command`, `autoModeResolution` join the known-skip list — no debug noise, nothing rendered.

**`textEditGroup` / `notebookEditGroup`:** render as collapsible `Edit: **sample.txt**` blocks — each chunk under an `@@ lines N-M @@` header with fenced replacement text, deletions noted, content uncapped (it's what the agent chose to write; the comment notes there's no before-text in the data, so it's applied content, not a true diff). Notebook groups share the builder with a `Notebook edit:` label; content-less groups still record *that* the file was edited. This closes the biggest content omission — inline edits in turns with unrecorded tools were previously invisible.

**`confirmation`:** renders as `> ❓ title — message` (none in this session, but implemented and sanitized like the rest).

**`codeblockUri`:** deliberately stays silent with a comment explaining why — it only labels the file for an adjacent `textEditGroup`, which now carries the content.

Two of the four "unused phase-2 placeholder types" from the dead-code list (`VSCodeTextEditGroupResponse`, `VSCodeConfirmationResponse`) are now in real use. Lint clean, full suite zero failures.

At this point the copilotide rendering pipeline has no known gaps against this session's data — remaining niceties are the narrow per-tool handlers above and `runSubagent`/GitHub tools we haven't seen data for yet.

461	// ExtractFinalAgentMessage gets the final text response from metadata
462	func ExtractFinalAgentMessage(metadata VSCodeResultMetadata) string {
463		// VS Code stores final messages in metadata.messages
464		for _, msg := range metadata.Messages {
465			if msg.Role == "assistant" {
466				return msg.Content
467			}
468		}
469		return ""
470	}
471	
472	// toolResultCap bounds how much tool output is pre-rendered into FormattedMarkdown.
473	// Inputs are not capped — they carry what the agent chose to do (e.g. the full content
474	// of a written file) — but results (file reads, command output) can be arbitrarily
475	// large and matter less once the agent has already responded to them.
476	const toolResultCap = 2000
477	
478	// FormatToolMarkdown pre-renders a tool call's Input/Output as markdown for
479	// ToolInfo.FormattedMarkdown. The markdown generator would fall back to an equivalent
480	// generic rendering on its own, but cross-agent resume would not: the flattener
481	// (spi.FlattenSessionData) carries only Summary/FormattedMarkdown, so without this the
482	// tool's payload (e.g. a written file's content) would collapse to a bare tool name in
483	// the resumed session. Returns empty when the tool has nothing to render.
484	//
485	// Tools with a dedicated formatter render through it; everything else gets the
486	// generic key/value Input plus fenced Result.
487	func FormatToolMarkdown(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
488		if custom := formatCustomToolMarkdown(tool); custom != "" {
489			return custom
490		}
491	
492		var b strings.Builder
493	
494		// Input as key-value pairs, multiline values fenced (mirrors the generic renderer).
495		keys := make([]string, 0, len(tool.Input))
496		for key := range tool.Input {
497			// Skip internal fields like _cwd (matches the markdown generator).
498			if !strings.HasPrefix(key, "_") {
499				keys = append(keys, key)
500			}
501		}
502		sort.Strings(keys)
503		if len(keys) > 0 {
504			b.WriteString("\n**Input:**\n\n")
505			for _, key := range keys {
506				valueStr := inputValueString(tool.Input[key])
507				if strings.Contains(valueStr, "\n") {
508					fence := codeFence(valueStr)
509					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s:\n\n%s\n%s\n%s\n\n", key, fence, valueStr, fence)
510				} else {
511					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s: `%s`\n", key, valueStr)
512				}
513			}
514		}

## What was built

**Handler dispatch** — `FormatToolMarkdown` now checks `formatCustomToolMarkdown` first; a handler returning `""` (missing/unexpected input shape) falls back to the generic rendering, so format drift degrades gracefully instead of hiding data. The generic result-fence logic moved into a shared `resultSection` helper both paths use.

**`run_in_terminal`** — explanation as prose, the command in a `bash` fence (uncapped — it's what the agent chose to run), then the capped result. The noise keys (`mode`, `goal`, `timeout`) no longer clutter the block.

**`manage_todo_list`** — renders the `todoList` as a markdown checklist (`- [x]` completed, `- [ ] … _(in progress)_`, `- [ ]` not started), built against VS Code's documented schema. Honest caveat: your session's todo invocations are all VS Code-internal (no arguments recorded anywhere in the JSON), so this session still shows the message-only blocks — the checklist engages in sessions where metadata records the arguments. Read operations fall back to generic. Both handlers have tests including their fallback paths; one existing test moved to `get_terminal_output` since its `run_in_terminal` fixture now (correctly) renders through the handler.

Yes, they should go, and they're gone. Final ledger of the review's dead-code list: `IsHiddenTool` ✂️, `GetSessionIDFromPath` ✂️, `BuildToolCallMap` ✂️ (removed just now — its "backward compatibility" claim was always wrong), and of the four placeholder types: `VSCodeTextEditGroupResponse` and `VSCodeConfirmationResponse` earned their keep in the phase-2 work, `VSCodeCodeblockUriResponse` and `VSCodeInlineReferenceResponse` removed just now (both kinds are parsed via purpose-built anonymous structs). _**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-06 21:32:48Z)**_

Both problems fixed. Here's what was wrong and what changed:

## `watch` — the real bug

You ran `specstory watch` in a brand-new folder *before* VS Code ever opened it. `WatchAgent` errored with "no workspace found," and the multi-provider watch treats a watcher error as terminal for that provider — so copilotide was dead before you typed your first prompt. (The earlier MIP #2 fix handled a missing `chatSessions` directory, but not a missing workspace *entry*; `run` survived only because `ExecAgentAndWatch` retries.)

**Fix:** `WatchAgent` now waits for the workspace entry instead of erroring — a context-aware 2-second poll (polling rather than fsnotify is deliberate and commented: a new entry is an opaque hash dir whose match is only knowable by re-running the lookup, so an event would trigger the same scan the poll does). Applied **symmetrically to cursoride**, which had the identical failure mode — in your copilot-2 test the Cursor IDE watcher had also silently died.

**Verified live:** I reproduced your exact sequence in a scratch dir — `watch` first, workspace created 3s later, first chat 4s after that — and got `✨ copilotide · aaaa1…67777 · 1 prompt · 1 agent activity` plus the generated history file. (The simulated workspace entry was removed from VS Code's storage afterward.)

## `run` — terminal feedback

Three changes to what you see in that idle terminal:

1. **The waiting message now resolves.** "Waiting for VS Code to open this project..." is followed by "**VS Code opened the project — auto-saving Copilot chats.**" when the workspace appears (the wait loop in `ExecAgentAndWatch` is now purely for feedback, since `WatchAgent` handles the actual waiting).
2. **Per-save lines.** Runs of IDE-backed providers (`cursoride`, any `copilotide*`) now print a watch-style line on every markdown save — `  17:32:13  ✨  hello-world-in-c` (✨ created / ♻️ updated), suppressed by `--silent`. The gate is explicitly ID-based with a comment explaining why: CLI agents own the terminal with their own TUI and must never have output interleaved; IDE runs leave it idle.
3. Wired through the existing `OnSaved` hook on the autosave callback — the same mechanism `watch` uses, no new plumbing.

Lint clean, full suite zero failures, race detector clean on both providers. Worth a quick interactive retest on your side — the `copilot-2`-style flow (watch first, open VS Code second, chat third) is the one that was completely broken.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-08-06 21:56:58Z)**_

Found it — three stacked problems, all fixed:

## What actually happened

**1. VS Code rejected our session format and clobbered it.** Comparing our reconstruction against files VS Code 1.131 writes itself: VS Code's `kind:0` snapshot is an *empty shell* (exactly 9 keys, `requests: []`) with content arriving as incremental `kind:1`/`kind:2` lines — and its request blocks have **no `kind` discriminator on message parts and no `result`/`followups`/`isCanceled`**. We wrote an all-inline snapshot with extra keys and a `"kind":"text"` part. VS Code's loader choked, adopted each session as *empty*, and **rewrote our files** — that's why every reconstructed file is an identical 1,353 bytes titled "New Chat" with zero requests (the "Resumed session · 0" row in your picker is our indexer honestly reading the clobbered file). Empty sessions are hidden from the panel → nothing shows.

**Fix:** `ReconstructSession` now mirrors VS Code's write pattern exactly — empty shell, then `customTitle`/`isImported`/`requests`/`lastMessageDate` as incremental lines — and the request block matches a real one field-for-field. Round-trip tests updated to *enforce* the shell shape (inlining those fields is now a test failure).

**2. Your folder has TWO workspace entries** differing only in path case: `file:///Users/sean/source/…` (holds your organic "Chatbot name inquiry" session) and `file:///Users/sean/Source/…` (what `code .` actually opens, since VS Code resolves the on-disk case). That's why even the organic session is invisible in the current window — it lives in the entry your window isn't using. Our mtime-based pick sprayed resume writes across *both*.

**Fix:** workspace matching now prefers entries whose stored path equals the canonical path byte-for-byte before falling back to newest-mtime — reads and writes deterministically target the entry VS Code will actually open.

**3. We were the ones minting the case-variant entries.** `specstory run` passes your typed path (`~/source/…`) verbatim to the `code`/`cursor` launcher, and the IDE derives workspace identity from that string. Both IDE providers now canonicalize the path before launching, so SpecStory-launched windows converge on the same entry as every other open method.

## To retest

Quit VS Code fully, then resume the Claude session into copilotide again from `~/Source/SpecStory/compositions/copilot-4` — the session should appear (titled "Resumed: …") in the Chat panel of the window our resume opens. Optional cleanup of the five clobbered "New Chat" husks: delete the 1,353-byte `.jsonl` files from both workspace entries' `chatSessions/` dirs while VS Code is closed — they're empty shells, nothing of value in them.

One honest remaining limitation: your organic session stays stranded in the lowercase entry (its markdown/index are already safe in SpecStory). The complete fix is merging reads across all matching workspace entries, Cursor-provider style — worth doing, but it's a separate structural change I didn't want to fold into tonight's correctness fix.

VS Code chat-session revival requirements (verified against VS Code 1.131 source, 2026-08-07), for the copilotide provider's `ReconstructSession`:

- The loader is `ChatModel._deserialize` in `/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js` (minified; search for `Loaded malformed session data` / `Failed to parse chat data`). ONE throw while deserializing ANY request drops ALL requests → session loads empty → VS Code auto-deletes it on close.
- Message parts MUST carry `"kind":"text"` — the part reviver ends with `throw new Error("Unknown chat request part: "+kind)`. Older VS Code builds serialized parts without `kind`; do not trust old session files as format references.
- Requests need completed-state fields to revive as finished turns: `agent` (must contain a `metadata` key), `modeInfo`, `modelState {value:1, completedAt}`, `result`, `responseTimestamp`.
- Sessions are discovered ONLY via the `chat.ChatSessionStore.index` row in the workspace's state.vscdb — there is NO chatSessions directory scan. A running VS Code holds that index in memory and flushes over external writes; closing all windows does NOT quit the macOS process (verify with `ps aux | grep "Visual Studio Code"`). Index writes only stick when the process is fully dead.
- Failures log `Failed to parse chat data` in VS Code's window log — check there before guessing at formats.
- inputState must never be templated into reconstructed sessions: it embeds the user's GitHub account label.

Open decision (Sean hasn't picked): guard for resume-while-VS-Code-running — detect-and-warn vs block vs wait-for-quit prompt.

Done and confirmed. The final accounting of what made resume-into-Copilot work, since it took four rounds to peel:

1. **Request revival requirements** (the core fix): message parts must carry `"kind": "text"` — VS Code's part reviver *throws* on an unknown/missing kind, and one throw drops every request in the session. On top of that, requests need the completed-state fields (`agent` with a `metadata` key, `modeInfo`, `modelState {value:1}`, `result`, `responseTimestamp`) to revive as finished turns. All verified against the actual deserializer in the VS Code bundle rather than inferred from sample files — the lesson of this bug is that old session files lie about the current format.
2. **Index-only discovery**: sessions surface exclusively via the `chat.ChatSessionStore.index` row; there's no directory scan. Our entry now mirrors the real shape including `permissionLevel`.
3. **Case-split workspaces**: canonical-path preference in matching plus canonicalized launcher paths, so writes land in the entry VS Code actually opens.
4. **Process-quit gotcha**: a "quit" VS Code whose process is still alive silently erases external index writes — that poisoned at least two earlier test rounds.

All of this is captured in code comments, the round-trip tests now enforce the revival-critical fields, and I've saved a memory with the requirements and the debugging entry points (the `Failed to parse chat data` window-log string would have saved us three rounds).
